teile.einleitung: A language border separates areas where different languages are spoken. In Switzerland such borders between German, French and Italian run right across cantons and valleys. Sometimes they lie only a few kilometres apart.
wichtigste: Many places on the German French language border have two names, for example Biel and Bienne.
In the Valais the Pfynwald counts as a natural language border.
Sierre is French speaking, and a few kilometres to the east people speak German.
The language border does not cross Vaud.
In Bosco/Gurin in Ticino people speak a German Walser dialect.

abschnitte.text: Many places on the **German French language border** have a German and a French name. Examples are **Biel and Bienne**, **Freiburg and Fribourg** or **Siders and Sierre**. The names show that both language groups know the place. The border crosses the cantons of **Bern**, **Fribourg** and the **Valais**. **Vaud**, by contrast, is entirely French speaking.

abschnitte.titel: The language border in the Valais
abschnitte.text: In the Valais the language border runs near **Sierre**. Sierre is French speaking, and a few kilometres further east people speak German. The **Pfynwald** near Leuk, in French Bois de Finges, counts as the natural border. It is one of the largest **pine forests** of the Alps. East of it people speak German, west of it French.

The holiday resort of **Gstaad** belongs to the Bernese municipality of Saanen in the German speaking **Saanenland**. In nearby **Rougemont** in the canton of Vaud, people already speak French. There are also language borders between German and Italian. The **Nufenen Pass** leads from Ulrichen in the Goms into the **Bedretto valley** in Ticino. On the top of the pass you cross the border between German and Italian.

In the Middle Ages **Walser** moved from the Valais into other Alpine valleys. Among other places, they founded **Bosco/Gurin** in Ticino. There a German Walser dialect has been spoken for over 600 years, **Gurin German**. All around, people speak Italian. Such an area is called a **language island**.

gewusst: Bosco/Gurin is the only Ticino municipality in which German is traditionally spoken.
The differences between German speaking and western Switzerland are jokingly called the “Röstigraben”.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland does not lie on the sea, but it still has ports. The Swiss Rhine Ports near Basel connect the country with the North Sea via the Rhine. Here ships arrive with oil, grain and containers.
wichtigste: The Rhine ports include ports in Basel, Birsfelden and Muttenz.
The largest port is Kleinhüningen on the Kleinbasel side.
Many ships sail as far as Rotterdam in the Netherlands.
Especially large amounts of heating oil and fuel come into Switzerland by ship.
In 2009 about 10 per cent of foreign trade by volume went through the Rhine ports.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland does not border the **sea**. Via the **Rhine** it is still linked to the sea by ship. The ships sail from Basel downstream on the Rhine as far as **Rotterdam** in the Netherlands. Rotterdam lies at the mouth of the Rhine and is one of the largest ports in the world. That is why the Rhine ports are very important for supplying Switzerland.

The **Swiss Rhine Ports** include ports in Basel, Birsfelden and at the **Auhafen** in Muttenz. Birsfelden and Muttenz lie in the canton of Basel-Landschaft. The largest port is called **Kleinhüningen**. It lies on the right of the Rhine in the north of Basel and has two large harbour basins. Very close by, Switzerland, Germany and France meet at the **Dreiländereck** (tri-country corner).

A large part of Switzerland's **heating oil** and **fuel** comes to Basel by ship and is stored in large tanks. In tall **silos**, bulk goods are kept, above all **grain**. Many goods travel in **containers**, standardised steel boxes. Big **cranes** lift the containers from the ship onto land. Then they go on by lorry or train.

On the old **Bernoulli Silo** in the port of Basel there is a **viewing platform** right at the top. From there you can look far over the port and the Dreiländereck. You can see the ships, the cranes and the harbour basins from above. In 2009 about **10 per cent** of Switzerland's foreign trade by volume was handled through the Rhine ports.

gewusst: A single large Rhine ship can carry as much cargo as many lorries put together.
At the Dreiländereck in Basel, the borders of three countries meet in the middle of the Rhine.

teile.einleitung: The Romansh language, also called Grisons Romansh, is the smallest national language of Switzerland. Its history tells of Romans, mountain valleys and the long struggle to preserve a minority language.
wichtigste: In 1938 Romansh was recognised as the fourth national language with 91.6 per cent yes.
In 1982 Heinrich Schmid developed the written language Rumantsch Grischun.
Sursilvan is the largest idiom, Sutsilvan the smallest.
After the city fire of 1464, Chur increasingly became German speaking.
Tourism and transport contributed to the decline of the language.
From about 2011, many schools returned to the regional idioms.

abschnitte.text: Grisons Romansh arose from the **Latin** that the Romans brought into the Alps. According to a widespread classification, together with **Ladin** in the Dolomites and **Friulian** in north eastern Italy, it forms the group of the **Rhaeto-Romance languages**. Whether these three really form a unit of their own is **disputed** in research. In the Val Müstair people speak a dialect of their own, **Jauer**, though Vallader is traditionally what is written there.

In the past, Romansh was spoken in much larger parts of the Grisons. After a great **city fire in 1464**, many German speaking craftsmen moved to **Chur** to help rebuild it. As a result the city switched to German. In the 19th and 20th centuries, the **railway, tourism** and economic ties brought many German speakers into the region. As a result, German became the everyday language in many municipalities.

On **20 February 1938**, 91.6 per cent of voters voted in favour of recognising Romansh as the fourth **national language**. The clear result was also seen as a statement against claims by Italy at the time, which presented Romansh as an Italian dialect. Since 1996 it has also been a partial official language of the Confederation.

There are five idioms. **Sursilvan** along the Vorderrhein has the most speakers, **Sutsilvan** the fewest. In 1982 the Zurich Romance scholar **Heinrich Schmid**, on behalf of the **Lia Rumantscha**, created the shared written language **Rumantsch Grischun**. He chose in each case the form that occurs in most of the idioms. When some municipalities introduced Rumantsch Grischun for learning to read and write, there was **resistance**. From about 2011, many schools returned to their idioms.

The canton of the Grisons is trilingual: German, Romansh and Italian. The cantonal **Languages Act** of 2008 regulates which language a municipality uses officially. With at least **40 per cent** members of a national language, a municipality counts as monolingual, and from **20 per cent** as multilingual. This is meant to let Romansh municipalities keep their language in school and administration.

gewusst: Heinrich Schmid built Rumantsch Grischun on a simple principle: in each case he took the word form that most of the idioms share.
The city of Chur was Romansh speaking until the late Middle Ages.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland has many towns and cities, but no city of a million people. The largest city is Zurich, followed by Geneva and Basel. Many towns are small but have a long history.
wichtigste: Zurich is the largest city in Switzerland, Geneva the second largest.
Basel is the third largest city.
At the end of 2023, Lausanne was the fourth largest and Bern the fifth largest city.
Statistically, a municipality with more than 10,000 inhabitants counts as a city.
About 170 municipalities count as cities (as of 2020).
Chur is the largest city in the Grisons, Lugano the largest in Ticino.

abschnitte.text: The largest city in Switzerland is **Zurich**. In second place comes **Geneva** with over 200,000 inhabitants. The third largest city is **Basel** on the Rhine with about 176,000 inhabitants (as of 2023). At the end of 2023, **Lausanne** on Lake Geneva, with about 144,000 inhabitants, was the fourth largest city. In fifth place came the federal city **Bern** with about 137,000 inhabitants.

In **statistics**, a municipality with more than **10,000 inhabitants** counts as a city. Whether it calls itself a city is decided by the municipality. Some small places have been called a city since the Middle Ages, because they were granted town rights then. In 2020 about **170 municipalities** counted as cities. Most municipalities in Switzerland, however, are much smaller.

The largest city in **central Switzerland** is **Lucerne** on Lake Lucerne with over 80,000 inhabitants. It is the seventh largest city in Switzerland. In Ticino, **Lugano** with about 60,000 inhabitants is the largest city, but the cantonal capital is **Bellinzona**. In the Grisons, **Chur** is the largest city and also the capital. Chur has about 40,000 inhabitants (as of 2024) and is regarded as one of the oldest cities in Switzerland.

Compared with other countries, Swiss cities are rather small. Many people live in the **agglomerations**, that is, in municipalities around the large cities. That is why far more people live in the Zurich region than in the city itself. Population figures change every year, so they are always given with the year.

gewusst: Bern is officially not a capital, but the federal city of Switzerland.
Switzerland has not a single city with a million inhabitants.

teile.einleitung: The Limmat is the river that flows out of Lake Zurich right through the city of Zurich. After about 35 kilometres it joins the Aare at the Water Castle of Switzerland. On its banks lie famous churches, old guild houses and popular river baths.
wichtigste: The Limmat flows out of Lake Zurich.
It flows right through the city of Zurich, which in Roman times was called Turicum.
Other towns on the Limmat are Dietikon, Wettingen and Baden.
At the Water Castle of Switzerland, the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet.
Nearby lay the Roman legionary camp Vindonissa.
In the city of Zurich, the Sihl flows into the Limmat.
The Anabaptist Felix Manz was drowned in the Limmat in 1527.

abschnitte.text: The **Limmat** leaves **Lake Zurich** in the city of Zurich at Bellevue. At the Platzspitz behind the main station, the Sihl joins it. After that it flows north-west through the Limmat valley, past Dietikon, Wettingen and **Baden**. After about 35 kilometres it joins the Aare near Brugg in the canton of Aargau.

In the old town of **Zurich**, the **Grossmünster** and the Fraumünster stand on the left and right of the Limmat. The little Wasserkirche stands almost in the river itself. On the **Lindenhof** hill on the left bank there was already a Celtic settlement and later a Roman fort. The Romans called the place Turicum, from which the name Zurich comes.

At Brugg and Windisch, the Aare, Reuss and Limmat flow together very close to each other. This spot is called the **Water Castle of Switzerland**, because the water from a large part of the country comes together here. Right next to it lay the Roman legionary camp **Vindonissa**, the only one on the territory of present-day Switzerland. From there the Romans could watch over the important river routes.

During the Reformation, Reformed Zurich persecuted the **Anabaptists**, who wanted to baptise only adults. Their leader Felix Manz was drowned in the Limmat as a punishment in 1527. In 1847 the first railway in Switzerland ran along the Limmat, the **Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn** from Zurich to Baden. Its locomotive bore the name Limmat.

In summer, many people swim in the Limmat in Zurich, for example at the river bath **Oberer Letten**. At the annual Limmat swim, thousands let themselves drift through the city in the river. Mallards, swans, coots and fish such as the grayling live on the Limmat. Several hydropower plants along the river produce electricity.

begriffe.erklaerung: The place near Brugg where the Aare, Reuss and Limmat flow together.
A large fortified camp where Roman soldiers lived.
A Christian group in the time of the Reformation that rejected infant baptism.
A marked-off bathing place directly in a river.

gewusst: The Limmat is really the continuation of the Linth, which flows into Lake Walen and Lake Zurich.
The first railway in Switzerland was called the Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn, because servants are said to have used it to fetch fresh pastries from Baden to Zurich.
Although the Limmat is only about 35 kilometres long, it carries a lot of water, because it drains the whole of Lake Zurich.

teile.einleitung: The Seeland lies in the west of Switzerland between Lake Biel, Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Murten. In the past it was a wet plain that was often flooded. Today, thanks to large building works, it is an important vegetable growing area.
wichtigste: Lake Biel, Lake Neuchâtel and Lake Murten form the Three Lakes Region.
“Moos” in field names means marsh or moor.
Before the river corrections, the Seeland was often flooded.
Johann Rudolf Schneider of Nidau is regarded as the initiator of the Jura Water Correction.
The painter Albert Anker was born in Ins.
Since Lake Biel was lowered, St Peter's Island has no longer been a true island.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Biel**, **Lake Neuchâtel** and **Lake Murten** are linked to one another by canals. Together they form the **Three Lakes Region**. Between them lies a flat plain, the **Grosses Moos**. The word “Moos” stands in many Swiss field names for a **marsh** or **moorland**. From the plain rises the wooded **Jolimont** like an island, about 600 m high.

In the past the Aare and other rivers deposited a lot of gravel and hindered the outflow of the lakes. In floods, rivers and lakes burst their banks, and the plain was often under water. The Nidau doctor and politician **Johann Rudolf Schneider** fought for decades to drain the Seeland. In the 19th century the **First Jura Water Correction** began. In it the Aare was diverted into Lake Biel, and the lake levels sank by about two metres.

After the drainage, the Grosses Moos became a large **vegetable growing area**. The soils, however, often consist of **peat**. Dry peat breaks down in the air and sinks. That is why the ground in the Grosses Moos has sunk in places by over a metre. Later a second Jura Water Correction followed, to protect the area further.

When Lake Biel was lowered, a strip of land towards Erlach emerged, the **Heidenweg**. Since then **St Peter's Island** has no longer been a true island. The little town of **Aarberg** is known for its covered wooden bridge from the 16th century, which is still used by traffic today. In the village of **Ins** the painter **Albert Anker** was born in 1831, and many of his pictures show village life. On Lake Neuchâtel lies the bird reserve **Fanel**, where many water birds rest and breed.

gewusst: Today you can reach St Peter's Island on foot over the Heidenweg.
A large part of the vegetables in Swiss shops grows in the Seeland.

teile.einleitung: Nagelfluh is a rock that occurs in many places in Switzerland. It looks like a natural concrete full of round stones and tells of old rivers at the edge of the Alps.
wichtigste: Nagelfluh is a conglomerate of rounded pebbles.
The pebbles are firmly cemented together by a mostly limy binding material.
The name comes from the way the stones stick out of the wall like nail heads.
Nagelfluh formed in large debris fans of rivers at the edge of the Alps.
The Rigi, the Speer and the Napf hills consist largely of Nagelfluh.
In 1806 layers of Nagelfluh slid off the Rossberg and buried Goldau.

abschnitte.text: Nagelfluh consists of many **rounded pebbles**, that is, stones from rivers. A mostly limy **binding material** holds them together like cement. Experts call such a rock a **conglomerate**. When the rock weathers, the pebbles stick out of the wall like the heads of nails. “Fluh” is the Swiss German word for a steep rock face.

There are also rocks made of angular fragments, which are called **breccia**. The difference tells you a lot. Rounded pebbles were carried a long way in a river and worn smooth in the process. Angular fragments in a breccia, by contrast, were hardly moved. In this way you can read from a stone how it was formed.

As the Alps were being formed, rivers brought huge amounts of debris out of the mountains. At the edge of the Alps they piled up large **debris fans**. In time the pebbles hardened into Nagelfluh. These rocks belong to the **molasse**, which shapes the Central Plateau and the edge of the Alps. Later some layers were tilted.

The **Rigi** in Central Switzerland consists largely of tilted layers of Nagelfluh. Only in the south do limestone cliffs such as the Vitznauerstock rise up. The **Speer** north of Lake Walen is about 1,950 metres high and is regarded as the highest Nagelfluh mountain in Europe. The **Napf hills** between the Emmental and the Entlebuch are also an old debris fan. In its streams you find fine flakes of gold, so called placer gold.

In **1806**, tilted layers of Nagelfluh came loose on the Rossberg. They slid off soft layers of marl, as on a slide. The masses of rock buried the village of **Goldau** in the canton of Schwyz. About 450 people lost their lives. It was one of the worst rockslides in Switzerland.

gewusst: In the Goldau animal park today, animals live among the large boulders of the 1806 rockslide.
The gold in the Napf area comes from the pebbles of the Nagelfluh, which once came from the Alps.

teile.einleitung: Swiss watches are known all over the world. The watchmaking industry began in Geneva and spread into the Jura. After a serious crisis in the 1970s, it found success again.
wichtigste: Huguenots brought the craft of watchmaking to Geneva in the 16th century.
In the Jura, farming families made watch parts in winter.
La Chaux-de-Fonds and Le Locle have been UNESCO World Heritage sites since 2009.
In the 1970s, cheap quartz watches triggered a major crisis.
From 1983, the Swatch helped to save the watchmaking industry.
The Swatch Group has its headquarters in Biel.
Since 2017, at least 60 per cent of the costs must arise in Switzerland for a watch to be “Swiss made”.

abschnitte.text: In the **16th century**, many **Huguenots** fled from France to **Geneva**. Huguenots were Protestants who were persecuted in their homeland because of their faith. Among them were skilled craftsmen who brought the craft of **watchmaking** with them. In this way Geneva became an important watchmaking city.

From Geneva the craft spread into the **Jura**. There the winters are long and cold, and there was **little work** in the fields at that time. So many farming families made **watch parts** at home. Later, whole watchmaking towns grew up. **La Chaux-de-Fonds** and **Le Locle** have been **UNESCO World Heritage** sites since **2009** as “watchmaking towns”. In the high valley of the **Vallée de Joux**, especially complicated watches are still made today.

In the **1970s**, cheap **quartz watches** from **Asia** and the **USA** came onto the market. They were very accurate and cost little. Many Swiss firms carried on building mechanical watches and lost customers. Numerous businesses had to close, and many people lost their jobs.

From **1983**, the **Swatch** came onto the market. It was a cheap, colourful plastic watch with few parts. It became a great success and helped to save the watchmaking industry. The **Swatch Group** has its headquarters in **Biel**, a bilingual town at the foot of the southern Jura.

Not every watch may call itself **“Swiss made”**. Since **2017**, the rule is that at least **60 per cent** of the production costs must arise in **Switzerland**. This is meant to make the label stand for quality from Switzerland. Watches are among the country's most important exports.

gewusst: The name Swatch is often explained as a short form of “Second Watch”, that is, a second watch.
After a fire, La Chaux-de-Fonds was rebuilt with chessboard-like streets, to suit the watchmaking workshops.

teile.einleitung: Lower Valais is the lower, western part of the canton of Valais along the Rhône. French is mainly spoken there. For a long time the area was ruled by Upper Valais.
wichtigste: Lower Valais lies in the lower part of the Rhône valley.
Until 1798 it was a subject territory of the Upper Valais districts.
The Great St Bernard links Lower Valais with the Aosta Valley.
At Martigny, the Rhône turns sharply north in a distinctive bend.
In Lower Valais, French is mostly spoken.

abschnitte.text: Until **1798**, Lower Valais was a **subject territory**. It was governed by the **Zenden** of Upper Valais. The Zenden were the old districts in the upper part of Valais. The people of Lower Valais therefore had fewer rights. This changed with the French invasion and the Helvetic Republic in 1798.

The **Rhône** first flows west through Valais. At **Martigny** it makes a sharp turn and then flows **north** towards Lake Geneva. This turn is called the **Rhône bend**. In the broad valley many fruits grow, for example apricots, and wine is grown on the slopes.

From Lower Valais, the **Great St Bernard** leads over the Alps into the Italian **Aosta Valley**. The pass has been used for a very long time. On the summit of the pass stands a **hospice** where monks have been taking in travellers for centuries. Today there is also a road tunnel.

gewusst: The famous St Bernard dogs are named after the hospice on the Great St Bernard.

teile.einleitung: Lake Oeschinen is a mountain lake above Kandersteg in the Bernese Oberland. Its water glows turquoise, and behind it rise steep rock walls and glaciers.
wichtigste: Lake Oeschinen lies above Kandersteg in the Bernese Oberland.
It lies at about 1,580 metres above sea level.
It is about 1.1 square kilometres in size.
Rockslides blocked the valley, and the lake was dammed up behind them.
Behind the lake rises the Blüemlisalp.
Since 2007 it has belonged to the World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch.

abschnitte.text: Lake Oeschinen lies in a side valley above **Kandersteg** in the canton of Bern. Its water level is at about **1,578 metres** above sea level. At about **1.1 square kilometres** it is quite large for a mountain lake. Steep rock walls rise all around. The clear water shimmers turquoise.

A long time ago several **rockslides** came down here. The masses of rock blocked the valley like a dam. Behind them the water was dammed up into a **lake**. A large part of the water drains away underground through the rubble.

Behind the lake rises the mountain massif of the **Blüemlisalp** with glaciers. Several peaks are over **3,000 metres** high. Since **2007** Lake Oeschinen has belonged to the extended **UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch**. The landscape is thus under special protection.

Since **2008** a **gondola lift** has run up from Kandersteg. From the top station it is another 25 minutes or so on foot to the lake. In summer you can walk, row or picnic on the shore. In cold winters the lake freezes over. If the ice is thick enough and there is little snow on it, you can **ice skate**.

gewusst: There are fish in Lake Oeschinen, which is why it is also popular with anglers.
Many people regard Lake Oeschinen as one of the most beautiful mountain lakes in the Alps.

teile.einleitung: Urban sprawl means that houses, roads and industrial areas spread out scattered into the countryside. In Switzerland a lot of meadowland is lost this way, above all on the Central Plateau. That is why spatial planning is often voted on.
wichtigste: Urban sprawl is the disorderly spreading of buildings into the countryside.
Above all, farmland is lost as a result.
Many detached houses encourage urban sprawl.
One remedy is the densification of existing settlements.
Buildings may normally stand only in the building zone.
In 2013 the people approved the revision of the Spatial Planning Act.
The Urban Sprawl Initiative was rejected in 2019.

abschnitte.text: With **urban sprawl**, houses, roads and industrial areas spread **scattered** into the open countryside. New settlements often arise on meadows and fields on the **Central Plateau**. So valuable **farmland** disappears, that is, land for agriculture. **Detached houses** use especially a lot of land, because a lot of area is built over per person.

In scattered settlements, shops, schools and workplaces are often far away. Buses and trains run rarely there. Many people therefore need a **car**. This leads to more traffic, more roads and more noise. Animals and plants also lose **habitat** when landscapes are cut up.

Each **municipality** decides where building is allowed. This area is called the **building zone**. Outside it, no homes or commercial buildings may normally be built. An important remedy is **densification**: instead of building over new meadows, existing districts are used better, for example with taller buildings.

In March **2012**, the people approved the **Second Homes Initiative**. Since then, the share of second homes in a municipality may be at most **20 per cent**. In March **2013**, the **revision of the Spatial Planning Act** was approved. Since then, building zones may only be large enough for the needs of about **15 years**. The **Urban Sprawl Initiative** wanted to freeze the area of building zones. On **10 February 2019**, a good three fifths of voters rejected it.

Researchers at the **WSL**, the Federal Research Institute for Forest, Snow and Landscape, measure urban sprawl with a single number. It is called **weighted urban proliferation**. It does not only count how much area is built over. How scattered the buildings are and how densely they are used also matter.

gewusst: The Second Homes Initiative was approved in 2012 with only 50.6 per cent Yes.
Since 2013, building zones in Switzerland that are too large have had to be reduced.

teile.einleitung: The village of Brienz/Brinzauls in the Albula Valley in the Grisons stands on a slope that is slowly moving down into the valley. Because of this slide, the population has had to leave the village several times.
wichtigste: Since 2015 Brienz/Brinzauls has belonged to the municipality of Albula/Alvra.
The whole village lies on a sliding mass.
In 2019 the village moved about one metre a year down the valley.
In June 2023 a debris flow came down and stopped just before the village.
In November 2024 the village had to be evacuated for the second time.
A drainage tunnel is meant to slow the slide in the long term.

abschnitte.text: Brienz/Brinzauls was a municipality of its own until 2014. Since the merger, the village has belonged to **Albula/Alvra** in the Albula Valley. The double name is German and Romansh. The whole village lies on a large **sliding mass**. In 2019 it moved about **one metre a year** down the valley, and many houses developed cracks.

Above the village lay a particularly unstable mass of rock, the **“island”**. It comprised about 1.9 million cubic metres of rock. The village was **evacuated** as a precaution in May 2023. In the night of 16 June 2023, about 1.2 million cubic metres came down as a **debris flow**. It came to a stop only a few metres before the edge of the village, and nobody was hurt.

In autumn 2024 the slide became faster, reaching just under **2.5 metres a year**. Because rockfalls were also threatening, the residents had to leave the village again by **17 November 2024**. The evacuation continued in 2025. **Drainage boreholes** slowed the movement markedly by 2025.

A lot of water in the ground makes the slope more mobile. A **drainage tunnel** in the stable rock beneath the slide is meant to drain the water away. It extends an exploratory tunnel completed in 2023, was begun in 2024 and, according to the canton of the Grisons, is to be finished by **the end of 2027**. In addition, in 2025 the municipality planned a **preventive partial relocation**: owners could register to move buildings voluntarily to safe places.

gewusst: Less water pressure in the ground can slow a whole slide, which is why boreholes and tunnels are used.
The debris flow of 2023 stopped only a few metres in front of the first houses.

teile.einleitung: The Reuss is one of the great rivers of Switzerland. It rises on the Gotthard, flows through Lake Lucerne and right through the city of Lucerne.
wichtigste: The Reuss rises in the Gotthard area in the canton of Uri.
It is about 164 kilometres long.
At Flüelen it flows into Lake Lucerne, and in Lucerne out again.
In Lucerne the Chapel Bridge and the Spreuer Bridge cross the Reuss.
In the Schöllenen Gorge stands the Devil's Bridge.
The Reuss flows north and joins the Aare.

abschnitte.text: The Reuss rises in the **Gotthard area** in the canton of **Uri**. First it flows through the **Urseren Valley** and right through the village of **Andermatt**. Then it plunges through the wild **Schöllenen Gorge** down into the Uri Reuss Valley. From the start it flows north.

In the Schöllenen Gorge the **Devil's Bridge** crosses the roaring Reuss. For a long time this gorge was a difficult obstacle on the way over the Gotthard. An old **legend** tells that the devil built the first bridge. As payment he wanted the first soul to cross it. The clever people of Uri, however, are said to have sent a billy goat across first.

At **Flüelen** the Reuss flows into **Lake Lucerne**. In the lake its water mixes with the lake water. At the western end of the lake, in **Lucerne**, it flows out again. There it runs right through the old town.

The **Chapel Bridge**, an old covered wooden bridge with the octagonal **Water Tower**, is famous. Old pictures hang in the gable. In 1993 a large part of the bridge burned down and was then rebuilt. A little further downstream stands the **Spreuer Bridge**, also a covered wooden bridge with old pictures.

After Lucerne the Reuss flows on north through the cantons of Zug and Aargau, for example past **Bremgarten**. Near Brugg it flows into the **Aare**. At about 164 kilometres long, after the Rhine, the Aare and the Rhône it is the **fourth longest** river in Switzerland. Its catchment area covers about 3,400 square kilometres.

gewusst: Near Brugg the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet almost at the same spot, and the area is called the Wasserschloss (water castle) of Switzerland.
The Chapel Bridge in Lucerne is among the best-known sights in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The pharmaceutical industry makes medicines and is one of the most important branches of the Swiss economy. Its centre lies in Basel, where two of the largest pharmaceutical firms in the world have their headquarters.
wichtigste: Roche and Novartis have their headquarters in Basel.
Basel's pharmaceutical industry developed in the 19th century out of the dye industry.
Novartis was formed in 1996 from Ciba-Geigy and Sandoz.
Chemical and pharmaceutical products make up about half of Swiss goods exports.
Swissmedic checks whether a new medicine is approved.
In 1986 poisonous firefighting water polluted the Rhine during the fire at Schweizerhalle.

abschnitte.text: In the 19th century, Basel firms made artificial **dyes**, above all for **silk ribbon weaving**. In doing so they learned a lot about chemistry. From this knowledge, firms for chemicals and **medicines** later arose. Basel was well placed on the Rhine and close to Germany and France.

Today **Roche** and **Novartis** have their headquarters in Basel. Both are among the largest pharmaceutical firms in the world. **Novartis** was formed in **1996** when **Ciba-Geigy** and **Sandoz** merged. At the time it was one of the largest company mergers in the world. In October **2023** Novartis separated from its generics division **Sandoz**, which has been independent since then. **Generics** are cheaper copies of medicines whose patent has expired.

Roche's **Building 2** was completed in 2022 and is **205 metres** high. This makes it the tallest building in Switzerland (as of 2025). Right next to it stands **Building 1** at 178 metres. The two towers can be seen from far away and shape the cityscape of Basel.

**Chemical and pharmaceutical products** make up about **half of Swiss goods exports**. A large part of them comes from the Basel region. The firms employ many specialists from all over the world. Basel lies in the **Dreiländereck** (three country corner), so every day many **cross-border commuters** travel to work from Alsace in France and from southern Baden in Germany.

Before a medicine may be sold, **Swissmedic** checks whether it is safe and effective. Swissmedic is the Swiss Agency for Therapeutic Products in **Bern**. Environmental protection is also important. On 1 November **1986**, a Sandoz warehouse burned in **Schweizerhalle** near Basel. With the firefighting water, a lot of poison got into the **Rhine**, and fish died over many kilometres. After that, the rules for chemical stores were tightened considerably.

gewusst: The Schweizerhalle fire is regarded as one of the greatest environmental disasters in the history of Switzerland.
Developing a new medicine often takes more than ten years.

teile.einleitung: The Linth is the main river of the canton of Glarus. It flows from the Tödi to Lake Walen and from there on into Lake Zurich. It became famous through the Linth Correction, one of the first large building projects in the whole of Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Linth flows mainly through the canton of Glarus.
It rises in the area of the Tödi, the highest mountain in the Glarus Alps.
In the past the Linth caused terrible floods and swamps in the Linth plain.
Hans Conrad Escher led the Linth Correction at the beginning of the 19th century.
The Escher Canal leads the Linth into Lake Walen, and the Linth Canal carries it on into Lake Zurich.
From Lake Zurich the water flows on as the Limmat.
In the time of the Helvetic Republic there was a canton of Linth.

abschnitte.titel: From the Tödi into the Glarus region
abschnitte.text: The **Linth** rises at the foot of the **Tödi**, at about 3,600 metres the highest mountain in the Glarus Alps. It flows north through the narrow Glarner Hinterland, past Linthal and Schwanden. Then it reaches the main town of **Glarus** and the village of Näfels. At Mollis it leaves the mountains and enters the flat Linth plain.

In the past, the Linth flowed freely across the plain at Mollis to Lake Zurich. It brought a great deal of **bedload**, that is, stones and gravel, down from the mountains. As a result its bed kept rising, and it often burst its banks. The plain became a **swamp**, and many people fell ill with swamp fever, a form of malaria. Lake Walen was also dammed up, so that villages such as Weesen were flooded.

From 1807, **Hans Conrad Escher** of Zurich led the correction of the Linth. First the **Escher Canal** was built, which since 1811 has led the Linth directly into Lake Walen. There the bedload can settle without doing harm. After that the **Linth Canal** was built from Lake Walen to Lake Zurich. For his achievement Escher received the honorary name Escher von der Linth.

abschnitte.titel: A work of the whole of Switzerland
abschnitte.text: The Linth Correction is regarded as one of the first great joint works of the Confederation. The money came to a large extent from citizens from all over Switzerland, who bought **shares**. The swamp became fertile land for farmers. Today the Linth plain is an area of fields, villages and protected natural areas.

In the time of the **Helvetic Republic**, from 1798 to 1803, there was a canton of Linth with Glarus as its main town. Together with the cantons of Säntis and Waldstätten, it existed only during this short period. After that the old cantons were restored. In the Linth area, electricity is also produced today, for example in the large Linth-Limmern pumped-storage power plant high above Linthal.

begriffe.erklaerung: A river is guided into a new, safe bed with dams and canals.
Stones, gravel and sand that a river pushes along its bottom.
An artificially built watercourse.
The period from 1798 to 1803, when Switzerland was governed as a unitary state on the French model.

gewusst: Hans Conrad Escher received the honorary name “von der Linth” only after his death in 1823; his family may still bear it today.
The Linth and the Limmat really form a single river that gets a different name only after Lake Zurich.
The Linth was diverted into Lake Walen so that the lake would catch the rubble like a giant basin.

teile.einleitung: The Rhône Glacier lies right at the top of the Valais at the Furka Pass. The Rhône is formed from its meltwater, and it is one of the best researched glaciers in the world.
wichtigste: The Rhône Glacier is just under 8 kilometres long and about 2 kilometres wide.
It begins at about 3,600 m above sea level on the Dammastock.
Around 1856 it reached almost to the hotels of Gletsch.
Today its tongue ends at a good 2,200 m above sea level.
Since about 2007 a glacier lake has formed in front of the tongue.
The glacier has been measured regularly since 1874.

abschnitte.text: The Rhône Glacier forms at about **3,600 m above sea level** on the south west slope of the **Dammastock**. From there it flows south towards the Valais. It is just under **8 kilometres** long, about 2 kilometres wide and covers about 15 square kilometres. From its meltwater the **Rhône** is formed, which later flows through the Valais and Lake Geneva.

The top 2.5 kilometres or so form the **Eggfirn**. Firn is old, granular snow that turns into glacier ice. This is the glacier's **accumulation area**. On this section it drops by about 600 metres. That gives a gradient of 600 m divided by 2,500 m, which is 0.24, so **24 per cent**. Over the whole length the average gradient is only about 16 per cent.

Around **1856** the glacier had its greatest extent. At that time it reached almost to the hotels of **Gletsch**. Since then it has retreated far, and today the tongue ends in a rock step at a good **2,200 m above sea level**. On long term average, the ice became about **25 centimetres** thinner each year. In hot years, however, the tongue now loses several metres.

Since about **2007**, meltwater has been collecting in front of the glacier tongue behind a rock threshold. In this way a new **glacier lake** has formed. It will keep growing as the ice melts. Such lakes are now forming at many glaciers in the Alps.

From **1874** the engineer Gosset measured the glacier precisely. Since then there have been almost unbroken measurements, which is why it is one of the best researched glaciers. In summer you can visit a walk-in **ice grotto**, which is cut anew into the tongue every year. A short path leads up to it from the Furka road.

gewusst: To make the ice grotto melt less, part of the glacier is covered with white sheets in summer.
Old photos and measurements show exactly how far the Rhône Glacier has retreated since the 19th century.

teile.einleitung: Romansh is the fourth national language of Switzerland. It is spoken mainly in the canton of the Grisons, and it descends from the Latin of the Romans.
wichtigste: Romansh developed out of Latin.
It is spoken mainly in the Grisons.
There are five regional written forms, the idioms.
Rumantsch Grischun has been the shared written language since 1982.
Since 1996 Romansh has been a partial official language of the Confederation.
“Allegra” is a typical greeting.

abschnitte.text: Over 2,000 years ago the **Romans** came into the Alps and brought their language, **Latin**, with them. From this, **Romansh** developed over time. That is why many words sound similar to Italian or French. For example, water in Romansh is **“aua”**, from the Latin “aqua”.

With **“Allegra”** people greet each other in Romansh speaking Grisons. The word originally means “be glad”. **“Bun di”** means “Good day”, because “bun” means good and “di” day. Counting goes like this: **“in, dus, trais”**, that is, one, two, three. In Italian, by contrast, people say “tre” and in French “trois”.

Because the valleys used to be poorly connected with one another, five written forms of their own arose, the **idioms**: **Sursilvan**, **Sutsilvan**, **Surmiran**, **Puter** and **Vallader**. **Sutsilvan** is spoken on the Hinterrhein, for example in the Schams, the Domleschg and on the Heinzenberg. It is the smallest idiom. **Surmiran** is spoken in central Grisons, in the Surses and the Albula Valley, for example in Savognin.

In 1982 **Rumantsch Grischun** was created as a shared written language. It is meant to unite all Romansh speakers. The **Confederation** and the **canton of the Grisons** use it in official texts. In everyday life, however, people mostly speak their own idiom.

Since **1938** Romansh has been the fourth **national language** of Switzerland. Since the vote of 10 March **1996** it has also been a **partial official language** of the Confederation. That means: anyone who speaks Romansh can approach the Confederation in that language. Romansh is spoken by only a small part of the population, which is why its protection is important.

gewusst: On many Grisons place name signs there are two names, one in German and one in Romansh.
The Romansh word “aua” for water is still very similar to the Latin “aqua”.

teile.einleitung: The Zurich Oberland is a hilly region in the east of the canton of Zurich. It has mountains with views, deep valleys and old factories from the time of the textile industry. Many people come here for walking and for the steam railway.
wichtigste: The Zurich Oberland lies in the east of the canton of Zurich.
Uster is the largest town in the region.
The Bachtel with its lookout tower is about 1,115 metres high.
The Töss has formed a long valley, the Tösstal.
In the 19th century a large textile industry grew up here.
Historic steam trains run between Bauma and Hinwil.
Lake Pfäffikon and Lake Greifen lie on the western edge.

abschnitte.text: The **Zurich Oberland** lies between Lake Zurich and the border with the cantons of **Thurgau** and **St Gallen**. In the west it is rather flat, in the east hilly and wooded. On the western edge lie **Lake Pfäffikon** and **Lake Greifen**, both important nature reserves. The largest town is **Uster**, with over 35,000 residents (as of 2023).

Above **Wald** and **Hinwil** rises the **Bachtel**, about 1,115 metres high. From its **lookout tower** you can see over Lake Zurich to the Alps. Another popular destination is the **Hörnli** on the border with Thurgau, about 1,133 metres high. On the summit there is an inn. The hills often consist of **Nagelfluh**, a rock made of many pebbles cemented together.

The **Töss** rises in the area of the **Schnebelhorn**. It flows north through the **Tösstal** and later joins the **Rhine**. The valley is narrow and has many steep, wooded slopes. The hill country here is an old fan of debris from the **Molasse period**, when rivers deposited a lot of gravel from the young Alps.

In the **19th century**, many **spinning mills** and **weaving mills** grew up along the streams. The water supplied the **power** for the machines. For this, canals and ponds were built. Many old factories and canals still bear witness to that time today. A walking trail, the industrial heritage trail, leads past such places.

The **Zurich Oberland Steam Railway Association** runs the line from **Bauma** to **Hinwil**. On summer Sundays, old **steam locomotives** with historic carriages run there. Many families take a trip by train. Volunteer helpers look after the old vehicles.

gewusst: Nagelfluh looks like concrete with many round stones in it, but it is a natural rock.
The steam trains in the Zurich Oberland are run by volunteers.

teile.einleitung: The Säntis is the highest mountain in the Alpstein in eastern Switzerland. At about 2,502 metres it can be seen from far around. On the summit stand a weather station and a tall transmission tower.
wichtigste: The Säntis is the highest peak in the Alpstein.
It is about 2,502 metres high.
On the summit, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden and St Gallen meet.
An aerial cableway runs up the Säntis from the Schwägalp.
The weather station has been taking measurements for over 100 years.
The name probably goes back to the personal name Sambatinus.

abschnitte.text: The **Säntis** is the highest peak in the **Alpstein**, a mountain range in **eastern Switzerland** near the Appenzell region. It is about **2,502 metres** high. On the summit the cantons of **Appenzell Ausserrhoden**, **Appenzell Innerrhoden** and **St Gallen** meet. Because it is not far from **Lake Constance**, you can see the lake clearly from the summit on clear days. Many Alpine peaks can also be seen from the top.

Anyone who does not want to walk takes the **aerial cableway**. The valley station of the **Säntis cableway** stands on the **Schwägalp**. In a few minutes you float up to the top station by the summit. There is a restaurant and a viewing terrace there. Experienced walkers can also reach the summit on foot by various routes.

On the Säntis, a **weather station** has measured wind, snow and temperature for over 100 years. Because the mountain stands alone and high, the weather there is often rough and very windy. In addition, a tall **transmission tower** stands on the summit. It sends **radio** and television signals across the country. You can recognise the tower from far away.

The name Säntis probably goes back to the Romansh personal name **Sambatinus**. It means roughly “the one born on Saturday”. At first the name referred to an **Alp** (mountain pasture). Later it passed to the summit. Many mountain names in Switzerland arose in a similar way.

gewusst: From the Säntis, on clear days you can see into six countries.
On the Säntis there is often still snow when in the valley it has long been spring.

teile.einleitung: The Susten Pass is an Alpine pass between the cantons of Bern and Uri. Its road leads past glaciers and mountain lakes. It was one of the first passes built especially for cars.
wichtigste: The Susten Pass links Innertkirchen in the canton of Bern with Wassen in the canton of Uri.
The top of the pass lies at about 2,260 metres above sea level.
The modern Susten road was opened in 1946.
By the road lie the Steingletscher and the Steinsee.
In winter the pass is closed for several months.

abschnitte.text: The **Susten Pass** links the cantons of **Bern** and **Uri**. The road begins in **Innertkirchen** in the Bernese Oberland and leads up through the Gadmen valley. On the Uri side it ends in **Wassen** in the Reuss valley. There it meets the Gotthard road. The top of the pass lies at about **2,260 metres** above sea level.

The modern **Susten road** was built from 1938 and opened to traffic in 1946. It was one of the first pass roads planned especially for **cars**. At the very top the road runs through a short **summit tunnel**. After that it goes down again on the other side. Because of snow and **avalanches**, the pass is closed for several months in winter.

Below the top of the pass on the Bern side lies the **Steingletscher**. Next to it stands the Hotel Steingletscher. In front of the glacier lies the little **Steinsee**. It formed when the ice of the glacier retreated and melted. Many excursionists stop here to marvel at the landscape.

gewusst: With the Grimsel and the Furka, the Susten forms a popular round trip over three passes.
The Steingletscher has shrunk strongly in recent decades.

teile.einleitung: The Seine is the best-known river in France and flows right through the capital, Paris. On its banks stand landmarks such as Notre-Dame Cathedral and the Eiffel Tower. In 2024 even the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games took place on it.
wichtigste: The Seine is about 780 kilometres long and flows only in France.
It rises in Burgundy on the Plateau de Langres.
It flows through Paris and Rouen.
At Le Havre it flows into the English Channel.
In 2024 the opening ceremony of the Olympic Games took place on the Seine in Paris.
The banks of the Seine in Paris are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

abschnitte.text: The Seine rises on the **Plateau de Langres** in Burgundy, north-west of Dijon. It flows north-west through Champagne and the Paris Basin. Important tributaries are the Aube, Yonne, Marne and Oise. After Rouen it grows wider and wider and flows into the **English Channel** at Le Havre.

In Paris, the islands **Île de la Cité** and Île Saint-Louis lie in the middle of the river. On the Île de la Cité stands Notre-Dame Cathedral, which was rebuilt after a fire in 2019. In Paris about 37 bridges cross the Seine, and the oldest is, of all things, the Pont Neuf, the “new bridge”. On the bank, the **bouquinistes** sell old books and postcards from green boxes.

At the 2024 Olympic Games, the teams travelled on boats over the Seine at the **opening ceremony**. It was the first time that an opening ceremony did not take place in a stadium. Triathlon and open-water swimming were also held in the Seine. For this, Paris had put a lot of money into cleaning the river.

For about a hundred years, swimming in the Seine in Paris was forbidden because the water was too dirty. New sewage treatment plants and storage basins for rainwater have improved the **water quality**. Since 2025 there have again been official bathing spots in the river in Paris in summer. In heavy rain, however, swimming is sometimes prohibited.

The Romans already knew the settlement of Lutetia on the Île de la Cité, which became Paris. For centuries the Seine was an important **trade route** for timber, wine and grain. In 1910 a great flood covered large parts of Paris. Since then the water level has been read, among other things, from a statue of a soldier at the Pont de l'Alma.

begriffe.erklaerung: The strait between France and Great Britain.
Booksellers who sell old books on the banks of the Seine.
An installation that cleans dirty wastewater.
A river that flows into a larger river.

gewusst: The Pont Neuf means “new bridge”, but it is the oldest bridge still standing in Paris.
The city of Paris bought the land at the source of the Seine, so the source belongs to the city of Paris.
In floods, Parisians measure the height of the Seine at the stone figure of a soldier, the Zouave at the Pont de l'Alma.

teile.einleitung: The Napf is a mountain between the Emmental and the Entlebuch. It is not an Alpine peak but rises out of the Central Plateau and is surrounded by many gullies and ridges.
wichtigste: The Napf is about 1,400 metres high.
It lies on the border of the cantons of Bern and Lucerne.
The summit belongs to the Bernese municipality of Trub in the Emmental.
The Napf consists mainly of Nagelfluh.
Ridges run out from the Napf in all directions like a star.
The Luthern rises on the north slope and flows to the Wigger.

abschnitte.titel: A mountain on the Central Plateau
abschnitte.text: The Napf reaches about **1,400 metres above sea level**. It is the highest peak of the **Napf hills** between the Emmental and the Entlebuch. It is mostly counted as part of the **Central Plateau**, because it consists of molasse rock. On the summit stands a mountain inn. From there you can see the Alps and the Jura in fine weather.

The summit of the Napf belongs to the municipality of **Trub** in the Emmental in the canton of **Bern**. Just north of it begins the canton of **Lucerne**. The cantonal border therefore runs very close to the summit. Both sides are rural and shaped by farms.

The Napf consists mainly of **Nagelfluh**. This rock is made of rounded pebbles that rivers brought here from the Alps. The Napf hills are an old **debris fan**. In the streams you find fine flakes of gold that come from these pebbles. That is why the area is known for its **Napf gold**.

From the Napf many narrow **ridges** run out like rays in all directions. Between them, streams have cut deep, steep **gullies** into the soft rock. This creates a landscape of many hills and narrow valleys. On the north slope the **Luthern** rises. It flows through a deep valley to the north to the Wigger.

gewusst: In the streams around the Napf you can pan for gold.
The Napf hills are a large old debris fan of rivers that came out of the Alps millions of years ago.

teile.einleitung: Orographic lift occurs when wind pushes moist air against a mountain range. The air has to rise, cools and forms clouds and rain. On the other side of the mountains the weather is often quite different.
wichtigste: In orographic lift, air is raised at the mountains, cools and rains out.
Unsaturated air cools by about 1 °C per 100 m as it rises.
Saturated air cools by only about 0.5 °C per 100 m, because heat is released during condensation.
With southern stau it rains in Ticino, while in the north the south foehn often blows.
The foehn wall is a wall of cloud over the Alpine crest.
Altdorf in the canton of Uri is known for frequent foehn.

abschnitte.text: When air flows against a mountain range, it has to **rise**. As it does, it expands and **cools**. Cool air can hold less water vapour, so it **condenses** into droplets, and clouds form. On the side facing the wind, the **windward side**, a lot of precipitation therefore falls. The other side is called the **lee side**.

**Unsaturated air** cools by about **1 °C per 100 m** as it rises. This is called dry adiabatic. As it sinks, it warms by the same amount. **Saturated air** cools by only about **0.5 °C per 100 m**. The reason: when water vapour condenses into droplets, **latent heat** is released, which slows the cooling.

The **cloud base** can be estimated with a rule of thumb: 125 m per degree of difference between temperature and **dew point**. If air is at 18 °C and has a dew point of 10 °C, the difference is 8 °C. 8 times 125 m gives about **1,000 m**. Foehn warmth can also be calculated: air at 20 °C at 200 m cools to 10 °C by 1,200 m and then rises moist to 3,000 m, where it is still at 1 °C. If it sinks dry down to 500 m, it warms by 25 °C and is at **26 °C** there.

With **southern stau** it often rains heavily in **Ticino**. The air rains out on the south side and sinks on the north side. As it does, it warms and blows as a warm, dry **south foehn** into the northern Alpine valleys. From the north you then see a sharp wall of cloud over the Alpine crest, the **foehn wall**. The foehn blows especially often in **Altdorf** in the Reuss valley, which runs in a north south direction.

In a **northwest stau** situation, moist air from the Atlantic meets the **northern edge of the Alps**. There it rises and rains out. On the northern slope of the Alps especially a lot of precipitation then falls, often a lot of snow in winter. South of the Alps it mostly stays drier in this situation. In this way the weather in Switzerland depends strongly on the direction the wind comes from.

gewusst: The foehn can make the temperature rise by many degrees within a few hours.
In popular speech the foehn is also called “the oldest man of Uri”.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland people speak four national languages: German, French, Italian and Romansh. Each language region has its own culture. So that everyone can live together well, there are clear rules in the constitution and in law.
wichtigste: The four national languages are German, French, Italian and Romansh.
About 23 per cent of the population give French as their main language.
Freedom of language is protected in Article 18 of the Federal Constitution.
Under the territoriality principle, the cantons decide their official language.
Bern, Fribourg and the Valais are bilingual, and the Grisons is trilingual.
The federal Languages Act has been in force since 2010.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland there are four **national languages**. Most people speak **German**, and about 23 per cent give **French** as their main language. Italian is spoken mainly in Ticino and in parts of the Grisons, **Romansh** only in the Grisons. Since 2010, people questioned in the structural survey of the Federal Statistical Office may give several main languages. That is why the shares add up to more than 100 per cent.

French speaking Switzerland is called the **Romandie**. It includes the cantons of Geneva, Vaud, Neuchâtel and Jura as well as parts of Bern, Fribourg and the Valais. The **Bernese Jura**, with places such as Saint-Imier and Tavannes, is also French speaking. Moutier belonged to it until the end of 2025 and then changed over to the canton of Jura. Only four cantons are multilingual: **Bern**, **Fribourg** and the **Valais** are bilingual, and the **Grisons** is trilingual.

Article 18 of the Federal Constitution guarantees **freedom of language**. Everyone may use their own language. In dealings with the authorities, however, the **territoriality principle** applies: in an area, the language traditionally spoken there is the official and school language. The **Languages Act** was passed in 2007 and came into force in 2010. It regulates the official languages of the Confederation and promotes understanding between the language groups.

In German speaking Switzerland people speak **Swiss German** in everyday life but mostly write **Standard German**. This division between two forms of language is called **diglossia**. At school children also learn a second national language. This way people from different regions can understand one another better.

abschnitte.titel: Languages in politics and the media
abschnitte.text: Article 175 of the Federal Constitution requires that the regions and language regions of the country be fairly represented in the **Federal Council**. There is no fixed quota, however. The **SRG** has its own broadcasters for each language region. **SRF** broadcasts for German speaking Switzerland, **RTS** for the Romandie, **RSI** for Italian speaking and **RTR** for Romansh speaking Switzerland. RTS stands for Radio Télévision Suisse and has sites in Geneva and Lausanne.

gewusst: Romansh is a national language, but is spoken by only a small part of the population.
On Swiss banknotes there are texts in all four national languages.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland has special areas with valuable nature and landscape, the parks of national importance. The Confederation awards them a label and supports them.
wichtigste: Federal law recognises three categories: National Park, Regional Nature Park and Nature Discovery Park.
The Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) awards the park label.
The label is valid for 10 years at a time.
The legal basis with the Parks Ordinance has existed since 2007.
The Parc Ela in the Grisons is the largest nature park in Switzerland.
The Wildnispark Zürich Sihlwald was the first Nature Discovery Park.

abschnitte.text: Since **2007**, with a revision of the **Nature and Cultural Heritage Protection Act** and the **Parks Ordinance**, there have been new park categories. Federal law distinguishes three kinds: **National Park**, **Regional Nature Park** and **Nature Discovery Park**. The most common are the regional nature parks. Regions can apply to the Confederation for a park label. The impetus comes from the municipalities and the people on the spot.

The **Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN)** examines the applications and awards the label “Park of National Importance”. It also supports the parks with money. The label is valid for **10 years**. After that the Confederation checks whether the park has reached its goals. Only then is the label renewed.

A **regional nature park** is an inhabited, rural region with fine nature and culture. The people live and work in the park. The **economy** there is to be strengthened in a sustainable way, for example through tourism and local products. The **Parc Ela** in central Grisons around the Albula and Julier passes is the largest nature park in Switzerland. In the Valais lies the **Pfyn-Finges Nature Park** with a large pine forest on the Rhône.

A **nature discovery park** lies close to a city, at most about 20 kilometres from a densely populated area. In its **core zone**, nature is to develop freely. A **transition zone** serves visitors' experience of nature. The **Wildnispark Zürich Sihlwald** was the first nature discovery park in Switzerland.

The **Swiss National Park** in the Engadine was founded in 1914 and is still the only national park in Switzerland. People wanted to create a second one. The **Parc Adula** project in the area of the Grisons and Ticino, however, was rejected in **2016** by the majority of the municipalities. Supporters hoped for nature conservation and tourism, while opponents feared too many restrictions.

gewusst: The Swiss National Park is one of the oldest national parks in the Alps.
In the Sihlwald near Zurich, the forest has been allowed to grow wild again for many years, without any timber being felled.

teile.einleitung: Lake Geneva is the largest lake in the Alps and lies in south-western Switzerland on the border with France. It has the shape of a crescent and stretches from Geneva to Villeneuve. In French it is called Lac Léman, and on its shores lie cities such as Geneva, Lausanne and Montreux.
wichtigste: Switzerland shares Lake Geneva with France.
At about 580 square kilometres, it is the largest lake in the Alps.
The largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland, however, is Lake Neuchâtel.
The Rhône comes from the Rhône Glacier, flows through Valais into Lake Geneva and out again at Geneva.
The landmark of Geneva is the Jet d'eau, a huge fountain of water in the lake.
Near Montreux stands the famous moated castle of Chillon.
The vineyard terraces of Lavaux on the north shore are a UNESCO World Heritage site.

abschnitte.text: Lake Geneva lies at about 372 metres above sea level between the Alps and the Jura. It is about 73 kilometres long, up to about 14 kilometres wide and about 310 metres deep at its deepest point. The north shore belongs to the cantons of **Vaud** and Geneva, the south shore mostly to the French département of **Haute-Savoie**, and in the far east Valais borders it. A little more than half of the lake's area belongs to Switzerland.

In the last ice age, the mighty **Rhône Glacier** filled the basin of today's lake and even reached as far as the area of Solothurn. When the ice melted, a deep basin remained, which filled with water. Today the **Rhône** flows into the lake at Le Bouveret and leaves it again at Geneva. Because the water stays in the lake for a long time, the mud settles, and the Rhône flows on clear and blue in Geneva.

At the outflow of the lake lies the city of Geneva, which was called Genava in Roman times. In the middle of the harbour, the **Jet d'eau** shoots its water about 140 metres into the air. Originally it was only a pressure relief valve of a waterworks, but today it is the city's landmark. The Helvetii already wanted to cross the Rhône at Geneva in 58 BC but were stopped by Julius Caesar.

On a rock in the lake near Montreux stands **Chillon Castle**, a moated castle from the Middle Ages. There in the past lived nobles such as the Counts of Savoy with their knights and servants. Between Lausanne and Montreux, the steep vineyard terraces of **Lavaux** climb the slope; they have been UNESCO World Heritage since 2007. The climate by the lake is so mild that even palms grow on the Riviera around Montreux.

Over a million people live around Lake Geneva. The International Olympic Committee has its seat in Lausanne, and many international organisations such as the Red Cross work in Geneva. On the lake sail the ships of the **CGN**, including several beautiful paddle steamers from around 1900. Fishers catch mainly perch and whitefish, which are regarded as a speciality.

Fish from the lake should be eaten only well cooked or fried. In 2006, several wedding guests were infected with the **fish tapeworm** after eating marinated raw perch from Lake Geneva. Heating or deep freezing kills such parasites. The lake water itself is clean again today and is even treated to make drinking water.

begriffe.erklaerung: The French name of Lake Geneva.
A castle surrounded by water, which made it better protected.
A place that UNESCO designates as especially valuable to all humanity and wants to protect.
A long parasite that can live in the gut if you eat raw, infected fish.

gewusst: Like a sea, Lake Geneva can have small oscillations of the water level, which are called seiches.
The Jet d'eau throws about 500 litres of water into the air every second.
Lake Geneva contains about 89 billion cubic metres of water and is therefore the lake with the most water in central Europe.

teile.einleitung: The Lunghin Pass lies in the Upper Engadine above Maloja. At this spot the paths of water divide in three directions and to three different seas.
wichtigste: The Lunghin Pass lies in the Upper Engadine near Maloja in the Grisons.
Three large catchment areas meet here.
The water flows via the Rhine, the Po and the Inn.
In this way it reaches the North Sea, the Adriatic and the Black Sea.

abschnitte.text: A **watershed** is a line in the landscape at which it is decided in which direction the water flows. At the **Lunghin Pass**, three large **catchment areas** meet. Rain that falls here can therefore run off in three different directions. That is why the spot is called a **triple watershed**.

To the north the water flows via the **Rhine** into the **North Sea**. To the south it reaches the **Adriatic**, a part of the Mediterranean, via the **Po**. To the east it flows via the **Inn** and the Danube into the **Black Sea**. Below the pass lies Lake Lunghin, which is regarded as the source of the Inn.

The Lunghin Pass lies high above **Maloja** in the Upper Engadine, canton of the Grisons. You can only reach it on foot along a mountain path. The path is popular with walkers, because here you stand at a special point in Europe.

gewusst: Depending on which side it falls on, a drop of water at the Lunghin Pass can end up in one of three seas that lie thousands of kilometres apart.

teile.einleitung: Lake Murten lies between the cantons of Fribourg and Vaud at the foot of the Jura. It is the smallest of the three great Jura foot lakes. On its shore lies the little town of Murten with its famous town wall.
wichtigste: Lake Murten lies in the cantons of Fribourg and Vaud.
In French it is called Lac de Morat.
It is about 23 square kilometres in size and at most about 45 metres deep.
The Broye flows through the lake on into Lake Neuchâtel.
On the north shore lies the Mont Vully with vineyards.
In 1476 the Confederates defeated Charles the Bold at Murten.
You can walk along the town wall of Murten.

abschnitte.titel: A lake at the foot of the Jura
abschnitte.text: **Lake Murten**, together with **Lake Neuchâtel** and **Lake Biel**, is one of the three great **Jura foot lakes**. It is the **smallest** of them, about **23 square kilometres** in size. At its deepest point it measures only about **45 metres**. The **Broye** flows into the lake and leaves it by the **Broye Canal** towards Lake Neuchâtel. In French the lake is called **Lac de Morat**, because the little town of Murten is called Morat in French.

**Murten** lies on the south east shore of the lake in the canton of Fribourg. The old town is surrounded by a well preserved **town wall** from the Middle Ages. You can **walk along** its covered walkway and look over the roofs as far as the lake. In Murten people speak German and French. The town, with its arcades and fountains, is a popular place to visit.

In **1476** a famous battle took place at Murten. Duke **Charles the Bold** of **Burgundy** besieged the town with his army. The **Confederates** and their allies hurried to help and **defeated** the Burgundian army. The victory is one of the best-known events in Swiss history. Shortly afterwards Charles the Bold lost his life at the Battle of Nancy.

On the north shore lies the **Mont Vully**, a hill between Lake Murten and Lake Neuchâtel. On its slope towards Lake Murten grow many **vines**, from which wine is made. The area around the Jura foot lakes is also called the **Three Lakes Region**. Not far from the lake lies **Avenches**, which in Roman times, as Aventicum, was an important town.

gewusst: For the national exhibition Expo.02, a large cube stood in Lake Murten, the Monolith by the architect Jean Nouvel.
On the shore of Lake Murten, remains of pile dwelling villages from the Stone Age were found.

teile.einleitung: St Gallen is a town in eastern Switzerland and the capital of the canton of the same name. It grew up around a famous monastery. Today it is known for its Abbey Library, its bratwurst and the Olma.
wichtigste: According to a legend, a bear helped the monk Gallus.
Gallus settled in the valley of the Steinach.
The abbey district has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
Around 1900 St Gallen was world famous for embroidery.
St Gallen bratwurst is traditionally eaten without mustard.
The Olma takes place in St Gallen in October.

abschnitte.text: The name of the town goes back to the monk **Gallus**. He settled in the valley of the **Steinach**. According to the legend, a **bear** brought wood for his fire and received a piece of bread as a reward. That is why the bear is still a symbol of St Gallen today. The Steinach now flows underground through the town for long stretches.

From the hermitage of Gallus a significant **monastery** later grew. The **abbey district** with its cathedral and **Abbey Library** has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983. The Abbey Library owns thousands of manuscripts, some of them over 1,000 years old. It is one of the oldest libraries in the world.

Around 1900 St Gallen was a world centre of **embroidery**. Fine St Gallen **lace** was sold to many countries. Rich merchants had houses with splendid **oriel windows** built in the old town. Today there are over a hundred, often richly decorated oriels there. Even today, firms in St Gallen still make fine fabrics.

Every year in October the **Olma** takes place, a large fair for agriculture and food. There you can see animals and try specialities. Famous is the **St Gallen bratwurst** made of veal. Traditionally it is eaten **without mustard**, because many people think mustard would spoil its taste. A modern work of art is the **Stadtlounge** in the Bleicheli quarter, where a red covering runs like a carpet over squares and furniture.

gewusst: In the Stadtlounge even a car is covered with the red surface.
The St Gallen bratwurst has a protected designation of origin.

teile.einleitung: Winterthur is the second-largest city in the canton of Zurich and the sixth-largest in Switzerland. Many people call it “Winti” for short. It used to be a big industrial city; today it is known for museums, gardens and its car-free old town.
wichtigste: Winterthur is the sixth-largest city in Switzerland (as of 2023).
In the canton of Zurich, only the city of Zurich is larger.
The city's nickname is “Winti”.
The Counts of Kyburg are regarded as the founders of the city.
The firm Sulzer built machines and ship engines here.
The Technorama is the Swiss Science Center.
Because of its many green spaces, Winterthur is called a garden city.

abschnitte.text: Winterthur lies in the **north-east** of the canton of **Zurich**. With about 120,000 residents it is the **sixth-largest city** in Switzerland (as of 2023). In the canton only the city of Zurich is larger. In everyday speech many people simply say **“Winti”**. The **Eulach** flows through the city and today runs in a channel in many places.

The **Counts of Kyburg** had their castle very close by. They are regarded as the **founders** of the city of Winterthur in the Middle Ages. Kyburg Castle still stands today and is a museum. Later Winterthur came under the rule of the Habsburgs and then belonged to the city of Zurich for a long time.

In the 19th and 20th centuries, Winterthur became an important **industrial city**. The firm **Sulzer** built large **machines** and **ship engines** there. The **Sulzer high-rise** was the tallest building in Switzerland from 1966 to 1978. Today many old factory halls are used for homes, schools and culture.

In the **Technorama**, the **Swiss Science Center**, you can experiment yourself at many stations. You play with light, water, magnets and electricity and so get to know the natural sciences. Winterthur also has many **art museums**. That is why the city is regarded as an important cultural city in Switzerland.

The **old town** of Winterthur is the largest continuous **pedestrian zone** in Switzerland. You can walk almost everywhere there, and cars hardly drive. Winterthur also has many **parks** and family gardens. That is why it is also called a **garden city**.

gewusst: The Sulzer high-rise in Winterthur was the tallest building in Switzerland from 1966 to 1978.
The old town of Winterthur is the largest continuous pedestrian zone in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Four-thousanders are mountains that are more than 4,000 metres high. In Switzerland there are about 50 of them, most in the canton of Valais. Anyone who wants to climb them needs experience, good equipment and often a mountain guide.
wichtigste: A four-thousander is a mountain that is more than 4,000 metres high.
In Switzerland there are about 50 four-thousanders.
Most of them stand in the canton of Valais.
The Matterhorn is a four-thousander, the Titlis is not.
The UIAA main list counts 82 four-thousanders in the Alps.
Higher up the air is thinner, so breathing is harder.
On glaciers you need crampons on your boots.

abschnitte.text: A **four-thousander** is a mountain whose summit lies **more than 4,000 metres** above sea level. In Switzerland there are **about 50** such peaks. The exact number depends on which subsidiary peaks are counted. The mountaineering association **UIAA** counts **82** four-thousanders in its main list for the whole of the Alps.

Most Swiss four-thousanders stand in the canton of **Valais**. These include the famous **Matterhorn** near Zermatt and the **Dufourspitze**, the highest peak in Switzerland. There are also a few in the Bernese Alps, such as the **Jungfrau** and the **Finsteraarhorn**. In the Grisons, the **Piz Bernina** is the only one. At about 3,238 metres, the **Titlis** is **not** a four-thousander.

On the four-thousanders there is almost always **snow and ice**, even in summer. Up there it is cold and windy. The **air is also thinner**. This means there is less oxygen in every breath. So you breathe harder and get tired more quickly. Many mountaineers therefore get used to the altitude for a few days first.

A climb is dangerous if you have no experience. A **mountain guide** takes guests safely to the summit. He knows the way and recognises dangers such as crevasses or sudden changes in the weather. On the glacier you need **crampons**, which are metal spikes on your boots. You also need a rope, an ice axe and a helmet.

gewusst: At 4,634 metres, the Dufourspitze in the Monte Rosa massif is the highest mountain in Switzerland.
The Matterhorn was first climbed in 1865.

teile.einleitung: In the mountains, forest stops above a certain height. This line is called the forest line. Where it lies depends mainly on the warmth in summer, but also on people.
wichtigste: Above the forest line only single trees remain, and only the tree line marks the end of all trees.
In Switzerland the natural forest line lies highest in the Central Alps.
Large mountain massifs raise the forest line through the massif elevation effect.
Below a mean temperature of about 6 °C in the growing season, trees no longer grow.
The transition zone with stunted trees is called the battle zone.
Clearing and grazing have lowered the forest line in many places.
Today the forest line is rising in the Swiss Alps.

abschnitte.text: The **forest line** is the height up to which a continuous forest grows. Above it there are only **single trees** or small groups of trees. Where these stop too, lies the **tree line**. Between the two lines lies the **battle zone**. There the trees grow low and **stunted**, because they are fighting against cold, wind and snow.

Trees need enough warmth to grow. According to present knowledge, they stop growing when the mean air temperature during the **growing season** is below **about 6 °C**. The growing season is the time of year when plants grow. At great heights this summer is too short and too cool.

In Switzerland the natural forest line lies highest in the **Central Alps**, for example in Valais and the Engadine. Large **mountain massifs** store warmth and have fewer clouds. As a result it is warmer there than on individual mountains at the edge of the Alps. This effect is called the **massif elevation effect**. Typical trees at the forest line are **larch** and **Swiss stone pine**.

In many places the forest line lies **lower** than would be naturally possible. The reason: over centuries, forest was **cleared** to win **alpine pastures** for livestock. **Grazing** prevented new trees from growing. Above the forest line, the **green alder** often forms dense thickets on damp, shady slopes.

Today the forest line in the Swiss Alps is **rising**. One reason is that many alpine pastures are no longer used. There the forest is slowly growing back. Another reason is **global warming**: when it gets warmer, trees can also grow higher up.

gewusst: Swiss stone pines at the forest line can live to be several hundred years old.
The larch is the only native conifer that loses its needles in autumn.

teile.einleitung: Hydropower means using the force of flowing or falling water to produce electricity. In Switzerland it is the most important domestic source of electricity. Mountains, glaciers and plenty of rain make this possible.
wichtigste: In 2024, about 60 per cent of Swiss electricity came from hydropower.
At the start of 2026 there were about 700 hydropower plants with an output of more than 300 kilowatts.
Run-of-river power plants use the flowing water of a river.
Storage power plants collect water in reservoirs in the mountains.
Nant de Drance in Valais is a large pumped-storage power plant.
The Mauvoisin dam is about 250 metres high.

abschnitte.titel: How electricity is made from water
abschnitte.text: Water that flows or falls has **energy**. In a power plant it streams through a **turbine** and makes it turn. The turbine drives a **generator**, which produces electricity. The more water and the greater the drop, the more electricity is produced. Hydropower is **renewable**, because rain and snow keep supplying the water again and again.

According to the Federal Office of Energy, **about 60 per cent** of the electricity produced in Switzerland in **2024** came from hydropower. On 1 January 2026, **706 hydropower plants** with an output of more than 300 kilowatts were in operation. There are also many small installations on streams. The Alps, with their high mountains and glaciers, are ideal for this.

A **run-of-river power plant** dams a river with a weir and uses the water flowing through continuously. It supplies electricity steadily round the clock. A **storage power plant** collects water in a **reservoir** high in the mountains. When needed, the water is let down through pipes to the turbines. That way electricity can be produced when it is needed.

A **pumped-storage power plant** works like a giant battery. When there is too much electricity, it pumps water into an upper lake.
