When electricity is needed, the water flows back and drives the turbines. **Nant de Drance** near Finhaut in Valais began operating in **2022**. It lies in a rock cavern between the reservoirs of Emosson and Vieux Emosson and has an output of **900 megawatts**.

The reservoirs need enormous **dams**. The arch dam **Mauvoisin** in the Val de Bagnes is about **250 metres** high. It is among the highest dams in Switzerland. An arch dam is curved against the water and directs the pressure sideways into the rock. The highest dam in Switzerland is the Grande Dixence.

gewusst: A pumped-storage power plant can store electricity by pumping water uphill.
The machines of Nant de Drance are hidden deep in the rock.

teile.einleitung: Pilatus is the local mountain of Lucerne. You can see it from the whole city, and old legends of dragons cluster around it. It is also famous for its very steep rack railway.
wichtigste: Pilatus stands south west of Lucerne.
Its highest peak is the Tomlishorn at 2,128 metres.
At up to 48 per cent, the Pilatus Railway is the steepest rack railway in the world.
It has run up from Alpnachstad since 1889.
In winter the rack railway does not run.
From Kriens you can get up by gondola lift and aerial cableway.

abschnitte.text: Pilatus rises **south west of Lucerne**. It has several peaks. The highest is the **Tomlishorn** at **2,128 metres**. The well-known peak **Esel** by the Pilatus Kulm top station is about ten metres lower. From the top you can see over Lake Lucerne, the Central Plateau and the Alps.

The **Pilatus Railway** has run since **1889** from **Alpnachstad** on Lake Alpnach to Pilatus Kulm. At its steepest point it is **48 per cent** steep. This makes it the **steepest rack railway in the world**. A rack railway has a cogwheel that engages in a toothed rack between the rails. This stops the train from slipping on the steep slope.

On the other side you go up from **Kriens**, first by **gondola lift** and then by **aerial cableway**. This lets you make a **round trip**: by boat to Alpnachstad, up by rack railway and down by cable cars. The rack railway only runs from about **spring to autumn**. In winter there is too much snow on the line.

In the past people said that **dragons** lived on Pilatus. One legend tells of a dragon stone that was supposed to have healing powers. That is why the **dragon** is still a symbol of the mountain today. According to another legend, the mountain is said to be named after **Pontius Pilate**, whose ghost is said to have haunted a mountain lake.

gewusst: In the past it was forbidden to climb Pilatus, because people feared disturbing the ghost in the mountain lake and causing storms.
The Pilatus Railway was built with a special rack in which two cogwheels engage from the side.

teile.einleitung: Raw materials are substances from nature from which things are made, for example wood, salt, gravel or crude oil. Switzerland has only a few raw materials of its own and has to import a lot.
wichtigste: Switzerland is poor in mineral resources.
Gravel and sand are the raw materials extracted in the largest quantities.
Salt is obtained at Schweizerhalle, Riburg and Bex.
Crude oil and natural gas are imported entirely.
Hydropower supplies more than half of Swiss electricity.
About a third of Switzerland is covered with forest, which supplies wood.

abschnitte.text: The raw material extracted in Switzerland in the largest quantities is **gravel and sand**. The glaciers of the **Ice Ages** deposited a lot of it on the Central Plateau. It is used mainly to make **concrete** for houses, roads and bridges. That is why gravel pits can be seen in many parts of the Central Plateau.

An important mineral resource is **salt**. The Swiss salt works produce it at **Schweizerhalle** and **Riburg** near Basel and at **Bex** in the canton of Vaud. The salt lies deep in the ground and is dissolved out with water. It serves as table salt, for industry, and in winter as **road salt** on the roads.

Switzerland itself produces no **crude oil** and no **natural gas**. Everything has to be brought in by pipeline, ship, rail or lorry. Many goods such as heating oil, grain and containers come by ship along the **Rhine** to the Rhine ports in **Basel**. An important home grown energy source, however, is water: reservoirs and river power stations produce more than half of Swiss electricity.

About a third of the country's area is **forest**. It supplies **wood**, a renewable raw material that is used as building material, for furniture and for heating. In the past there were also mines in Switzerland. At the **Gonzen** near Sargans in the St Gallen Rhine Valley, **iron ore** was mined for centuries. The mine closed in 1966 and can be visited today.

abschnitte.titel: Making a lot from a little
abschnitte.text: Because raw materials of its own are lacking, Switzerland imports many of them and **processes** them into valuable products. Examples are medicines, machines and watches. Well trained **specialists** are important here. In addition, many large firms have their seats in **Zug** and **Geneva** that trade worldwide in oil, metals and grain. These raw materials mostly do not come to Switzerland at all.

gewusst: The Swiss Rhine ports in Basel are connected via the Rhine with Rotterdam on the North Sea.
The old iron mine at the Gonzen can be explored today as a visitor mine.

teile.einleitung: With the Swiss national coordinates you can fix every point in Switzerland exactly. Two numbers say how far east and how far north a place lies. This is how national maps, surveying and many navigation devices work.
wichtigste: The old reference point in the LV03 system was the old observatory in Bern.
In LV03, Bern had the coordinates 600,000 / 200,000.
In the new LV95 system, every easting begins with a 2 and every northing with a 1.
You always give the easting first, then the northing.
The values are given in metres, so distances are easy to calculate.
The fundamental point of LV95 is the Zimmerwald Observatory south of Bern.

abschnitte.text: On every Swiss national map you can see a fine **coordinate grid**. Every point has two numbers: the **easting** (the east value) and the **northing** (the north value). You always give the easting first and then the northing. The numbers are given in metres. The Federal Office of Topography, **swisstopo** for short, is responsible for national surveying.

In the old **LV03** system, the **old observatory in Bern** was the reference point. It was given the coordinates 600,000 and 200,000. From there the whole country was surveyed. Bern was deliberately given such large values so that all points in Switzerland have positive numbers. In addition, all eastings lie above 480,000 and all northings below 300,000, so you can never mix up the two values.

Today the more precise reference frame **LV95** applies. In it a 2 is put in front of the easting and a 1 in front of the northing. The point in Bern is therefore called 2,600,000 / 1,200,000. This way you can see at once whether a figure comes from the old or the new system. The **fundamental point** of LV95 is the **Zimmerwald Observatory**, about 10 km south of Bern. The new survey also uses satellites.

Because the coordinates are given in metres, you can work out distances directly. If one point is at easting 2,610,500 and another at 2,600,000, the difference is 10,500 m, that is **10.5 km**. If point B lies 3,000 m east and 4,000 m north of point A, the **Pythagorean theorem** helps. The square root of 9 million plus 16 million gives 5,000 m. The straight line distance is therefore **5 km**.

gewusst: Thanks to the coordinates, you can give any place on the national map to the nearest metre.
The Zimmerwald Observatory also watches satellites in the sky.

teile.einleitung: The network of national roads connects Switzerland from Geneva to St Margrethen and from Basel to Chiasso. It was built piece by piece from the 1960s and is still being extended and maintained today.
wichtigste: The first section of the N1 was the Grauholz motorway near Bern, opened in 1962.
The motorway vignette was introduced in 1985, and since 2023 it has also been available electronically.
On expressways the maximum speed is 100.
The A13 runs through the San Bernardino Tunnel from Ticino to the Grisons.
The Seelisberg Tunnel of the A2 runs about 9 kilometres along Lake Uri.
In 2017 the people accepted the NAF fund, and in 2024 they rejected a motorway extension.

abschnitte.text: On 10 May **1962** the **Grauholz motorway** between the Wankdorf in Bern and Schönbühl was opened. It is regarded as the first section of national road **N1**, today's A1. In the following decades more and more sections were added. Today the motorways connect almost all the larger cities in the country.

The **A13** connects Ticino with the Rhine Valley and runs through the **San Bernardino Road Tunnel**. On the A2 lies the **Seelisberg Tunnel**. It is about 9 kilometres long and connects Beckenried in the canton of Nidwalden with Seedorf in the canton of Uri. The tunnel runs inside the mountain along **Lake Uri**. Before that you had to drive there on narrow shore roads.

The **motorway vignette** was introduced in **1985**. The money is used to build and maintain the national roads. Since August **2023** you can also buy it online as an **e-vignette**. It is then linked to the vehicle's number plate. The sticker vignette still exists.

On **motorways** the maximum speed is 120. There are also **expressways**: they are only for motor vehicles, but usually have no separate carriageways. There the maximum speed is **100**. In a traffic jam everyone must form an **emergency lane**, which has been compulsory since 2021. Cars in the left lane move to the left, and all the others to the right.

In **2017** the people accepted the **NAF**, the fund for national roads and agglomeration transport. From this unlimited fund the Confederation pays for operation, maintenance and extension. On 24 November **2024**, about 53 per cent of voters said no to extending several motorway sections. Supporters wanted to reduce traffic jams, while opponents feared more traffic and use of land.

gewusst: The emergency lane helps ambulances, the fire brigade and the police to reach the scene of an accident quickly, even in the densest traffic jam.
The San Bernardino Road Tunnel was opened in 1967 and was then one of the longest road tunnels in the world.

teile.einleitung: Lake Neuchâtel lies at the foot of the Jura in western Switzerland. It is the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland, and borders four cantons.
wichtigste: Lake Neuchâtel is about 218 square kilometres in size.
It is about 38 kilometres long and up to 8 kilometres wide.
It borders the cantons of Neuchâtel, Vaud, Fribourg and Bern.
On the north shore lies the city of Neuchâtel, and behind it the Jura rises.
The Thielle flows in the Thielle Canal into Lake Biel.
On the south shore lies the large nature reserve Grande Cariçaie.

abschnitte.text: Lake Neuchâtel has an area of about **218 square kilometres**. It is about **38 kilometres** long and up to 8 kilometres wide. This makes it the largest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland. It borders **four cantons**: Neuchâtel, Vaud, Fribourg and Bern. Around the lake, mainly French is spoken.

On the **north shore** lies the city of **Neuchâtel**, which gives the lake its name. Behind it rise the hills and mountains of the **Jura**. At the south west end lies **Yverdon-les-Bains**. On the **south shore**, in the canton of Fribourg, lies the little town of **Estavayer-le-Lac**. “Le Lac” means “the lake” in English.

The **Areuse** comes from the Val de Travers in the Jura and is one of the most important inflows. At Yverdon the **Orbe** flows in, which is called the Thielle there. The outflow of the lake is the **Thielle** (Zihl in German). It flows in the **Thielle Canal** into Lake Biel. Lake Neuchâtel is one of the three lakes of the **Three Lakes Region**, together with Lake Biel and Lake Murten.

Thousands of years ago, people already lived on the shore of Lake Neuchâtel. They built their houses on **piles** by the water. Archaeologists found many remains of these **pile dwellings**, for example wooden piles and tools. Some of the sites belong to the **UNESCO World Heritage** of prehistoric pile dwellings around the Alps.

In the 19th century, the lake level was lowered during the **Jura Water Correction**. On the flat south shore, wide strips of shore were left dry as a result. There the **Grande Cariçaie** formed, a long area of reeds, wet meadows and riverside woodland. Today it is an important **nature reserve**. Many birds find food and shelter here.

gewusst: The Grande Cariçaie is regarded as the largest lakeshore wetland in Switzerland.
The Jura Water Correction lowered the lakes of the Three Lakes Region by several metres and so protected the Seeland from flooding.

teile.einleitung: National roads are the most important roads in Switzerland. They include above all the motorways, which connect cities and parts of the country. They belong to the Confederation.
wichtigste: In 1960 parliament passed the law on national roads.
Since 2008 the national roads have belonged entirely to the Confederation.
Since 1996 motorways have been marked on signs with an A, such as A1 or A2.
Since 1985 the speed limit on motorways has been 120.
Vehicles up to 3.5 tonnes need a vignette, and heavy vehicles pay the LSVA.
In 2020 about 400 kilometres of cantonal roads were added to the national road network.

abschnitte.text: In June **1960** parliament passed the **National Roads Act**. It laid down which roads are important for the whole of Switzerland. After that the motorways were built over many decades. In the past the cantons were more responsible. With the reform of fiscal equalisation (**NFA**), the Confederation took over ownership, operation and maintenance in **2008**.

Since **1996**, signs carry numbers with an **A**, for example A1 or A2. Before that people spoke of N1 or N2. The **A2** runs from Basel via Lucerne and the Gotthard to Chiasso on the Italian border. It is the most important north south route on the road. With the new network decision, the Confederation took over about 400 kilometres of former cantonal roads in **2020**.

Anyone driving on the motorway in a car, motorcycle or light van up to **3.5 tonnes** needs a **vignette**. It costs 40 francs a year (as of 2025). On 24 November **2013** the people rejected an increase to 100 francs. Heavy vehicles instead pay the **LSVA**, the heavy vehicle charge based on performance.

Since **1985** the maximum speed on motorways has been **120 km/h**, whereas before it was 130 km/h. At the same time a limit of 80 km/h was introduced outside built up areas. For heavy lorries there is a **night driving ban** from 22:00 to 05:00 and a **Sunday driving ban**. There are exceptions, for example for perishable goods.

The **Federal Roads Office (FEDRO)** is responsible for the national roads. Its **traffic management centre** in Emmenbrücke in the canton of Lucerne monitors traffic across the whole country. From there, for example, signals and ramp metering at entrances are controlled. This is meant to keep traffic flowing better in the event of congestion or accidents.

gewusst: For decades the vignette was stuck onto the windscreen, and today it is also available electronically.
The night driving ban for heavy lorries has existed in Switzerland for decades.

teile.einleitung: The Rigi is a well-known viewing mountain in Central Switzerland, almost completely surrounded by lakes. Since 1871 a rack railway has run up it, the first mountain railway in Europe.
wichtigste: The Rigi is often called the “Queen of the Mountains”.
The highest point is called Rigi Kulm and is just under 1,800 metres high.
The Rigi belongs to the cantons of Lucerne and Schwyz, and the summit lies in the canton of Schwyz.
Since 1871 the Vitznau-Rigi Railway has run up it.
Since 1875 the Arth-Rigi Railway has also run from Arth-Goldau.
Around the Rigi lie Lake Lucerne, Lake Zug and Lake Lauerz.

abschnitte.text: The Rigi bears the fine nickname **“Queen of the Mountains”**. In the past people believed that its name came from the Latin word for queen. Language research sees it differently today: in Swiss German, “Rigi” meant **horizontal bands of rock**, that is, layers that run across the mountain. You can see such bands clearly on the Rigi.

The highest point is called **Rigi Kulm** and is just under 1,800 metres high. Part of the mountain belongs to the canton of **Lucerne**, another to the canton of **Schwyz**, where the summit also lies. The Rigi is almost completely surrounded by lakes: in the south **Lake Lucerne**, in the north **Lake Zug** and in the east **Lake Lauerz**. From the top you have a wide view over lakes, the Central Plateau and the Alps.

abschnitte.titel: The first mountain railway in Europe
abschnitte.text: Since **1871** the **Vitznau-Rigi Railway** has run from Vitznau on the lakeshore to Rigi Kulm. It was the first mountain railway in Europe. Because the mountain is so steep, it needs a **rack**: a cogwheel under the locomotive engages in a toothed rail between the tracks. This stops the train from slipping.

Since **1875** the **Arth-Rigi Railway** has also run from Arth-Goldau up the Rigi. So you can get up by train from two sides. From **1907** the Arth-Rigi Railway ran **electrically**, the first standard gauge rack railway in the world to do so. Today there are also cable cars, for example from Weggis to Rigi Kaltbad.

As early as the 19th century, many travellers from abroad came to the Rigi. It was especially popular to experience the **sunrise** on the summit. For this, guests stayed overnight in hotels on Rigi Kulm. To this day the Rigi is a popular place for outings for walking, tobogganing and enjoying the view.

gewusst: Because the Rigi is almost completely surrounded by lakes, from a distance it looks almost like an island.
The Arth-Rigi Railway was the first standard gauge rack railway in the world to run on electricity.

teile.einleitung: Around Basel, Switzerland, Germany and France meet. In the Trinational Eurodistrict Basel, municipalities and regions from all three countries work together so that life across the borders becomes easier.
wichtigste: The Trinational Eurodistrict Basel covers areas of Switzerland, Germany and France.
It was founded in 2007.
Legally it is an association under French law.
About 60 per cent of the population live in Switzerland, 30 in Germany and 10 in France.
From 1963, the Regio Basiliensis promoted cooperation.
It initiated the International Building Exhibition IBA Basel 2020.
Since 2014 tram line 8 has run as far as Weil am Rhein.

abschnitte.text: Many people in the Basel region live in one country and work in another. So that this works well, the **Trinational Eurodistrict Basel** was founded in **2007**. It covers areas in **Switzerland**, in **Germany** and in **France**. Legally it is an **association under French law**.

From Switzerland, the cantons of **Basel-Stadt** and **Basel-Landschaft** take part. In addition there is the canton of **Solothurn** with the districts of **Dorneck** and **Thierstein**. Municipalities from southern Baden and Alsace also take part. Of the population, about **60 per cent** live in Switzerland, **30 per cent** in Germany and **10 per cent** in France.

Cooperation across borders is nothing new in Basel. From **1963**, the **Regio Basiliensis** worked to get people on the **Upper Rhine** to look for solutions together. The Eurodistrict builds on this. For example, it initiated the International Building Exhibition **IBA Basel 2020**, which promoted cross border building projects.

How closely the region is linked is shown by transport. Since **2014** the Basel tram line **8** has run across the border to **Weil am Rhein** in Germany. The **Badischer Bahnhof** lies on Basel city territory but belongs to **Deutsche Bahn**. The airport of the region lies on French soil and is run jointly by France and Switzerland.

gewusst: At the Badischer Bahnhof in Basel, you can board a Deutsche Bahn train on Swiss soil.
EuroAirport Basel-Mulhouse-Freiburg is one of the few airports in the world run jointly by two countries.

teile.einleitung: The Rhine is one of the most important rivers in Europe and flows from the Swiss Alps to the North Sea. It links Switzerland with Germany, France and the Netherlands. With the Rhine Falls near Schaffhausen, it has one of the most famous waterfalls in Europe.
wichtigste: The Rhine is about 1,230 kilometres long.
It rises in the Grisons in the area around the Gotthard and the Oberalp.
It flows through Lake Constance and afterwards often forms the border with Germany.
At Schaffhausen it plunges over the Rhine Falls.
In Basel, ships are loaded that sail as far as the North Sea.
The Rhine flows into the North Sea in the Netherlands.

abschnitte.text: The **Vorderrhein** rises near the Oberalp Pass, the Hinterrhein in the area of the Rheinwaldhorn. At Reichenau in the Grisons the two join. As the Alpine Rhine it then flows past Liechtenstein into **Lake Constance**. After that it flows as the High Rhine to Basel, turns north and reaches the Netherlands via Germany.

The **Rhine Falls** lie at Neuhausen am Rheinfall near Schaffhausen. The water plunges about 23 metres over a rock step about 150 metres wide. In summer, several hundred cubic metres of water often thunder down every second. You can go by boat as far as a rock in the middle of the waterfall.

**Basel** joined the Confederation in 1501 and is the Swiss city on the Rhine par excellence. In the Rhine ports, containers, oil and grain are transferred. Via the Rhine, Switzerland is linked to the sea although it has no coast. Downstream, big cities such as Strasbourg, Mainz, Cologne and Rotterdam lie on the Rhine.

In the time of Julius Caesar, the Rhine formed the northern border of the territory of the **Helvetii**, who in the 1st century BC lived mainly on the Central Plateau between the Jura and the Alps. Later it was for a long time the border of the Roman Empire. In the Middle Ages, knights built many castles on its banks, especially in the Middle Rhine valley. There also lies the famous rock Loreley.

In the past, many **salmon** swam up the Rhine from the North Sea every year as far as Switzerland. Because of power plants, river works and pollution, the salmon has died out in Switzerland. Today people try to open the way back for it with fish ladders and **renaturation**. The eel could also migrate up the Rhine into Swiss rivers and lakes, where it used to be more common.

Although the Rhine rises in Switzerland, it does not flow only through Switzerland. The longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland is the **Aare**, which joins the Rhine at Koblenz AG. In the Gotthard area the Rhine, Rhône, Reuss and Ticino rise. In summer in Basel, many people let themselves drift in the Rhine with a waterproof bag.

begriffe.erklaerung: The place where a river emerges from the ground or from a lake.
A place where water plunges down over a rock step.
A stepped channel that lets fish bypass a power plant.
Making a straightened river more natural again.
A port in Basel where river ships are loaded and unloaded.

gewusst: Six countries lie on the Rhine: Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Austria, Germany, France and the Netherlands.
In 1986 a fire at a chemical firm in Schweizerhalle near Basel turned the Rhine red and killed many fish.
The Rhine Falls are regarded as the waterfall with the greatest volume of water in Europe.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland is a country of hydropower. Rivers, glaciers and reservoirs supply most of its domestic electricity. There are different types of power plant and rules to protect waters.
wichtigste: In 2024, about 60 per cent of the country's production came from hydropower.
In 2024 Switzerland produced about 80 terawatt hours of electricity.
Valais produces the most electricity from hydropower.
Run-of-river power plants supply electricity continuously but can hardly store any.
Storage power plants keep meltwater from the summer for the winter.
Operators pay a water rent for using the water.
The Water Protection Act requires enough residual flow in streams.

abschnitte.titel: The most important source of electricity
abschnitte.text: According to the Federal Office of Energy, Switzerland's **domestic production** in 2024 was about **80 terawatt hours**. Of this, about **60 per cent** came from hydropower. Because 2024 was a wet year, Switzerland exported a net of about 14 TWh more electricity than it imported. **Valais**, with its high mountains and reservoirs such as the **Lac des Dix**, supplies the most hydropower electricity, about 28 per cent of Swiss production.

**Run-of-river power plants** stand on rivers such as the **Rhine** and the **Aare**. They use the water that happens to be flowing past and supply steady **baseload energy**. They can hardly store anything. **Storage power plants** in the Alps collect the meltwater from snow and glaciers in summer. In **winter**, when a lot of electricity is needed and little water flows in, it is released through the turbines as required.

Each power plant needs a different **turbine**. For very large drops in the Alps, the **Pelton turbine** is often used. There a fast jet of water hits cup-shaped blades. On rivers with a small drop and a lot of water, the **Kaplan turbine** works. It looks like a ship's propeller with adjustable blades.

Anyone who uses the force of a body of water pays the **water rent** for it. The money goes to the **cantons** and often also to the **municipalities**. For many mountain cantons such as Valais, the Grisons or Uri, this is an important source of income. The Confederation sets the maximum amount the water rent may be.

Hydropower changes waters. Below a water intake, a minimum amount of water must remain under the **Water Protection Act**, the **residual flow**. Another problem is **“surge and sink”**: when a storage power plant runs its turbines, the flow in the river suddenly rises and then falls again. This harms fish and tiny creatures. That is why the law requires remedial work.

gewusst: A reservoir in the Alps keeps the meltwater of summer for the cold season.
The Pelton turbine is named after the American Lester Pelton, who invented it.

teile.einleitung: Lake Maggiore is a long, deep lake at the southern foot of the Alps, lying partly in Switzerland and partly in Italy. The Swiss part belongs to the canton of Ticino. On its shore lies the lowest point in the whole of Switzerland, and thanks to the mild climate, palms and camellias grow here.
wichtigste: Lake Maggiore lies partly in Switzerland and partly in Italy.
The Swiss part lies in the canton of Ticino; the larger part belongs to Italy.
On the shore near Ascona, at about 193 metres above sea level, lies the lowest point in Switzerland.
The River Ticino flows into the lake and out again at the southern end.
Its water reaches the Adriatic Sea by way of the Ticino and the Po.
The Ticino city of Locarno lies at the northern end of the lake.
The lake is about 65 kilometres long and up to about 370 metres deep.

abschnitte.text: Lake Maggiore extends for about 65 kilometres from north to south. It has an area of about 212 square kilometres and is about 370 metres deep at its deepest point. Only about a fifth of its area lies in Switzerland, in the **canton of Ticino**. The rest belongs to the Italian regions of Piedmont and Lombardy.

The most important inflows are the **Ticino** and the Maggia, which flow in at Locarno and Ascona. At the southern end at Sesto Calende, the Ticino leaves the lake again and flows to the Po, which joins the Adriatic. The lake level lies at about 193 metres above sea level. The shore near Ascona is therefore the **lowest point in Switzerland**.

The Alps in the north protect the lake from cold winds, and the large body of water stores warmth. So there is a mild, almost Mediterranean climate with many hours of sunshine. In the gardens grow palms, camellias, magnolias and citrus trees. On the **Brissago Islands** there is a botanical garden with plants from many parts of the world.

At the northern end lies the town of **Locarno**, which holds the famous film festival on the Piazza Grande every summer. Right next to it lies Ascona with its pretty lakeside promenade. On the Italian side lie places such as Stresa, Verbania and Luino. Off Stresa lie the **Borromean Islands**, including Isola Bella with a magnificent palace and terraced garden.

Passenger boats run on the lake, on which you can travel from Locarno to Italy. In summer, beaches, sailing boats and bathing spots attract many visitors from all over Switzerland. From Locarno a funicular leads up to the pilgrimage church of **Madonna del Sasso**, from where you can see far over the lake. The Romans called the lake Verbanus, which is where its second name Verbano comes from.

begriffe.erklaerung: The southernmost canton of Switzerland, where Italian is spoken.
A garden in which many different plants are shown and studied.
The place where a river flows into a lake, a sea or another river.
A climate with warm, sunny summers and mild winters.

gewusst: The highest point of Switzerland, the Dufourspitze, and the lowest point on Lake Maggiore are over 4,400 metres apart in height.
“Maggiore” means “larger” in Italian, but the lake is only the second-largest lake in Italy after Lake Garda.
The Brissago Islands are the lowest-lying islands in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Upper Valais is the eastern, German speaking part of the canton of the Valais. It stretches from the Rhône Glacier to the area around Leuk and Sierre and is surrounded by high mountains.
wichtigste: In the Upper Valais people speak German, in the Lower Valais French.
The Rhône rises in the Goms at the Rhône Glacier near Gletsch.
Zermatt belongs to the district of Visp.
The Simplon Pass connects Brig with Domodossola in Italy.
The Pfynwald is regarded as one of the largest pine forests in the Alps.
In the past the upper Valais was divided into seven Zenden.

abschnitte.text: The canton of the **Valais** is bilingual. In the **Upper Valais** people speak German, more precisely the dialect **Valais German**. In the **Lower Valais** they speak French. Important places in the Upper Valais are **Brig**, **Visp** and **Naters**. The districts are called, for example, Goms, Brig, Visp, Raron and Leuk.

Right in the east lies the **Goms**. There the **Rhône** rises from the Rhône Glacier near Gletsch. In the south lies the Vispertal with its side valleys. At the very end of the Mattertal lies **Zermatt** with the Matterhorn. It belongs to the **district of Visp**. The great **Aletsch Glacier** also lies in the Upper Valais.

The **Simplon Pass** leads at 2,005 metres from Brig to **Domodossola** in Italy. The pass road was built under **Napoleon**. Under the mountain, the Simplon railway tunnel passes through. In this way the Upper Valais is an important link between north and south.

Between **Leuk** and **Sierre** lies the **Pfynwald**. It is regarded as one of the largest **pine forests** in the Alps. Here runs roughly the **language border** between the Upper and Lower Valais. In this area the Rhône is still allowed to flow quite freely. Today the area belongs to the Pfyn-Finges Nature Park.

In the early modern period the upper Valais was divided into **seven Zenden**. These were Goms, Brig, Visp, Raron, Leuk, Sierre and Sion. Together they formed the **Republic of the Seven Zenden**, the centre of power of the old Valais. The Lower Valais was ruled by them at that time. Only in 1815 did the Valais become a canton of Switzerland.

gewusst: The Aletsch Glacier is the longest glacier in the Alps.
Under Napoleon, the Valais was part of France for a few years.

teile.einleitung: The Second Homes Initiative wanted to limit the building of holiday homes in Switzerland. The people and the cantons narrowly approved it in March 2012. Since then, a ceiling of 20 per cent second homes has applied in municipalities.
wichtigste: The people and the cantons approved the initiative on 11 March 2012.
It now stands as Article 75b in the Federal Constitution.
Municipalities may have at most 20 per cent second homes.
The best-known initiator was the environmentalist Franz Weber.
The Second Homes Act has applied since 1 January 2016.
Mountain areas such as the Grisons and Valais were particularly affected.

abschnitte.text: The popular initiative was called **“Stop the endless building of second homes!”**. It was launched by the environmentalist **Franz Weber** and his foundation **Helvetia Nostra**. On **11 March 2012**, the people and the cantons narrowly approved it. Since then it has stood as **Article 75b** of the **Federal Constitution**. Franz Weber campaigned for decades for the protection of the landscape.

A **second home** is a home in which nobody lives permanently, such as a holiday flat. Municipalities with more than **20 per cent** second homes may in principle not approve any new ones. What counts is the municipality's **housing inventory**. The **Second Homes Act** came into force on **1 January 2016**. Before that, a transitional ordinance of the Federal Council applied.

**Cold beds** are holiday homes that are used only a few weeks a year and otherwise stand empty. They use up land and infrastructure but bring in little money. The law therefore allows new **tourist-managed** homes that are rented out permanently to holiday guests. This is meant to create more **“warm beds”**.

Homes that existed or were approved before **11 March 2012** count as **old-law homes**. They may still be used freely, including as second homes. **Mountain areas** such as the **Grisons** and **Valais** were particularly affected. In many tourist municipalities the share was well over 20 per cent. There, the building of new holiday homes fell sharply.

gewusst: The initiative was approved with only a good 50 per cent Yes, so very narrowly.
In some mountain villages, more than half of all homes were second homes.

teile.einleitung: The Zytglogge is a famous tower in the old town of Bern. It has an old astronomical clock and a figure show that draws many spectators before every full hour. The tower is over 800 years old.
wichtigste: “Zytglogge” means “time bell” in standard German.
The tower was built around 1218 to 1220.
At first it was a defensive tower to protect the city.
The figure show begins about 4 minutes before the full hour.
A cockerel crows, a jester rings bells and bears walk in a circle.
The god of time, Chronos, turns over an hourglass.
A golden knight strikes the hour with a hammer.

abschnitte.text: The Zytglogge was built around **1218 to 1220** and is therefore over **800 years** old. At first it was a **defensive tower** on the western edge of the young city of **Bern**. As the city grew, the tower soon stood in the middle of the town. Only later did it get a **clock**. Today it belongs to the old town of Bern, which is a UNESCO World Heritage site.

“Zyt” means time in **Bernese German**, and “Glogge” means bell. **Zytglogge** therefore means **time bell**. The big bell in the tower shows the time with its strokes. The tower also has an **astronomical clock**. It shows not only the hour but also the signs of the zodiac and the position of the moon.

About **four minutes** before the full hour, the **figure show** begins to move. First a wooden **cockerel** crows. A **jester** in a fool's cap rings two small bells above his head. Then little **bear figures** walk past in a circle, carrying weapons and musical instruments. Many tourists are already waiting in front of the tower beforehand.

In the middle sits **Chronos**, the bearded **god of time**. He turns over an **hourglass** and counts the strokes of the bell. At the very top of the tower stands a gilded **knight** called **Hans von Thann**. He strikes the big bell with a **hammer** and so announces the full hour.

gewusst: The bear figures recall Bern's heraldic animal.
The Zytglogge tower once also served as a prison.

teile.einleitung: The Swiss franc is the money of Switzerland. One franc has 100 centimes, and people pay with coins and colourful banknotes.
wichtigste: The abbreviation of the Swiss franc is CHF.
One franc has 100 centimes.
The smallest coin is the five centime piece.
The big five franc coin is called the “Fünfliber”.
The largest banknote is the thousand franc note.
In Liechtenstein, too, people pay with Swiss francs.

abschnitte.text: The **Swiss franc** has existed as the common money of the whole of Switzerland since **1850**. Before that, many cantons had their own money. The abbreviation is **CHF**. CH stands for **Confoederatio Helvetica**, the Latin name of Switzerland, and F for franc. One franc is divided into **100 centimes**, called Rappen in German.

There are coins of 5, 10 and 20 centimes as well as of half a franc, one, two and five francs. The smallest coin is the **five centime piece**. The one centime piece has no longer been legal tender since **2007**. The largest coin is the five franc coin, popularly called the **“Fünfliber”**. The coins are made by **Swissmint** in Bern.

There are banknotes of 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 1,000 francs. Each note has its own **colour**, so that you can tell them apart easily. The ten franc note is **yellow**, the twenty is red, the fifty is green and the hundred is blue. The largest note is the **thousand franc note**, and there is no five hundred franc note. The notes are issued by the **Swiss National Bank**.

**Liechtenstein** has no currency of its own. There, too, people pay with Swiss francs. The two countries have concluded a treaty for this. In the neighbouring countries Germany, France, Italy and Austria, by contrast, people pay with the **euro**.

gewusst: The Swiss banknotes are designed in portrait format, so you hold them upright to look at them properly.
On many Swiss coins it does not say “Schweiz” but “Helvetia” or “Confoederatio Helvetica”.

teile.einleitung: The Penninic is one of the great rock units of the Alps. Its rocks tell of an ancient ocean that once lay between Europe and the Adriatic Plate.
wichtigste: The name comes from the Pennine Alps in the Valais.
Many Penninic rocks come from the Tethys, an ancient ocean.
Ophiolites are remains of oceanic crust and mantle.
Bündnerschiefer are finely layered deep sea sediments from the Penninic.
The Briançonnais was a continental ridge between two ocean basins.
In the Lower Engadine Window, Penninic rocks emerge from under Eastern Alpine nappes.

abschnitte.text: The Penninic is named after the **Pennine Alps**, that is, the Valais Alps. Their Latin name was **Mons Poeninus**. Some people used to think the name came from the general Hannibal, but that is regarded as wrong. In geology, Penninic refers to a group of **nappes**. These are huge packages of rock that were pushed over one another when the Alps were formed.

A large part of the Penninic rocks comes from the **Tethys**. This was an ocean between Europe and the Adriatic Plate. It included the **Piedmont-Ligurian Ocean**. Between them lay a continental ridge, the **Briançonnais**. It separated the Valais Trough in the north from the Piedmont Ocean in the south. As the continents approached, the ocean was squeezed together.

**Ophiolites** are remains of oceanic crust and mantle. They consist of rocks such as serpentinite, gabbro and basalt. They prove that an ocean once lay here. The **Bündnerschiefer** (Grisons schists) are grey, finely layered rocks of lime and clay. They were deposited in the deep sea and are widespread in the **Grisons**, hence the name.

In Ticino the Penninic was strongly uplifted. This is called the **Lepontine gneiss region** or the Lepontine Dome. There the deepest Penninic **gneiss nappes** come to the surface, such as the Maggia or the Leventina nappe. Gneiss is a rock that was transformed under great heat and high pressure.

Sometimes Penninic rocks lie like islands on younger layers. The **Mythen** near Schwyz belong to such a **klippe nappe**. It lies on Helvetic rocks and flysch. In the **Lower Engadine** there is the opposite, a **tectonic window**. There the Inn has cut through the Eastern Alpine nappes lying above, so that the Penninic rocks beneath become visible. The window reaches as far as Prutz in Tyrol.

gewusst: Rocks from an ancient ocean can now be found high up in the Alps.
The Mythen are older than the rocks they lie on, because they were pushed over them from far away.

teile.einleitung: The residual flow is the water that must remain in a stream or river when part of it is diverted, for example for a hydroelectric power station. This is meant to protect fish, plants and landscape.
wichtigste: Residual flows are regulated in the Water Protection Act (GSchG).
The law dates from 24 January 1991 and was accepted by the people on 17 May 1992.
The deciding figure is the flow rate Q347, a typical low water flow.
Article 31 GSchG sets how much water must at least remain.
Water that is deliberately released to comply is called compensation water.
Below storage power stations, hydropeaking often occurs.

abschnitte.text: In Switzerland a lot of electricity is produced with **hydropower**. For this, water is taken from streams and rivers and led through pipes to the turbines. Without rules, stream beds could almost dry up. The **Water Protection Act** of 24 January 1991 therefore regulates in Articles 29 to 36 how much water must remain. A referendum was called against the law, and on 17 May 1992 the people accepted it.

The basis is the flow rate **Q347**. This is the quantity of water, averaged over ten years, that is reached or exceeded on an average of 347 days a year. So only on about 18 days a year does even less water flow. Q347 therefore describes a typical **low water flow** and is given in litres per second (l/s).

**Article 31** sets a sliding scale. Up to Q347 = 60 l/s, a minimum of 50 l/s applies, and for every further 10 l/s, 8 l/s are added. A stream with 100 l/s therefore needs 50 plus 4 times 8, which is **82 l/s**. At 160 l/s, 130 l/s applies, and for every further 10 l/s, 4.4 l/s are added. At 500 l/s, 280 l/s applies, and for every further 100 l/s, 31 l/s are added: a river with 1,000 l/s needs 280 plus 5 times 31, which is **435 l/s**. From 60,000 l/s, a fixed value of **10,000 l/s** applies.

The calculated amount is only the minimum. The law requires **more residual flow** if otherwise, for example, water quality, the feeding of groundwater or rare habitats are not secured. More water must also flow if the necessary water depth for free **fish migration** is lacking. If the water over a weir is not enough, **compensation water** is also released. It can even produce electricity in small compensation turbines.

Another problem arises below **storage power stations**. They produce electricity above all when a lot is needed. Then the flow in the river rises quickly, which is called **surge**. After that it falls rapidly again, which is the **drop**. Fish and small animals can be stranded on the bank as a result.

gewusst: For very large rivers the legal minimum no longer rises any further, and stays at 10,000 litres per second.
A power station operator's economic reasons do not count when it comes to increasing the residual flow to protect nature.

teile.einleitung: The UNESCO Entlebuch Biosphere lies in the canton of Lucerne between Bern and Lucerne. It was the first biosphere reserve in Switzerland under the new UNESCO rules and is especially known for its moorland landscapes.
wichtigste: Entlebuch was the first biosphere reserve in Switzerland under UNESCO's Seville Strategy.
Typical of the biosphere are its moorland landscapes.
Since 2008 it has also carried the label “Regional Nature Park”.
Seven whole municipalities belong to the biosphere.
The people living there decided on its founding in votes.
The Rothenthurm Initiative gave the impetus for the idea.
The Schrattenfluh, with its karst fields, lies in the biosphere.

abschnitte.text: A **biosphere reserve** is an area where nature is protected and people still live and work. For this, UNESCO set new rules in the **Seville Strategy**. **Entlebuch** was the first area in Switzerland to be recognised under this concept. Since **2008** it has also carried the national label **Regional Nature Park**.

Especially typical of Entlebuch are its **moorland landscapes**. Moors are very wet soils in which dead plants decay only slowly. This produces **peat**. Rare plants and animals live in moors, for example the sundew, which catches small insects. Moors also store a lot of water and carbon.

The idea of a biosphere arose after the **Rothenthurm Initiative**. With it, the Swiss people wrote the protection of moors into the Federal Constitution in 1987. Because there are many moors in Entlebuch, people looked for a way to combine protection and the economy. The people living there decided on the founding of the biosphere in **votes** in the municipalities. Today **seven whole municipalities** belong to it.

A well-known mountain in the biosphere is the **Schrattenfluh**. It is made of limestone. Over a long time, rainwater has dissolved the limestone and formed deep grooves and cracks. Surfaces like this are called **karst fields**. Beneath the mountain there are also many caves.

gewusst: In Entlebuch, regional products are sold with their own biosphere label.
A biosphere reserve is not a place without people, but shows how people and nature can live well together.

teile.einleitung: The Toggenburg is a valley region in the canton of St Gallen through which the Thur flows. The area is known for its mountains, its folk music and old customs.
wichtigste: The Toggenburg is shaped by the Thur.
Wattwil is regarded as the main town of the Toggenburg.
Wildhaus and Unterwasser are well known holiday resorts in the upper Toggenburg.
The reformer Ulrich Zwingli was born in the Toggenburg in 1484.
Of the usually seven Churfirsten, the Chäserrugg can be reached by lift.
The Halszither belongs to the folk music.
The Toggenburg goat is named after the area.

abschnitte.text: The **Toggenburg** lies in the canton of **St Gallen**. Right through the valley flows the **Thur**. **Wattwil** is regarded as the main town. In the upper Toggenburg lie the holiday resorts of **Wildhaus** and **Unterwasser**. In winter you ski there, in summer you walk over Alpine pastures.

In the south of the Toggenburg rise the **Churfirsten**. Usually **seven** peaks are counted. On the side towards Lake Walen they fall away as steep rock walls, on the Toggenburg side they are gentler. A lift runs up to the **Chäserrugg** from the Toggenburg. In the north you can see the Säntis.

In the Toggenburg, **folk music** has a long tradition. A typical instrument is the **Halszither**, a stringed instrument with a long neck. On the **Klangweg** (sound trail) between Alt St Johann, Unterwasser and Wildhaus, instruments stand by the wayside. There you can **try out sounds and tones**, for example on bells or xylophones.

An old tradition is **farmer painting**. In it, furniture, cupboards or pictures are painted with Alpine processions, cows and flowers. Also named after the area is the **Toggenburg goat**, a goat breed with brown fur and white stripes on the head. Today it is kept in many countries.

In **Wildhaus**, **Ulrich Zwingli** was born in **1484**. He later became a pastor in Zurich and was one of the most important **reformers** of Switzerland. The Reformation was a movement that wanted to renew the church. You can still visit his birthplace in Wildhaus today.

gewusst: The restaurant on the Chäserrugg was designed by the well known Basel architects Herzog & de Meuron.
The Toggenburg goat is among the goat breeds that are spread worldwide.

teile.einleitung: The Rhône is a large river that rises at the Rhône Glacier in the canton of Valais and flows to the Mediterranean. On the way it crosses Lake Geneva and then flows through France. It is one reason why Switzerland is called the “water tower of Europe”.
wichtigste: The Rhône is about 810 kilometres long.
It rises at the Rhône Glacier in the canton of Valais.
It flows through the whole of Valais and then into Lake Geneva.
In Geneva it leaves Lake Geneva again.
In France it flows through Lyon and joins the Mediterranean at the Camargue.
Switzerland is called the “water tower of Europe” because many great rivers rise here.

abschnitte.text: The Rhône begins at the **Rhône Glacier** near the Furka Pass, not far from the Gotthard area. It flows through the long main valley of Valais past Brig, Sion and Martigny. At Le Bouveret it flows into **Lake Geneva** and leaves it again in Geneva. After that it travels through France south to the Mediterranean.

The Rhône is the great river of Valais; in Upper Valais it is also called the “Rotten”. Glacier streams from the side valleys bring a lot of water and rock. Because it used to burst its banks often, it was straightened and embanked in the 19th century. With the third **Rhône Correction**, it has for some years been given more room again and more safety from floods.

In the 1st century BC, the **Helvetii** lived mainly on the Swiss Central Plateau between the Jura and the Alps. In 58 BC they wanted to emigrate and first to cross the Rhône at Geneva. Julius Caesar had the bridge destroyed and stopped them. In Roman times Geneva was called **Genava**.

In Lyon the Saône flows into the Rhône and makes it richer in water still. On the way south it passes Avignon with its famous half bridge. Many power plants, including nuclear power plants, use its water. Before the Mediterranean it forms the delta of the **Camargue** with flamingos, white horses and rice fields.

With many hydropower plants, the Rhône supplies electricity for Switzerland and France. It irrigates fields and vineyards in Valais and in the Rhône valley. In Geneva it is so clean that you can swim in it in summer. Because the Rhône Glacier is melting, its water level will change in the future.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large mass of ice in the mountains that moves slowly.
An area where many great rivers rise.
Rebuilding a river so that it causes fewer floods.
A mouth area in which a river divides into many arms.

gewusst: At the Rhône Glacier, in summer you can walk through an ice grotto that is dug anew every year.
In Lake Geneva the mud of the Rhône settles, which is why it flows out blue and clear in Geneva.
In Geneva the clear Rhône meets the grey Arve, and for a long way you can see the two colours flowing side by side.

teile.einleitung: The Pre-Alps lie between the Central Plateau and the High Alps. Their mountains are lower than the great Alpine peaks, and there are usually no big glaciers there. Many well-known mountains for day trips belong to them.
wichtigste: The Pre-Alps lie between the Central Plateau and the Alps.
There are usually no big glaciers there.
The Rigi is called the “Queen of the Mountains”.
From 1871 the Rigi Railway ran as the first mountain railway in Europe.
Pilatus, Moléson and Säntis are well-known Pre-Alpine mountains.
In summer, farmers drive their cows up to the alp and mow the grass for hay.

abschnitte.titel: Between the Central Plateau and the Alps
abschnitte.text: The **Pre-Alps** form the transition between the flat **Central Plateau** and the high **Alps**. Their mountains are mostly between 1,000 and a good 2,000 metres high. Because they are not so high, there are usually **no big glaciers** there. Instead you find green pastures, forests and rocky peaks.

Between **Lake Lucerne** and **Lake Zug** lies the **Rigi**. It is called the **“Queen of the Mountains”**. From **1871**, the **Rigi Railway** ran up to a summit as the **first mountain railway in Europe**. It is a cog railway. From the top you can see over many lakes and, on clear days, as far as the High Alps.

On Lake Lucerne rises **Pilatus**, a well-known peak of the central Swiss Pre-Alps. In the **Gruyère region** in the canton of Fribourg rises the **Moléson**. In eastern Switzerland lies the **Alpstein** with the **Säntis**. At about 2,500 metres, it is the highest peak of the eastern Swiss Pre-Alps.

In the Pre-Alps, **alpine farming** is important. In summer, farmers drive their **cows up to the alp**, where they eat fresh grass. Cheese is often made there too. On the steep slopes, farmers **mow** the grass and dry it into **hay**. That way the animals have enough fodder in winter.

gewusst: The steepest cog railway in the world runs up Pilatus.
Gruyère cheese is named after the Gruyère region at the foot of the Moléson.

teile.einleitung: The snow line is the height above which snow stays on the ground. It is important for understanding where glaciers form and how the climate is changing.
wichtigste: Above the snow line there is snow, and below it the ground is free of snow.
Above the climatic snow line, the snow does not melt completely even in summer.
Only above the climatic snow line can glaciers form.
On a glacier, the equilibrium line corresponds to it roughly.
In the dry inner Alps it lies higher than at the edge of the Alps.
If the climate gets warmer, the snow line rises.

abschnitte.text: The **snow line** is the height above which snow stays on the ground. Below it the ground is free of snow. In winter it lies low, and in summer it rises high into the mountains. The **climatic snow line** is the height above which snow stays even in summer. There, more snow falls in a year than melts.

Snow that has lasted at least one summer becomes granular and dense. It is called **firn**. If it is pressed together further, **glacier ice** is formed from it. That is why **glaciers** can only form above the climatic snow line. There lies their **accumulation area**, from where the ice flows down the valley into the **ablation area**, where it melts.

On a glacier there is a line at which growth and melting balance each other. This is the **equilibrium line**. There exactly as much melts in a year as is added in snow. It corresponds roughly to the snow line at the end of summer. Above it the glacier grows, and below it it loses ice.

The snow line does not lie at the same height everywhere. In the **inner Alps**, for example in the **Valais**, it is drier and sunnier than at the rainy **northern edge of the Alps**. Because less snow falls, the snow line lies higher there. Sunny slopes are also free of snow earlier than shady slopes.

If the climate becomes **warmer**, snow melts even at greater heights. That is why the snow line rises, and the glaciers lack a supply. The snow line should not be confused with the **snowfall line** in the weather report. That is the height above which precipitation falls as snow. Below it, it rains, and it is given in metres above sea level.

gewusst: At the end of a summer you can see on many glaciers where the bright snow stops and the darker ice begins.
The snowfall line in the weather report can rise or fall by several hundred metres in a day.

teile.einleitung: At about 288 kilometres, the Aare is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland. It rises in the Bernese Alps, flows through several lakes and towns such as Bern and Solothurn, and finally joins the Rhine. In summer, swimming in the Aare in Bern is a popular experience.
wichtigste: The Aare is the longest river that flows entirely within Switzerland.
It rises at the Aare glaciers in the Grimsel area.
It flows through Lake Brienz, Lake Thun and Lake Biel.
In a big loop it flows around the old town of the capital, Bern.
The Aare also flows right through Solothurn.
At Brugg, the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet.
The Aare joins the Rhine at Koblenz in Aargau.

abschnitte.text: The **Aare** rises at the Aare glaciers in the Grimsel area in the Bernese Alps. At Meiringen it flows through the narrow **Aare Gorge**. After that it crosses Lake Brienz and Lake Thun. Since the Jura Water Correction in the 19th century, it has also been led through Lake Biel.

In a big **loop**, the Aare flows around the old town of Bern. The old town is a UNESCO World Heritage site. On the bank lies the Bear Park, because the bear is Bern's heraldic animal. In summer many people let themselves drift through the city in the green water.

The Aare flows right through **Solothurn**, which was called Salodurum in Roman times. On the bank of the Aare there stands the beautiful old **Landhaus**. After that it flows on through Olten, Aarau and Brugg. Along the Aare there are also several hydropower plants and two nuclear power plants.

At Brugg, the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet. This spot is called the **Water Castle of Switzerland**. Nearby, at Windisch, lay the Roman legionary camp **Vindonissa**. A little later the Aare joins the Rhine at Koblenz in Aargau.

The Celts already settled on the Aare. On the **Engehalbinsel**, in a loop of the river near Bern, there was a Helvetian oppidum, that is, a fortified town. The Romans built roads and camps on the Aare. Later many towns were founded on the Aare, because the river made transport and trade possible.

The Aare is a habitat for many animals. Mallards, swans and grey herons are often seen. In the water live fish such as the **grayling** and the brown trout. On natural banks the beaver is also returning today.

begriffe.erklaerung: The place where a river flows into another river, a lake or the sea.
A large building project in which rivers and lakes in the Seeland were redirected to prevent flooding.
A fortified town of the Celts.
The place near Brugg where the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet.

gewusst: When the Aare joins the Rhine, it usually carries more water than the Rhine itself.
The green water of the Aare in Bern comes from fine rock flour from the glaciers.

teile.einleitung: The UNESCO World Heritage Site Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch is a huge high mountain landscape in the Bernese Oberland and the Upper Valais. At its centre lies the Great Aletsch Glacier, the largest glacier in the Alps.
wichtigste: The area was inscribed in 2001 as the first natural World Heritage Site in the Alps.
At first it was called Jungfrau-Aletsch-Bietschhorn.
In 2007 it was extended to about 824 square kilometres.
It lies in the cantons of Bern and the Valais.
The highest mountain is the Finsteraarhorn at 4,274 metres.
The Aletsch Forest has been a nature reserve since 1933.

abschnitte.text: **UNESCO** inscribes areas whose nature is unique for the whole of humanity. In **2001** the area was inscribed as **Jungfrau-Aletsch-Bietschhorn**. It was the **first natural World Heritage Site** in the whole Alpine region. With this, Switzerland commits itself to protecting and preserving this landscape.

In **2007** the area was enlarged from about 540 to about **824 square kilometres**. In the west, areas as far as the **Blüemlisalp** above Kandersteg were added. Since then it has been called **Swiss Alps Jungfrau-Aletsch**. The World Heritage Site lies in the **Bernese Oberland** and the **Upper Valais**, so it is spread over the cantons of Bern and the Valais. It is much larger than the Swiss National Park.

The highest summit is the **Finsteraarhorn** at 4,274 metres, also the highest mountain of the Bernese Alps. The **Eiger, Mönch and Jungfrau** are also well known. On the Valais side flows the **Great Aletsch Glacier**, the largest glacier in the Alps. It is about 20 kilometres long. Because it is getting warmer, more ice melts in summer than is added in winter, so it has been getting shorter for decades.

Above the glacier grows the **Aletsch Forest** with old Swiss stone pines and larches. It was placed under protection as early as **1933**, with about 400 hectares. On the Riederfurka stands the **Villa Cassel**, built by the English banker Ernest Cassel. Since 1976 it has housed the **Pro Natura Centre Aletsch**, where you can learn a great deal about nature and glaciers.

gewusst: The Aletsch Forest had already been protected for almost 70 years before the area became a World Heritage Site.
Some of the Swiss stone pines in the Aletsch Forest are several hundred years old.

teile.einleitung: Samnaun is a municipality in a remote side valley of the Lower Engadine in the Grisons. It is a customs free area, so you can buy many goods there duty free.
wichtigste: Samnaun has been a customs free area since 1892.
The reason was that for a long time there was no road over Swiss territory.
The Samnaun road from Vinadi opened in 1912.
Today people in Samnaun speak a Tyrolean dialect.
Until the 19th century they spoke Romansh.
With Ischgl in Austria, Samnaun forms the Silvretta Arena ski area.

abschnitte.text: In the past, Samnaun could only be reached easily via **Tyrol** in Austria. Goods therefore came into the valley with duty paid and were expensive. After applications from the municipality, the Confederation granted Samnaun **customs exemption** in **1892**. At first it applied only until a road was built over Swiss territory, but it was later extended. To this day Samnaun is a **customs free area**, and many visitors come to shop.

Since **1912** the **Samnaun road** has run from Vinadi in the Lower Engadine to Samnaun. It is narrow, winding and not entirely safe in winter. The road runs through a narrow gorge with tunnels and galleries. In addition there is a connection over Austrian territory.

Until the 19th century people in Samnaun spoke **Romansh**, namely the idiom **Vallader**, as in the Lower Engadine. Because the valley was closely tied to Tyrol, the population gradually switched to **German**. Today they speak a southern Bavarian **Tyrolean**. Samnaun is thus the only Swiss municipality in the Bavarian dialect area.

Together with **Ischgl** in the Austrian Paznaun, Samnaun forms the large ski area **Silvretta Arena**. The pistes run across the national border. In Samnaun the world's first **double decker aerial cableway** was built. Each cabin of this reversible cableway has two floors, so many more people fit in.

gewusst: Many guests come to Samnaun to buy goods such as perfume or watches duty free.
People in Samnaun do speak German, but a dialect that you otherwise only hear in Tyrol and Bavaria.

teile.einleitung: Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden are called the original cantons. They are regarded as the origin of the Swiss Confederation, and many well-known legends are woven around them, such as that of William Tell.
wichtigste: In the Middle Ages, Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden were also called the Forest Cantons.
According to legend, the pact was sworn on the Rütli meadow on Lake Uri.
1 August commemorates the Federal Charter of early August 1291.
According to legend, Tell shot the bailiff Gessler in the Hohle Gasse near Küssnacht.
Friedrich Schiller wrote the play “William Tell” in 1804.
In 1806 a huge rockslide buried the village of Goldau.
In the Muota valley, the “weather sniffers” predict the weather.

abschnitte.text: The three **original cantons** are **Uri**, **Schwyz** and **Unterwalden**. Today Unterwalden is divided into two cantons, **Obwalden** and **Nidwalden**. In the Middle Ages the three places were also called the **Forest Cantons**. **Lake Lucerne** takes its German name from this. All three lie on it, together with Lucerne.

abschnitte.titel: The Federal Charter and the Rütli
abschnitte.text: In early August **1291**, the valley communities made a pact and set it down in the **Federal Charter**. In it they promised to help one another. According to legend, the pact was sworn on the **Rütli meadow** on **Lake Uri**. The **national holiday on 1 August** commemorates this. Today you can see the Federal Charter in a museum in Schwyz.

The best-known legend tells of **William Tell**. He is said to have shot an apple from his son's head. Later he is said to have killed the **bailiff Gessler** in the **Hohle Gasse** near **Küssnacht**. Nobody knows whether Tell really existed. The story became famous through the play **“William Tell”**, which **Friedrich Schiller** wrote in **1804**.

In **1806**, an enormous mass of rock broke loose on the Rossberg. The **rockslide** buried the village of **Goldau** in the canton of Schwyz and further hamlets. Many people lost their lives. You can still see the huge boulders in the landscape today, for example in the Goldau Nature and Animal Park.

In the **Muota valley** in the canton of Schwyz there are the **“weather sniffers”**. These are weather prophets who predict the **weather** without any measuring instruments. To do so, they observe animals, plants, clouds and other signs in nature. Twice a year they present their forecasts in public, which many people follow with delight.

gewusst: The canton of Schwyz later gave its name to the whole of Switzerland.
Every year on 1 August, celebrations take place on the Rütli.

t1sqr1dx.t: New Rail Link through the Alps

teile.einleitung: The New Rail Link through the Alps, NEAT for short, is one of the greatest building projects in Swiss history. With long base tunnels it takes the railway flat under the Alps.
wichtigste: The NEAT consists mainly of the Lötschberg axis and the Gotthard axis.
The Gotthard axis connects Zurich with Milan.
The Ceneri Base Tunnel is about 15 kilometres long and lies between Bellinzona and Lugano.
The whole NEAT cost about 23 billion francs.
In 1998 the people accepted the FinöV proposal on financing.
Part of the heavy vehicle charge LSVA flowed into the FinöV fund.

abschnitte.text: In the past, trains had to climb steeply up to tunnels high in the mountains. The NEAT, by contrast, builds **base tunnels** deep down in the mountain. This keeps the route almost flat, and trains can run faster and carry heavier loads. The aim was also to move more **goods from road to rail**. That spares the Alpine valleys noise and exhaust fumes.

The **Gotthard axis** is the main axis. It runs from **Zurich** through the Gotthard and the Ceneri to **Milan**. The **Lötschberg axis** runs from Bern through the Lötschberg into the Valais. From there it goes through the **Simplon Tunnel** to Domodossola in Italy. The Gotthard Base Tunnel is about 57 kilometres long, and the Ceneri Base Tunnel about **15 kilometres**.

Many lorries are carried through the Alps on railway wagons. Tall **semi trailers** need enough room for this in tunnels and under bridges. By 2020 the Gotthard axis was adapted from Basel to Ticino. Since then semi trailers with a **corner height of 4 metres** fit through. This route is called the **4 metre corridor**.

In 2017 the final cost of the NEAT was estimated at about **22.6 billion francs**. In **1998** the people accepted the **FinöV** proposal, on financing public transport. The FinöV fund was fed mainly from the **LSVA**, a share of one per mille of VAT and money from the mineral oil tax. In this way lorries help pay for the railway. It was built by **AlpTransit Gotthard AG**, a subsidiary of the SBB.

The NEAT also includes the approach routes. The first part of the **Zimmerberg Base Tunnel** between Zurich and Thalwil has been in operation since 2004. A second stage towards Zug was meant to connect eastern Switzerland better. It was put on hold and is to be built later. After the large tunnels were completed, the **SBB** took over operation.

gewusst: At about 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world.
The Ceneri Base Tunnel was opened in 2020 and completed the flat railway through the Alps.

teile.einleitung: The Verzasca valley is a wild valley in the canton of Ticino. It is famous for the crystal-clear, green water of the Verzasca, for old stone houses and for a huge dam at the entrance to the valley.
wichtigste: The water of the Verzasca is very clear and green.
At the entrance to the valley stands a dam about 220 metres high.
Behind it lies Lago di Vogorno.
You can bungee jump from the dam.
At Lavertezzo stands the stone bridge Ponte dei Salti with two arches.
At the very back of the valley lies the village of Sonogno.
The little stone village of Corippo used to be the smallest municipality in Switzerland.

abschnitte.text: The **Verzasca** is famous for its **very clear and green** water. You can see right down to the bottom, where smoothly polished rocks lie in many colours. But the water is cold even in summer. **Swimming** is also dangerous: after thunderstorms, or when water is released from the reservoir, the river can **rise suddenly and sharply**.

At the **entrance** to the valley stands a **high dam**. It is about **220 metres** high. Behind it lies the reservoir **Lago di Vogorno**. The water is used to generate electricity. From the dam, the brave can do a **bungee jump** and leap down into the depths on a rope. The jump became well known through a James Bond film.

At **Lavertezzo**, an old **stone bridge** crosses the river. It is called the **Ponte dei Salti** and has **two arches**. The bridge is one of the best-known photo spots in Ticino. All around are big rocks where many visitors sunbathe on warm days.

In the valley there are many old **stone houses**, which in Ticino are called **rustici**. At the very back of the valley lies the village of **Sonogno**. The little stone village of **Corippo** clings to the slope. It used to be the **smallest municipality in Switzerland**, until it merged with other villages to form the municipality of Verzasca.

gewusst: In the 1995 James Bond film “GoldenEye”, a stuntman jumps from the Verzasca dam.
As a municipality, Corippo finally had only about a dozen residents.

teile.einleitung: The Elbe is one of the great rivers of central Europe. It rises in the Giant Mountains in the Czech Republic, flows right across Germany and joins the North Sea at Cuxhaven. On it lie cities such as Dresden, Magdeburg and the big port city of Hamburg.
wichtigste: The Elbe is about 1,100 kilometres long.
It rises in the Giant Mountains in the Czech Republic, where it is called the Labe.
Hamburg is the largest port city on the Elbe.
The rocky landscape of Saxon Switzerland lies on the Elbe.
On 25 April 1945, American and Soviet troops met at Torgau on the Elbe.
The Elbe flows into the North Sea at Cuxhaven.

abschnitte.text: The **Elbe** rises in the **Giant Mountains** in the Czech Republic, where in Czech it is called the Labe. At Mělník it takes in the Vltava, which flows through Prague. Then it flows into Germany and through Dresden, Magdeburg and Hamburg. At Cuxhaven it joins the North Sea after about 1,100 kilometres.

South-east of Dresden, the Elbe has cut deep into sandstone. This created **Saxon Switzerland** with its table mountains, rock needles and gorges. It was given its name in the 18th century by two Swiss painters who worked in Dresden and for whom the landscape recalled their homeland. Well known is the rock formation Bastei with a stone bridge.

The big port city of **Hamburg** lies on the Elbe, about 100 kilometres before the mouth. Large container ships sail up the Elbe into the port. The Port of Hamburg is one of the largest ports in Europe. Right on the bank stands the **Elbphilharmonie**, a famous concert hall.

In Roman times the Romans wanted to extend their empire as far as the Elbe. After the **Battle of the Teutoburg Forest** in the year 9 AD, in which they lost three legions to Germanic tribes, they gave up this plan. On 25 April 1945, American and Soviet troops met on the Elbe at Torgau, which is known as **Elbe Day**. Later a section of the Elbe formed the border between West and East Germany.

Large parts of the banks of the Elbe have remained natural, with floodplain forests and meadows. Beavers, storks and many waterbirds live there. In summer 2002 there was an enormous **flood** that hit Dresden and many other places hard. Since then, protective measures have been greatly expanded.

begriffe.erklaerung: The place where a river flows into the sea or into another river.
Rock made of pressed-together grains of sand.
Flat land beside a river that is flooded when the water is high.
A large unit of the Roman army with several thousand soldiers.

gewusst: Saxon Switzerland got its name from two Swiss painters, Adrian Zingg and Anton Graff.
The flood of 2002 reached a level of over 9 metres in Dresden.

teile.einleitung: In the Upper Engadine in the Grisons, a chain of lakes lies one after another in the valley. They are called the Upper Engadine Lakes. They lie at about 1,800 metres and are among the best-known landscapes in the Alps.
wichtigste: The lakes include Lake Sils, Lake Silvaplana, Lake Champfèr and Lake St Moritz.
The Inn flows from lake to lake down the valley.
Lake Champfèr lies between Lake Silvaplana and Lake St Moritz.
In summer the Maloja wind often blows in the afternoon.
Lake Silvaplana is popular with kite surfers and windsurfers.

abschnitte.text: From the **Maloja Pass** the lakes lie one after another in the broad valley: first **Lake Sils**, then **Lake Silvaplana**, the small **Lake Champfèr** and finally **Lake St Moritz**. The **Inn** connects them and flows from lake to lake. Lake Champfèr is closely linked with Lake Silvaplana. High mountains rise all around.

On many summer days the **Maloja wind** blows in the afternoon. It blows from the Maloja Pass down the valley. This is unusual, because valley winds usually blow **up the valley** during the day. The wind is strong and very regular.

Because of the regular wind, **Lake Silvaplana** is a well-known spot for **kite surfers** and **windsurfers**. The water is very cold, however, so they wear wetsuits. In winter the lakes often freeze over. On Lake St Moritz there are then even horse races on the ice.

gewusst: The Inn flows from the Engadine to the Danube, and its water thus reaches the Black Sea.
Lake Sils is the largest of the Upper Engadine lakes.

teile.einleitung: Space is becoming scarce in Switzerland, because houses and roads are spreading onto meadows and fields. With inward densification, more living space is meant to be created without building on new land.
wichtigste: Inward settlement development means growing within the existing building zones.
A typical example is adding extra storeys to an existing building.
Industrial wasteland means former factory sites that can be put to new use.
The utilisation ratio determines how much floor area may be built.
The IVHB is meant to standardise building terms across the cantons.
There is often a conflict of aims between more living space and green areas.
The Prime Tower of 2011 shapes the densified Zurich West district.

abschnitte.text: **Inward settlement development** means that villages and towns grow **within the existing building zones**. So people no longer build on the “green field” at the edge of town. This leaves more land for farming and nature. Switzerland's **Spatial Planning Act** has required this kind of development since its revision, which the people approved in 2013.

There are many ways to fit more people onto the same area. One example is **adding storeys**: an existing house gets an extra floor. You can also build on gaps between houses. **Industrial wasteland** is especially important. This means **former factory sites** where new homes, offices and schools can be built.

The **utilisation ratio** says how much floor area is allowed on a plot. If a plot measures **800 m²** and the ratio is **0.6**, you may build **480 m²** of countable floor area. The **user density** counts residents and employees per hectare. 1,200 residents and 600 employees on 20 ha give **90 per hectare**. So that such terms mean the same everywhere, there is the **IVHB**, an agreement between the cantons.

Densification has advantages, but also disadvantages. A **conflict of aims** often arises: **more living space** is set against **preserving green and open spaces**. When building becomes denser, good parks, squares and playgrounds are needed. The neighbours also often have questions, for example about the view or the traffic. That is why such projects are often discussed.

A well-known example of densification is the **Zurich West** district. It used to have many factories. Today there are homes, offices, universities and culture. The district is shaped by the **Prime Tower**, a high-rise that was completed in **2011**. At the time it was among the tallest buildings in Switzerland.

gewusst: A hectare is an area of 100 by 100 metres, so a little bigger than a football pitch.
Many old factory halls are not pulled down but converted into flats, studios or theatres.

teile.einleitung: The Rhaetian Railway, RhB for short, is the great railway of the canton of the Grisons. With its narrow tracks it runs over spectacular viaducts and through many tunnels, high up into the mountains.
wichtigste: The Rhaetian Railway has its headquarters in Chur.
Its network is about 385 kilometres long.
It is one of the largest narrow gauge railways in Europe.
The name comes from the Roman province of Raetia.
The Vereina Tunnel has connected the Prättigau with the Lower Engadine since 1999.
In October 2022 the longest passenger train in the world ran on the Albula line.

abschnitte.text: The Rhaetian Railway has its seat in **Chur**, the capital of the Grisons. Its network measures about **385 kilometres**. The tracks are narrower than on most railways, which is called **narrow gauge**. This lets the railway take tighter bends, which is very useful in the mountains. The RhB is among the largest narrow gauge railways in Europe.

The RhB grew out of the **Landquart-Davos narrow gauge railway**, which was founded in 1888. A few years later it was given the name Rhaetian Railway. The name comes from the **Roman province of Raetia**. In Roman times the area of today's Grisons belonged to this province.

The **Albula line** runs from Thusis to St Moritz. It was built at the beginning of the 20th century and overcomes large differences in height with spiral tunnels and viaducts. Famous is the **Landwasser Viaduct** near Filisur. It is about 65 metres high, 136 metres long and was completed in 1902. Its trains run straight into a tunnel in the rock face.

The **Vereina Tunnel** is about 19 kilometres long and was opened in 1999. It connects the **Prättigau** with the **Lower Engadine** and shortens the journey greatly. There is no road in the tunnel. Cars are loaded onto railway wagons at Klosters-Selfranga and travel through the mountain by train. This is called the **car shuttle**.

In **October 2022** the RhB set a world record. A train made up of 25 multiple units, about **1.9 kilometres** long, ran over the Albula line as far as Alvaneu. It was the **longest passenger train in the world**. Many people watched along the line.

gewusst: The Albula line and the Bernina line of the RhB have been UNESCO World Heritage since 2008.
On the Landwasser Viaduct the trains run straight out of the air into a tunnel in the rock face.

teile.einleitung: A reservoir comes into being when a wall or a dam holds back a river. In Switzerland there are many reservoirs, above all in the Alps. They store water in order to produce electricity with it.
wichtigste: Reservoirs store water for hydroelectric power stations.
A pumped storage power station pumps water up into an upper lake and lets it flow down again when needed.
An arch dam passes the water pressure sideways into the rock walls.
The Mauvoisin dam is about 250 metres high.
The Lago di Lei lies mostly in Italy, but the dam stands on Swiss soil.
Lake Mattmark is held back by an earth dam.
