Tiny crustaceans clean the water by eating algae. Because the lake is so old and remote, many species are **endemic**, that is, found only here.

In 1996, Lake Baikal was declared a **World Heritage** site by UNESCO. In the past a large paper mill on the south shore polluted the water; it was closed in 2013. Today sewage, tourism and climate change threaten the lake. Many people in Russia regard it as a national treasure.

begriffe.erklaerung: Water with very little salt, as in rivers and most lakes.
A long depression where the Earth's crust is drifting apart.
An animal species or plant that is found in only a single place.
A particularly valuable place that UNESCO protects worldwide.

gewusst: If you were to channel all the rivers of the Earth into the empty Lake Baikal, they would need almost a year to fill it.
How the Baikal seals once came into the lake, which is far from the sea, has still not been fully explained.
Lake Baikal has a large island called Olkhon, where about 1,500 people live.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland has very many lakes, from huge lakes in the Mittelland to small mountain lakes. It shares some with neighbouring countries. Lakes are important for drinking water, leisure, fishing and shipping.
wichtigste: Lake Geneva is the largest lake with a Swiss shore, and about 60 per cent of its area belongs to Switzerland.
Lake Constance is the second largest lake with a Swiss shore.
Lake Neuchâtel is the largest lake lying entirely in Switzerland.
Lake Maggiore is up to about 372 metres deep.
Lake Thun is the largest lake lying entirely in the canton of Bern.
The Lac de Joux is the largest lake in the Jura.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Geneva** is the largest lake with a Swiss shore. Of its roughly 580 square kilometres, about 345 lie in Switzerland, and the rest belongs to **France**. It holds about 89 cubic kilometres of water, more than any other lake in Switzerland. **Lake Constance**, together with the Untersee, is the second largest lake with a Swiss shore, but only a part of it belongs to Switzerland. The largest lake entirely in Switzerland is **Lake Neuchâtel**.

The deepest lake with a Swiss share is **Lake Maggiore**. It is up to about 372 metres deep. Its deepest point lies in the Italian part, far below sea level. **Lake Thun** lies entirely in the canton of Bern and is larger than Lake Brienz. Lake Biel is smaller and also borders the canton of Neuchâtel.

On **Lake Sempach** in the canton of Lucerne the **Battle of Sempach** took place in 1386. The lake is about 14 square kilometres in size. Many lakes in Switzerland were formed after the last **ice age**. The glaciers had scooped out deep basins, which later filled with water. Other lakes are **reservoirs**, built by people.

The **Lac de Joux** lies in the Vallée de Joux in the canton of Vaud at about 1,000 metres above sea level. It is about 9 kilometres long and is regarded as the largest lake in the Jura mountains. On the **Doubs** lies the **Lac des Brenets**, which forms the border between Switzerland and France. It was formed by a rockslide that dammed the river. At its end the water plunges into the depths at the **Saut du Doubs**.

gewusst: The deepest point of Lake Maggiore lies below sea level, although the lake is in the mountains.
In French, Lake Geneva is called “Lac Léman”.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland has to store its radioactive waste from nuclear power stations, medicine, industry and research safely. In 2022 Nagra proposed the Nördlich Lägern area in the canton of Zurich for this. There a deep geological repository is to be built far down in the rock.
wichtigste: Nagra chose Nördlich Lägern in 2022 because the rock there has the best barrier effect.
The repository is to be built in Opalinus Clay, about 175 million years old.
A depth of about 800 metres is planned.
The surface facility is planned in Stadel (ZH).
High level as well as low and intermediate level waste is to be stored.
The people can vote on the general licence by an optional referendum.
According to the plan (as of 2024), storage is to begin around 2050.

abschnitte.text: **Nagra**, the National Cooperative for the Disposal of Radioactive Waste, searched for a suitable site for many years. In the last stage three areas were still in the procedure: **Jura Ost**, **Zürich Nordost** and **Nördlich Lägern**. In **2022** Nagra proposed Nördlich Lägern. As the main reason it named the **best geological barrier effect**. The rock there is meant to shield the waste best.

The repository is to be built in **Opalinus Clay**. This rock is about **175 million years** old. It is very **dense**, so that hardly any water flows through it. In addition, the clay can **seal** fine **cracks itself**, because it swells slightly on contact with water. A depth of about **800 metres** is planned.

On the surface, a facility is planned in the municipality of **Stadel** in the canton of Zurich. From there, access routes lead into the depths. The spent fuel elements are to be packed into special containers at the **interim store in Würenlingen** in Aargau. **High level** as well as **low and intermediate level** waste is to be stored. High level waste radiates especially strongly.

Nagra submits an application for a **general licence**. First the **Federal Council** and then **Parliament** decide on it. After that an **optional referendum** can be called. If enough signatures are collected, the people vote on it. There are people who support the project and those who have concerns.

It will be a long time until the repository is finished. According to Nagra's plan (as of 2024), **storage is to begin around 2050**. The waste has to stay safely enclosed for a very long time, because its radiation decreases only slowly. That is why planning covers a period of many thousands of years.

gewusst: Opalinus Clay is named after an ammonite, a fossil that is common in it.
Until the repository is ready, the waste is kept in interim stores on the surface.

teile.einleitung: Zermatt is a famous holiday resort in the canton of Valais, right below the Matterhorn. The village is car-free, and visitors arrive by train. Mountain railways lead from here high up into the eternal ice.
wichtigste: Zermatt lies at the very back of the Mattertal in the canton of Valais.
A railway has run from Visp to Zermatt since 1891.
Petrol and diesel cars are not allowed in the village.
Most visitors park in Täsch and take the shuttle train.
In 1865 Edward Whymper and his rope team were the first to reach the summit of the Matterhorn.
The Gornergrat Railway is a cog railway and has run since 1898.
The Glacier Express links Zermatt with St Moritz.

abschnitte.text: Zermatt lies at the very back of the **Mattertal**, which joins the Rhône valley at **Visp**. It belongs to the canton of **Valais**. Around the village stand many four-thousanders, above all the **Matterhorn**. The **Matter Vispa** is formed from the meltwater of the glaciers around Zermatt. At **Stalden** it joins the Saaser Vispa to form the Vispa.

Zermatt is **car-free**: ordinary cars with combustion engines may not enter the village. For visitors the road ends at **Täsch**. There most people park their car and take the **shuttle train** of the Matterhorn Gotthard Railway to Zermatt in a few minutes. The railway line from Visp to Zermatt has existed since **1891**. In the village only small **electric vehicles** run.

abschnitte.titel: The first ascent of the Matterhorn
abschnitte.text: In **1865**, the Englishman **Edward Whymper** and six companions were the first to reach the summit of the Matterhorn. On the descent, four of them were killed in an accident. The event made the Matterhorn and Zermatt famous all over the world. Soon more and more **mountaineers** and holidaymakers came to the village.

The **Gornergrat Railway** has been in operation since **1898**. With a **cogwheel** it overcomes the steep line up to over 3,000 metres. It goes even higher with the cable car up the **Klein Matterhorn**. The top station **Matterhorn Glacier Paradise** lies at **3,883 metres**. It is the highest cable car station in Europe.

The **Glacier Express** links Zermatt with **St Moritz** in the Engadine. It takes about **eight hours** for the journey. It crosses many bridges and runs through tunnels and over the Oberalp Pass. Because it travels so leisurely, it is often called the **“slowest express train in the world”**.

gewusst: The cable car station on the Klein Matterhorn lies at 3,883 metres above sea level.
The Glacier Express calls itself the slowest express train in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Abbey Library of St Gallen is one of the oldest libraries in the world. It belongs to the abbey district, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In its splendid Baroque hall stand books that are over a thousand years old.
wichtigste: The Abbey Library owns very old manuscripts from the Middle Ages.
In the Middle Ages, monks copied the books by hand.
Visitors wear felt slippers in the Baroque hall.
The abbey district has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1983.
In the library lies the mummy Shepenese from Egypt.

abschnitte.text: The **Abbey Library** belonged to the monastery of St Gallen. In the Middle Ages there were no printing presses yet. The **monks** therefore copied the books carefully by hand. They wrote on **parchment**, which was made from animal skin, and often decorated the pages with colourful pictures. In this way precious **manuscripts** came into being, many of which have survived to this day.

The heart of the library is the splendid **Baroque hall** with its wood carvings and ceiling paintings. It was built in the 18th century. Anyone who visits it pulls **felt slippers** over their shoes. This way the valuable **wooden floor** is not scratched when walking. Above the entrance stands a Greek word that means “pharmacy of the soul”.

The **abbey district** with its cathedral and library was inscribed as **UNESCO World Heritage** in 1983. It is regarded as especially valuable for the whole of humanity. An unusual treasure is the **mummy** of a woman named **Shepenese** from Egypt. She is over 2,600 years old. Many visitors are amazed that a mummy lies in a library.

gewusst: In the Abbey Library lies the Plan of St Gall, one of the oldest surviving architectural drawings of the Middle Ages.
Many manuscripts of the library can also be viewed on the internet today.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland, vines grow on many sunny slopes. The largest wine-growing areas are in Valais and Vaud. Especially famous are the steep terraces of Lavaux on Lake Geneva.
wichtigste: Valais is the largest wine-growing canton in Switzerland.
Lavaux lies between Lausanne and Vevey on Lake Geneva.
Since 2007, the terraces of Lavaux have been a UNESCO World Heritage site.
Monks laid out the first terraces in the Middle Ages.
Fendant is a Valais white wine made from the Chasselas grape.
In Visperterminen, vines grow at over 1,000 metres.
Suonen bring glacier water to the Valais vineyards.

abschnitte.text: Vines need plenty of **sun** and warmth. In Switzerland they grow mainly in **Valais**, **Vaud**, **Geneva**, **Ticino** and around the Jura lakes. There are also vineyards in German-speaking Switzerland, for example on Lake Zurich or in the Klettgau. Each region has its typical **grape varieties**. In Ticino, for example, Merlot is especially common.

**Lavaux** stretches between **Lausanne** and **Vevey** along the north shore of **Lake Geneva**. The vineyards descend in steep **terraces** to the lake, supported by stone walls. In the **12th century**, **Cistercian monks** began to reshape the slopes in this way. Since **2007**, Lavaux has been a **UNESCO World Heritage** site.

In Lavaux people speak of the **“three suns”**. The vines receive direct **sunlight**. There is also the light reflected from the **lake**. The third sun is the warmth of the **stone walls**, which store heat during the day and give it back in the evening. This helps the grapes ripen especially well.

**Valais** is the largest wine-growing canton in Switzerland. The best-known white wine is called **Fendant**, which is what they call **Chasselas** there. **Dôle** is a red wine made mainly from **Pinot Noir** and a little **Gamay**. In **Visperterminen**, vines grow up to about 1,100 metres above sea level. The white wine **Heida** is made there.

Valais is very dry, because the high mountains keep the rain away. That is why people built **suonen** centuries ago, called **“bisses”** in French. These are narrow channels that carry **glacier water** to meadows and vineyards. Many suonen run along steep rock faces. Today they are also popular walking trails.

gewusst: The vineyards of Visperterminen are among the highest in Europe.
In Lavaux, the stone walls warm the vines like a small heater.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland, rain and snow do not fall in equal amounts everywhere. Mountains, valleys and the direction of the moist air determine where it is wet and where it is dry.
wichtigste: The driest measuring site in Switzerland is Ackersand in the Vispertal in the Valais.
There only about 550 millimetres fall per year on average.
The inner Valais lies in the rain shadow of high mountains.
On the Central Plateau about 1,000 to 1,500 millimetres fall per year.
The Alps, Central Switzerland and Ticino receive about 2,000 millimetres and more.
Precipitation mostly increases with height.
1 millimetre of precipitation is equal to 1 litre per square metre.

abschnitte.text: Precipitation is rain, snow or hail. It is measured in **millimetres**. **1 millimetre** means that **1 litre** of water has fallen on one square metre. If 1,200 millimetres fall in a year, that is 1,200 litres per square metre. On a roof of 150 square metres, **180,000 litres** then fall.

abschnitte.titel: A lot of rain at the mountains
abschnitte.text: When moist air meets mountains, it is lifted upwards. As it does so it cools, and the water vapour turns into drops. That is why precipitation mostly increases with **height**. Especially large amounts fall in the **Alps**, in **Central Switzerland** and in **Ticino**, with about 2,000 millimetres a year. The **Central Plateau** receives middling amounts, about 1,000 to 1,500 millimetres.

The measuring site **Ackersand** in the Vispertal is regarded as the driest place in Switzerland. There only about **543 millimetres** fall per year on average, measured for the years 1991 to 2020. The inner Valais lies in the **rain shadow**: the moist air rains itself out over the Bernese and Valais Alps. In the valley the air sinks, warms up and becomes dry. That is why vines and plants that like dry conditions grow there.

In **summer**, about twice as much precipitation generally falls in Switzerland as in winter. Then **thunderstorms** and showers bring a lot of rain. Warm air can also hold more water vapour than cold air. In winter, precipitation in the mountains mostly falls as **snow**. It stays on the ground and only flows away as meltwater in spring.

In Switzerland, measurements have been made regularly since **1864**. The measurement series show that precipitation on the Central Plateau has **increased** since then. The increase concerns mainly the **winter**. Such long measurement series help us understand the climate and its changes better.

gewusst: In the dry Valais, long water channels called Suonen were built in the past to water meadows and fields.
Ackersand receives less than half of the precipitation that falls on the Central Plateau.

teile.einleitung: The Rhine Falls is a large waterfall on the Rhine near Schaffhausen. It is one of the most powerful waterfalls in Europe and one of the best-known sights in Switzerland.
wichtigste: The Rhine Falls is about 23 metres high and about 150 metres wide.
It is one of the largest waterfalls in Europe.
At the Rhine Falls the cantons of Schaffhausen and Zurich meet.
On the Schaffhausen side lies Neuhausen am Rheinfall.
Above the waterfall stands Laufen Castle on the Zurich bank.
It came about after the last Ice Age.

abschnitte.text: At the Rhine Falls the **Rhine** plunges over rocks into the depths. The water falls about **23 metres**, which is about as high as a house with seven storeys. The waterfall is about **150 metres** wide, so longer than a football pitch. It is not very high, but because of the large amount of water it is one of the **most powerful waterfalls in Europe**.

At the waterfall the Rhine forms the **cantonal border**. The right bank belongs to **Schaffhausen**, where the municipality of **Neuhausen am Rheinfall** lies. It even has the waterfall in its name. The left bank belongs to the canton of **Zurich**, to the municipality of Laufen-Uhwiesen.

On a rock on the Zurich bank stands **Laufen Castle**. From there paths and platforms lead right up close to the roaring water. In the middle of the waterfall a large **rock** rises up. Small **boats** take visitors there, and then you can climb up a staircase.

Directly above the Rhine Falls a **railway bridge** crosses the Rhine. It was built as early as 1855 and 1856. Today trains run on it between Schaffhausen and Winterthur. From the bridge you look down from above onto the foaming water.

The Rhine Falls came about roughly **14,000 to 17,000 years ago**. After the last **Ice Age**, glaciers had changed the landscape. The Rhine had to find a new bed. In doing so it flowed over a step of hard limestone, which is only slowly worn away. That is why the waterfall still exists today.

gewusst: The rock in the middle of the Rhine Falls has stood for thousands of years, although the water keeps hitting it.
In summer, noticeably more water usually flows over the Rhine Falls than in winter.

teile.einleitung: The Ticino flows from the Nufenen Pass through the canton of Ticino into Lake Maggiore and from there on through Italy as far as the Po. Along its course there are power stations, gorges and many traces of history.
wichtigste: The Ticino joins the Po near Pavia.
Its catchment area is about 7,200 square kilometres in size.
In the Leventina it flows through the Piottino Gorge.
The Ritom power station supplies mainly power for the SBB railway.
In 218 BC Hannibal defeated a Roman army on the Ticino.
The Golasecca culture is named after a find site on the river.
In Pavia the Ponte Coperto crosses the river.

abschnitte.titel: From the Nufenen to the Po
abschnitte.text: The Ticino begins at the **Nufenen Pass** and flows through the canton of Ticino into **Lake Maggiore**. Into the same lake also flows the **Toce** from the Italian **Ossola valley**. At the south end the Ticino leaves the lake and flows through the Po plain. Near the town of **Pavia** it joins the **Po**, the longest river in Italy. Its **catchment area**, that is, the whole area from which its water comes, is about **7,200 km²** in size.

In the **Leventina** the Ticino flows between Rodi-Fiesso and Faido through the narrow **Piottino Gorge**. In the past this spot was very hard for travellers to get past. In the upper valley at Piotta stands the **Ritom power station**. Its power is used mainly for the **SBB railway operation**, for example for the trains on the Gotthard.

South of Lake Maggiore lies the place **Golasecca**. After finds there, a pre-Roman culture was named, the **Golasecca culture**. In **218 BC** the general **Hannibal** crossed the Alps from Carthage into Italy. On the Ticino he defeated a **Roman army**. This is called the Battle of the Ticinus.

In **Pavia** a famous **roofed bridge** leads over the Ticino. It is called the **Ponte Coperto**, which means “covered bridge”. The old bridge was badly damaged in the Second World War and then rebuilt. Today it is a landmark of the town.

gewusst: Power from Ticino flows as railway power into many parts of the SBB network.
On his march over the Alps, Hannibal even brought war elephants.

teile.einleitung: At about 650 kilometres, the Po is the longest river in Italy. It flows from the Western Alps right across northern Italy to the Adriatic. Water from Switzerland also reaches the Po by way of the Ticino.
wichtigste: The Po is the longest river in Italy.
It rises at Monviso in the Western Alps near the border with France.
It flows from west to east through the fertile Po Valley.
The Po flows into the Adriatic south of Venice with a delta.
The Swiss river Ticino joins the Po at Pavia.
The Po Valley is the most important agricultural region in Italy.

abschnitte.text: The Po rises at about 2,000 metres at the foot of **Monviso**, a distinctive mountain in Piedmont. After that it flows through Turin and on to the east. On the way it passes cities such as Piacenza and Cremona. Between Venice and Ravenna it flows into the Adriatic with the **Po Delta**.

Many tributaries of the Po come from the Alps. The **Ticino** flows from the canton of Ticino through Lake Maggiore and joins the Po at Pavia. The Adda also brings water from the Grisons, for example from the Val Poschiavo. So part of the rain from southern Switzerland ends up in the Adriatic in the end.

The **Po Valley** is a huge, flat plain between the Alps and the Apennines. Maize, wheat, fruit and above all a lot of rice for risotto grow here. Famous cheeses and hams such as Parmigiano Reggiano and Parma ham also come from this area. Milan, Turin and Bologna make the region one of the most important economic areas in Europe.

Because meltwater and rain come from the mountains, the Po can swell strongly. In the great flood of 1951, the Polesine area was flooded over a wide area. That is why its banks are protected with high **dykes**. In hot summers such as 2022, by contrast, the Po carried so little water that old shipwrecks appeared.

The delta grows a little further out into the sea every year, because the river brings a lot of sand and mud. It consists of lagoons, reeds, sandbanks and many river arms. Herons, flamingos and many other birds live here. Part of the area is protected as a **nature park** and biosphere reserve.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large, flat land without mountains.
A river that flows into a larger river.
An earth bank that protects the land from floods.
A shallow body of water by the sea that is cut off by sandbanks.

gewusst: At its mouth the Po carries more water than any other river in Italy.
The Po Delta lies partly below sea level and is kept dry by pumps.
The Romans called the Po “Padus”, which is where the name Pianura Padana for the Po Valley comes from.

teile.einleitung: The Rütli is a meadow on the shore of Lake Uri, a part of Lake Lucerne. According to legend, men from the original cantons swore an alliance here, which is why it is regarded as the birthplace of the Confederation.
wichtigste: The Rütli lies in the canton of Uri above Lake Uri.
According to legend, men from Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden swore an alliance here.
This oath is called the Rütli Oath.
On 1 August there is a ceremony on the Rütli every year.
The best way to reach the Rütli is by boat.
In 1940 General Henri Guisan called his officers together here.

abschnitte.text: According to **legend**, men from **Uri**, **Schwyz** and **Unterwalden** met on the Rütli. They swore to help one another against foreign lords. This oath is called the **Rütli Oath**. The story also became known through the play **“William Tell”** by Friedrich Schiller. Whether the meeting really took place like this is not known exactly, and it is a tradition.

The Rütli is a meadow on a steep slope above the lake. The easiest way to get there is by **boat**, for example from **Brunnen**. You can also walk down from **Seelisberg**. There is no road for cars, which is why it is quiet there.

Every year on **1 August** there is a large ceremony on the Rütli. 1 August is the **Swiss National Day**. On this day people remember the founding of the Confederation. Since the 19th century the Rütli has belonged to the Confederation and is looked after by the Swiss Public Utility Society.

During the **Second World War**, Switzerland was surrounded by warring parties. On **25 July 1940**, General **Henri Guisan** called his senior officers together on the Rütli. He explained to them how Switzerland was to be defended. The place was chosen deliberately, because the Rütli stands for the unity of the country. This meeting is called the **Rütli Report**.

gewusst: Many schoolchildren also collected money for the purchase of the Rütli in the 19th century.
No road leads to the Rütli, and you can only get there by boat or on foot.

teile.einleitung: The Reuss is one of the great rivers of Switzerland and flows from the Gotthard to the Aare in the canton of Aargau. On the way it plunges through the wild Schöllenen Gorge and flows in Lucerne under the famous Chapel Bridge. On its banks, important events in Swiss history took place.
wichtigste: The Reuss is about 160 kilometres long and flows entirely within Switzerland.
It rises in the Gotthard area, where the Rhine, Rhône and Ticino also rise.
At Andermatt it flows through the Schöllenen Gorge with the Devil's Bridge.
It flows through Lake Lucerne and leaves it in Lucerne.
In Lucerne it flows under the wooden Chapel Bridge.
At Windisch, the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet.

abschnitte.text: The Reuss is formed from headwater streams in the **Gotthard area** and flows through the Urseren valley at Andermatt. After that it rushes through the Schöllenen Gorge down into the Uri Reuss valley. At Flüelen it flows into **Lake Lucerne**. In Lucerne it leaves the lake again and flows north through the Freiamt to the Aare.

The **Schöllenen Gorge** was for a long time a dangerous obstacle on the way over the Gotthard. According to legend, the devil built the first bridge and demanded in return the first soul to cross it. But the clever people of Uri sent a billy goat across. That is why it is still called the **Devil's Bridge** today, and a big devil is painted on the rock wall.

In Lucerne the **Chapel Bridge** and the Spreuer Bridge cross the river, both old covered wooden bridges. The Chapel Bridge dates from the 14th century and has painted picture panels in its gable. In 1993 a large part of it burned down and was rebuilt afterwards. A needle weir on the river regulates the water level of Lake Lucerne.

At **Vindonissa**, today's Windisch, lay the only Roman legionary camp on the territory of present-day Switzerland. Here the Aare, Reuss and Limmat meet. On 23 November 1847, the decisive engagement of the Sonderbund War took place at **Gisikon** on the Reuss. This engagement decided the war for Lucerne, and shortly afterwards the Swiss federal state came into being in 1848.

In Aargau there are protected floodplains and river loops along the Reuss. Beavers, kingfishers and many waterbirds live there. The Reuss is also used to generate electricity, for example with river power plants. It is popular with canoeists and swimmers in summer, but it can have a strong **current**.

begriffe.erklaerung: A deep, narrow valley with steep rock walls.
A large fortified camp of Roman soldiers.
A short civil war in Switzerland in 1847.
An installation made of many wooden rods with which the water level is regulated.
Natural landscape beside a river that is flooded when the water is high.

gewusst: The Chapel Bridge is regarded as one of the oldest covered wooden bridges in Europe.
In 1799, Russian troops under General Suvorov fought the French at the Devil's Bridge.
The area around Brugg and Windisch, where the Aare, Reuss and Limmat flow together, is called the Water Castle of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Inn is an Alpine river that rises in the Upper Engadine in the Grisons. It flows through Switzerland, Austria and Germany and joins the Danube at Passau. It even gave the Engadine its name.
wichtigste: The Inn rises at Lake Lunghin above Maloja in the Grisons.
It is about 520 kilometres long.
The Engadine is named after the Inn, which in Romansh is called En.
The Inn flows through Austria, for example through Innsbruck.
At Passau in Germany the Inn joins the Danube.
By way of the Danube its water reaches the Black Sea.
At the confluence the Inn often carries more water than the Danube itself.

abschnitte.text: The **Inn** rises at **Lake Lunghin** at about 2,500 metres above sea level, above the Maloja Pass. After that it flows through the Upper Engadine lakes: Lake Sils, Lake Silvaplana and Lake St Moritz. In **Romansh** the river is called En. The word **Engadin** means roughly “valley of the Inn”.

From St Moritz the Inn flows north-east through the Lower Engadine, past Zernez and Scuol. At Martina it leaves Switzerland and flows into **Austria**, into the Tyrol. There it crosses Landeck, **Innsbruck** and Kufstein. After that it flows through Bavaria, forms the border between Germany and Austria for a stretch and finally reaches Passau.

At **Passau** the Danube, Inn and Ilz come together, which is why Passau is also called the city of three rivers. There the Inn is often richer in water than the **Danube**. At the confluence you can clearly see how the greenish water of the Inn and the darker water of the Danube move side by side for a while. By way of the Danube, the water of the Inn reaches the **Black Sea**.

Almost all the great rivers of Switzerland flow into the North Sea or the Mediterranean. The Inn is the most important Swiss river that belongs to the Danube and so to the Black Sea. Switzerland therefore lies on a **watershed** between several seas. At the Lunghin Pass near the source of the Inn, the catchment areas of the Rhine, Po and Danube even meet.

In the Engadine and the Tyrol, the water of the Inn is used in **hydropower plants** to generate electricity. In the Lower Engadine the Inn flows through gorges where you can also go rafting. Near Zernez lies the Swiss National Park, whose waters flow into the Inn. In winter the frozen Upper Engadine lakes are known for cross-country skiing and horse races on the ice.

begriffe.erklaerung: The boundary between areas from which water flows into different rivers or seas.
The fourth national language of Switzerland, spoken mainly in the Grisons.
The place where a river flows into another river, a lake or the sea.
The whole area from which water reaches a particular river.

gewusst: The city of Innsbruck owes its name to a bridge over the Inn.
A raindrop that falls at the Lunghin Pass can, depending on the side, end up in the North Sea, the Mediterranean or the Black Sea.
On the frozen Lake St Moritz, horse races take place in winter.

teile.einleitung: In Switzerland people pay very different amounts of tax depending on where they live. Cantons and municipalities set their own tax rates and so compete for residents and firms. This competition is called tax competition.
wichtigste: In federalism, cantons and municipalities have their own tax sovereignty.
The Tax Harmonisation Act sets out principles, but not the tax rates.
Since 2008 the New Fiscal Equalisation has balanced out differences between the cantons.
Zug pays the most per head into the resource equalisation.
The direct federal tax is regulated in the same way throughout Switzerland.
In 2023 the people accepted a minimum tax of 15 per cent for large corporations.

abschnitte.text: In Swiss **federalism**, cantons and municipalities have their own **tax sovereignty**. They can decide for themselves how high their taxes are. That is why there are great differences between the cantons. Many cantons calculate a **simple tax** according to a fixed scale. Of this, the canton and municipality levy a percentage, the **tax multiplier**, which they can set every year.

The cantons are not completely free, however. The **Tax Harmonisation Act** (StHG) regulates, for example, which incomes are taxed and how the procedures run. The level of the tax rates remains a matter for the cantons. The **direct federal tax**, by contrast, is levied throughout Switzerland on the same scale. Differences arise only in the cantonal and municipal taxes.

Since 2008 there has been the **New Fiscal Equalisation**, **NFA** for short. Under it, resource rich cantons and the Confederation pay money to resource poor cantons. Thanks to many firms and wealthy residents, the canton of **Zug** has the highest resource potential per head. That is why it pays in the most per resident. The equalisation softens the effects of tax competition.

On 19 May 2019 the people accepted the **tax reform and AHV financing** (STAF). It abolished special rules for holding and domiciliary companies that were criticised internationally and brought additional money for the **AHV** (old age insurance). On 18 June 2023 the people agreed to the **OECD minimum tax**. Large corporations with turnover of over 750 million euros are to pay at least **15 per cent** profit tax.

A special feature is the **lump sum taxation** of rich foreigners who do not work. In this, it is not their income but their **cost of living** that is taxed. Some cantons such as Zurich have abolished it, others keep it. Supporters of tax competition say it keeps taxes low and forces the state to save. Critics find that it leads to inequality between the cantons.

gewusst: Two neighbouring municipalities can have very different tax multipliers.
In Switzerland you fill in the tax return every year for the Confederation, canton and municipality together.

teile.einleitung: Although Switzerland has hardly any raw materials of its own, it is one of the most important places for the worldwide trade in crude oil, metals and grain. The centres are above all Geneva and the canton of Zug.
wichtigste: Geneva is the most important centre for trading in crude oil and grain.
The commodities company Glencore has its headquarters in Baar in the canton of Zug.
Glencore emerged from the firm that Marc Rich founded in Zug in 1974.
In transit trading the goods never reach Switzerland.
Low corporate taxes drew many traders to the canton of Zug.
The Responsible Business Initiative failed in 2020 on the majority of the cantons.

abschnitte.text: Switzerland is a **landlocked country** with no access to the sea. Even so, huge quantities of raw materials are traded here. This is because commodity trading is mainly about **contracts**, financing and organising transport. Specialists, banks, legal certainty and taxes are therefore important. The goods themselves do not have to pass through the country for this.

In **transit trading**, also called **merchanting**, a Swiss firm buys raw materials abroad. It then sells them to customers in another country. The ship with oil or grain goes, for example, directly from South America to Asia. The goods never cross the Swiss border, but the trade is handled in Switzerland.

In **Geneva**, large traders such as **Vitol, Trafigura, Gunvor and Mercuria** have their seats or branches. There crude oil, grain and oilseeds in particular are traded. The canton of **Zug** lowered taxes for certain companies as early as the 1940s, which attracted many trading firms. In 1974 the trader **Marc Rich** founded a firm in Zug. In 1994 it was renamed **Glencore**, today one of the largest commodities groups in the world, with its seat in **Baar**.

Traders often have to pay for large cargoes before they have been resold. For this they need short term credit and guarantees, called **trade finance**. Specialised banks in Geneva offer it. The firms in the sector are joined together in the **Swiss Trading and Shipping Association (STSA)**, based in Geneva. It represents traders, trade finance banks and shipping companies.

There is a lot of debate in Switzerland about commodity trading. Supporters stress the **jobs** and **tax revenue**. Critics such as aid organisations call for more responsibility for the environment and **human rights** in the countries where raw materials are mined. The **Responsible Business Initiative** wanted to make firms liable for damage abroad. On 29 November 2020 it received about 50.7 per cent yes, but failed on the **majority of the cantons**, because most of the cantons rejected it.

gewusst: A large part of the worldwide trade in raw materials is organised by firms in Switzerland, although the goods never see the country.
The Responsible Business Initiative is one of the few proposals that reached the popular majority but not the majority of the cantons.

teile.einleitung: Lake Constance is one of the largest lakes in central Europe and lies between Switzerland, Germany and Austria. The Rhine flows through it, and it supplies millions of people with drinking water. A special feature is that exact national borders were never fixed on most of the lake.
wichtigste: Lake Constance borders three countries: Switzerland, Germany and Austria.
It is about 536 square kilometres in area and up to 251 metres deep.
It consists of the Upper Lake and the Lower Lake.
On the Upper Lake, the national borders were never fixed exactly.
The canton of Thurgau lies on the south shore of Lake Constance.
Lake Constance is known for the Blaufelchen.

abschnitte.text: Lake Constance lies on the northern edge of the Alps between the cantons of Thurgau and St Gallen, Baden-Württemberg, Bavaria and Vorarlberg. The **Rhine** flows in near Bregenz and out again at Stein am Rhein. The large part is called the **Upper Lake** (Obersee), the smaller western part the Lower Lake (Untersee). By the way, the largest lake entirely within Switzerland is Lake Neuchâtel.

On the shore lie towns such as Constance, Friedrichshafen, Lindau, Bregenz, Romanshorn, Arbon and Rorschach. On the **island of Mainau**, hundreds of thousands of flowers bloom in spring and summer. The monastery island of Reichenau is a UNESCO World Heritage site. In Friedrichshafen the first **Zeppelins** were built.

The best-known fish is the **Blaufelchen** (a kind of whitefish), which professional fishers often catch with floating nets in open water. Its relative, the Gangfisch, stays smaller. The perch is called Kretzer around Lake Constance. Today fishers catch fewer whitefish than before, because the lake has become poorer in nutrients and less plankton grows.

Lake Constance is an important resting and wintering area for waterbirds. In winter you can often watch large groups of resting **wild geese**. Great crested grebes can also be watched especially well here, as on Lake Neuchâtel. The Ermatingen Basin and the Rhine Delta are important nature reserves.

Drinking water for about four to five million people is obtained from Lake Constance, mainly in southern Germany. On the Upper Lake the three countries never agreed on exact **borders**. The lake there is treated in practice as a shared area. Many questions are settled jointly by the riparian states in treaties.

begriffe.erklaerung: Countries or municipalities that lie on a lake or river.
Tiny plants and animals that float in the water and serve fish as food.
A silvery fish of the salmon family that lives in many Swiss lakes.
The Swiss German word for when a large lake freezes over completely.

gewusst: In winter 1963 Lake Constance froze over completely for the last time, and people walked from shore to shore.
With ferries you can cross the lake between Romanshorn and Friedrichshafen in about 40 minutes.
When the foehn blows, from the German shore the Swiss Alps look close enough to touch.

teile.einleitung: The Thames is the most important river in England and flows right through the capital, London. Over it runs the famous Tower Bridge, whose roadway can open for ships. For many centuries the Thames was the most important trade route in Great Britain.
wichtigste: The Thames is about 350 kilometres long and the longest river entirely in England.
It rises in the Cotswolds in the west of England.
It flows through Oxford, Windsor and London.
It flows into the North Sea in a broad funnel-shaped estuary.
Tower Bridge in London can open so that large ships can pass through.
A large barrier protects London from storm surges.

abschnitte.text: The Thames rises at **Thames Head** in the green hills of the Cotswolds. It flows east through the university city of Oxford and past Windsor Castle. After that it crosses London in great loops. East of the city it widens into a broad **estuary** and reaches the North Sea.

**Tower Bridge** opened in 1894 and stands next to the Tower of London. Its two halves of the roadway can be lifted up like flaps, which is called a **bascule bridge**. This still happens several times a week today, when tall ships pass through. At the top, two walkways link the two towers, partly with a glass floor.

On the bank of the Thames stand the Houses of Parliament with the clock tower Big Ben and the big wheel London Eye. Further downstream lie the Tower of London and modern high-rises. In the past the docks of London were one of the largest ports in the world. Today the Thames carries mainly pleasure boats and fast river boats.

Up to the lock at Teddington in west London, you can feel the **ebb and flow of the tide** in the Thames. The water level in London can therefore change by several metres within a few hours. Against dangerous storm surges, the **Thames Barrier** was built in the 1980s. Its huge rotating gates can close off the river in times of danger.

In the 19th century the Thames was so polluted that in 1858 people spoke of the “Great Stink”. After that London got a modern sewer system. Today fish, seals and sometimes even dolphins live in the estuary again. Every year the universities of Oxford and Cambridge row their famous **Boat Race** on the Thames.

begriffe.erklaerung: A bridge whose roadway can be folded upwards.
A broad, funnel-shaped river mouth at the sea with ebb and flow of the tide.
The regular rising and falling of sea level, that is, ebb and flow.
Very high water when strong wind pushes the sea onto the coast.

gewusst: In very cold winters of earlier centuries, the Thames froze over in London, and fairs were held on the ice.
In Oxford the Thames is also called the Isis.
The Thames is the longest river entirely in England, but the longest river in Great Britain is the Severn.

teile.einleitung: The Würm glaciation was the last great ice age in the Alps. Back then, huge glaciers covered large parts of Switzerland. It ended about 12,000 years ago and has strongly shaped our landscape.
wichtigste: The Würm glaciation is the youngest of the classic Alpine cold periods.
The order is Günz, Mindel, Riss, Würm.
Penck and Brückner established this division.
In Switzerland the last ice age is also called the Birrfeld glaciation.
Before it came the Eemian warm period.
Sea level was then about 120 metres lower.
At the end came one last cold snap, the Younger Dryas.

abschnitte.text: The researchers **Albrecht Penck** and **Eduard Brückner** wrote the work “Die Alpen im Eiszeitalter” (“The Alps in the Ice Age”) from 1901 to 1909. They distinguished four **cold periods** and named them after rivers in the Alpine foreland: **Günz, Mindel, Riss and Würm**. The order follows the alphabet, from old to young. Further cold periods were added later. In Switzerland people today also speak of the **Birrfeld glaciation**, named after a place in the canton of Aargau.

abschnitte.titel: Before and during the cold period
abschnitte.text: Before the Würm glaciation came the **Eemian warm period**. It began about 126,000 years ago and lasted about 11,000 years. After that it got colder. But the Würm glaciation was not always equally cold. Cold phases with glacier advances are called **stadials**, warmer phases in between **interstadials**.

At the time of the greatest glaciation, mighty glaciers flowed out of the Alps onto the **Central Plateau**. Only high peaks stuck out of the ice. They are called **nunataks**, a word from Greenlandic. They offered plants a refuge. In the older **Riss glaciation** the glaciers reached even further, in Switzerland as far as the **Jura**. That is why the moraines of the Würm lie inside the older deposits.

During the cold period, **mammoths** and other animals of the cold steppe lived in the foreland. In a bog near **Niederweningen** in the canton of Zurich, **mammoth bones** were found in 1890 and 2003. A small **mammoth museum** shows the finds today. Because huge ice sheets locked up a lot of water, **sea level** was about **120 metres** lower than today. The North Sea and the Bering Strait fell dry.

abschnitte.titel: The end of the ice age
abschnitte.text: After a warming in the **Allerød**, it became clearly colder again for a good 1,000 years. This phase is called the **Younger Dryas** and is named after the mountain avens, a small plant. About 12,000 years ago the cold period then ended. The glaciers left behind **moraines**, erratic boulders and many of the **lakes** that we see on the Central Plateau today.

gewusst: The mountain avens is called Dryas in scientific terms, which is where the name Younger Dryas comes from.
Because sea level was so low, you could walk from Asia to America with dry feet at that time.

teile.einleitung: The zero degree line is an important quantity in the weather report. It shows at what height the air is exactly 0 degrees. For glaciers, snow and walks in the mountains it is very important.
wichtigste: The zero degree line is the height at which the air is 0 °C, and above it it is colder.
It is measured with radiosondes on weather balloons.
In August 2023 it stood at about 5,300 metres, higher than ever measured before.
Since about 1970 it has risen markedly because of global warming.
The snowfall line is usually a few hundred metres lower.
When it lies above the peaks, the glaciers melt over their whole area.

abschnitte.titel: What the zero degree line is
abschnitte.text: In the air it mostly gets colder upwards. Somewhere the air is exactly **0 °C**. This height is called the **zero degree line**. Above it the temperature is below zero, and below it above. In the weather report you hear, for example: “The zero degree line is at 3,000 metres.”

Measurements are made with **radiosondes**. These are small measuring instruments on a **weather balloon**. On the way up they continuously measure temperature, humidity and air pressure. In Switzerland, MeteoSwiss sends up such balloons in **Payerne**. The measurement series go back to **1954**.

Often the temperature falls by about **0.65 °C per 100 metres**. If a station at 500 metres measures 13 °C, you work out 13 divided by 0.65, which is 20. That is 20 times 100 metres, so 2,000 metres above the station. The zero degree line is then at about **2,500 metres**. If the air becomes 1 °C warmer everywhere, the line rises by about **150 metres**.

The **snowfall line** is usually **a few hundred metres lower** than the zero degree line. Snowflakes need a certain distance before they have melted in the warmer air. That is why it still snows below the zero degree line. For ski areas and roads this line is very important.

On **20 July 1995** the zero degree line was above 5,000 metres for the first time. In the night of **21 August 2023**, **5,298 metres** were measured, a new record. Since about 1970 the zero degree line has risen markedly because of **global warming**. When it lies above the peaks in summer, ice and snow melt over the whole **glacier area**. Precipitation then also falls as rain instead of snow.

gewusst: At the record value of 5,298 metres, the air was warmer than 0 °C even above the summit of the Dufourspitze.
In winter, in an inversion, the zero degree line can lie higher in the mountains than in the valley, where it is bitterly cold.

teile.einleitung: The Saane is a river in western Switzerland that flows from the Valais into the canton of Bern. In French it is called the Sarine, and it is regarded as an image of the language border between German and French.
wichtigste: The Saane is called the Sarine in French.
It rises at the Sanetschhorn in the canton of the Valais.
It flows through the Valais, Bern, Vaud and Fribourg.
The city of Fribourg lies in a loop of the Saane.
In the Gruyère region it is dammed into Lake Gruyère.
It is about 126 kilometres long and flows into the Aare in the canton of Bern.

abschnitte.titel: From the mountains into the valley
abschnitte.text: The Saane rises at the **Sanetschhorn** in the canton of the **Valais**. Then it flows north into the **Bernese Oberland**. There it flows through **Saanen** near Gstaad. The village got its name from the river. After that it flows through the canton of Vaud into the canton of Fribourg.

In the **Gruyère region**, the Saane is dammed at Rossens into a large reservoir, **Lake Gruyère**. In French it is called Lac de la Gruyère. The area is also known for Gruyère cheese. The water of the lake is used to produce **electricity**.

The bilingual cantonal capital **Fribourg**, in German Freiburg, lies on the Saane. Its old town lies in a **loop** of the river, with steep rocks and many bridges. In the city people speak **German and French**. After that the Saane flows on north and joins the **Aare** in the canton of **Bern**.

abschnitte.titel: A river on the language border
abschnitte.text: In the canton of Fribourg, the Saane separates **German speaking** and **French speaking** areas in some places. The language border does not follow the river exactly everywhere, however. Even so, the Saane is regarded as an image of the **Röstigraben**, the imaginary border between German speaking Switzerland and western Switzerland.

The Saane is about **126 kilometres** long. It is one of the most important **tributaries of the Aare**. On its way it flows through four cantons: Valais, Bern, Vaud and Fribourg. It does not flow through the Grisons, because that canton lies far in the east of Switzerland.

gewusst: The village of Saanen near Gstaad and the whole Saane district in the canton of Fribourg are named after the river.
The Saane flows through areas with German and with French language.

teile.einleitung: The Ticino is the most important river in the canton of Ticino. It rises near the Nufenen Pass, flows south through several valleys and joins Lake Maggiore.
wichtigste: The Ticino rises near the Nufenen Pass.
First it flows through the Bedretto valley, and after Airolo through the Leventina.
It flows south and joins Lake Maggiore.
Bellinzona with its three castles lies on the Ticino.
At Biasca the Brenno joins from the Blenio valley, later the Moesa from the Misox.
Along the river people speak Italian.
The Ticino is about 250 kilometres long.

abschnitte.text: The **Ticino** rises near the **Nufenen Pass**, on the border with the Valais. Right after its source it flows through the **Bedretto valley**. At **Airolo** at the foot of the Gotthard the valley becomes wider. From there it flows through the **Leventina**, ever further **south**.

On its way the Ticino takes in many streams and rivers. At **Biasca** the **Brenno** joins from the **Blenio valley**. A little further south the **Moesa** joins. It flows from the **Misox**, a valley that belongs to the canton of the **Grisons**. There, too, people speak Italian.

On the Ticino lies **Bellinzona**, the capital of the canton of Ticino. The town is famous for its **three castles**: Castelgrande, Montebello and Sasso Corbaro. In the past they guarded the way through the narrow valley to the Alpine passes. Today they belong to the **UNESCO World Heritage**.

After Bellinzona the Ticino flows through the flat **Magadino plain**. Then it joins **Lake Maggiore**. The lake lies mostly in Italy. At the south end the Ticino leaves the lake again and flows on through Italy. In total it is about **250 kilometres** long.

gewusst: The canton of Ticino bears the name of the river, because “Ticino” is the Italian name for both.
Along the Ticino people speak Italian, one of the four national languages of Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The Spatial Planning Act, RPG for short, regulates in Switzerland where building is allowed and where it is not. It is meant to ensure that scarce land is used carefully and landscapes are preserved.
wichtigste: The RPG was passed on 22 June 1979 and has applied since 1 January 1980.
A first draft failed in a referendum vote in 1976.
The basic principle is the economical use of land.
Building zones and non-building zones are to be clearly separated.
The Confederation lays down principles, and the cantons and municipalities do the planning.
The revision of 2013 was accepted with almost 63 per cent yes, and only the Valais rejected it.

abschnitte.text: In the 1960s and 1970s, a great deal was built in Switzerland, often without clear rules. A first Spatial Planning Act failed in 1976 in a **referendum vote**. A new draft was passed on 22 June 1979 and came into force on 1 January 1980. Its basis today is **Article 75 of the Federal Constitution**.

The most important aim is stated right in the first article: land is to be used **economically**. That means it should be treated sparingly, because it cannot be increased. In addition, **building zones** and **non-building zones** are to be kept separate. In this way forests, meadows and fields are not to be built over bit by bit.

The Confederation lays down only the **principles**. The actual planning is a matter for the **cantons** and their **municipalities**. Each canton draws up a **structure plan**, which is binding on the authorities and must be approved by the Federal Council. For landowners, only the municipality's **land use plan** applies, which sets out the building zones, for example. For its own tasks such as transport, the military or crop rotation areas, the Confederation draws up **sectoral plans**.

On 3 March 2013 the people accepted a revision of the RPG with almost **63 per cent** yes. The aim was above all to shrink building zones that were too large and to develop settlements inwards. The only canton to vote no was the **Valais**, where there were especially large reserves of building zones. A **value added levy** was also newly required: anyone who profits from land being rezoned as building land must hand over part of the gain.

The responsible federal authority is the **Federal Office for Spatial Development (ARE)**. Among other things, it examines the cantonal structure plans. Cantons that did not adapt their structure plan or the value added levy in time received a **rezoning freeze**. They were then not allowed to create any new building zones until the requirements were met.

gewusst: For crop rotation areas, that is, especially good farmland, the Confederation lays down how much of it each canton must keep.
A structure plan binds only the authorities, and only the land use plan also applies to the owners of plots of land.

teile.einleitung: Lake Lucerne lies in central Switzerland and, with its many arms, is one of the best-known lakes in the country. The history of the Swiss Confederation began on its shores.
wichtigste: The German name comes from four old cantons on its shore.
Today five cantons border the lake.
It is about 114 square kilometres in area and around 200 metres deep.
The part in the canton of Uri is called Lake Uri.
In the west the lake ends at Lucerne.
The Schillerstein commemorates the author of “William Tell”.
The new islands in Lake Uri are made of rock from tunnel building.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Lucerne** has its German name, **Vierwaldstättersee** (“Lake of the Four Forest Cantons”), from **four old cantons** on its shore: **Uri**, **Schwyz**, **Unterwalden** and **Lucerne**. The first three used to be called the Forest Cantons. Because Unterwalden is now divided into Obwalden and Nidwalden, **five cantons** border the lake. In the west it ends at the city of **Lucerne**.

Seen from above, the lake does not look round. It has **many arms** that wind between the mountains. The part in the canton of Uri is called **Lake Uri**. In total the lake is about **114 square kilometres** in area. At its deepest point it measures **around 200 metres**.

Several rivers bring water into the lake. The **Reuss** flows in at Flüelen and out again at Lucerne. The **Muota** from the Muota valley flows in at **Brunnen**. In Lake Uri, new **islands** have been built. They are made of **rock from tunnel building** that was excavated when the Gotthard Base Tunnel was built. There, birds and plants find new habitats.

A rock rises out of the water in the lake, the **Schillerstein**. It commemorates **Friedrich Schiller**, the author of the play **“William Tell”**. There is an inscription in his honour on the rock. Very close by lies the **Rütli meadow**, where, according to legend, the pact of the Confederates was sworn.

gewusst: Several historic paddle steamers still sail on Lake Lucerne.
After Lake Neuchâtel, Lake Lucerne is the largest lake that lies entirely in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: Lake Thun lies in the canton of Bern at the edge of the Bernese Oberland. It is surrounded by mountains, castles and villages and is flowed through by the Aare.
wichtigste: Lake Thun lies in the canton of Bern.
At its deepest point it is about 217 metres deep.
At the northwest end lies the town of Thun with its castle.
Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz.
The Kander was diverted into the lake over 300 years ago.
Above Spiez rises the pyramid shaped Niesen.
The “Blümlisalp” is a paddle steamer on the lake.

abschnitte.text: **Lake Thun** lies entirely in the canton of **Bern**. At its deepest point it measures about **217 metres**. The **Aare** flows into the lake from **Interlaken** and out again at **Thun**. Interlaken lies between Lake Thun and **Lake Brienz**, hence its name, which means “between the lakes”.

In the past the **Kander** did not flow into the lake but into the Aare below Thun. There it often caused floods. So over 300 years ago, in 1714, it was led through a tunnel into **Lake Thun**. Since then it has brought a lot of gravel into the lake and has built up a large **delta** at its mouth.

On Lake Thun stand several castles. **Thun Castle** towers over the town at the northwest end. **Oberhofen Castle** has a little turret that stands directly in the **water**. In **Hilterfingen** lies **Hünegg Castle**, a museum of domestic culture. **Spiez** also has a castle right on the lake.

Above Spiez rises the **Niesen**. It has the shape of an almost perfect **pyramid** and can be reached by funicular. On the north shore you can visit the **St Beatus Caves**. According to a legend, the holy Beatus once lived there. The caves are furnished with stalactites and underground streams.

On Lake Thun, scheduled boats run between the villages. Especially well known is the **“Blümlisalp”**, a **paddle steamer**. Its big paddle wheels at the side drive the ship, powered by a steam engine. It is named after the mountain massif of the Blümlisalp in the Bernese Oberland.

gewusst: The diversion of the Kander is regarded as one of the early large hydraulic engineering projects in Switzerland.
The name Interlaken comes from Latin and means “between the lakes”.

teile.einleitung: The Volga is the longest river in Europe and flows through the west of Russia. It is about 3,500 kilometres long and flows into the Caspian Sea. For the people of Russia it is so important that it is lovingly called “Mother Volga”.
wichtigste: The Volga is the longest river in Europe.
It is about 3,530 kilometres long and flows entirely within Russia.
It rises in the Valdai Hills north-west of Moscow.
The Volga flows into the Caspian Sea.
On it lie big cities such as Nizhny Novgorod, Kazan, Samara and Volgograd.
Many dams have turned the Volga into a chain of huge reservoirs.

abschnitte.text: The Volga rises as a small stream in the **Valdai Hills** between Moscow and Saint Petersburg. It flows first east, then south at Kazan. Its largest tributaries are the **Oka** and the Kama. At Astrakhan it forms a huge delta and flows into the Caspian Sea.

On the Volga lie many old Russian cities such as Tver, Yaroslavl and Nizhny Novgorod. Kazan is the capital of the Republic of Tatarstan with a famous kremlin. Further south lie Samara, Saratov and **Volgograd**, which used to be called Stalingrad. There, one of the greatest battles in history took place in the Second World War.

The Volga is one of the most important waterways in Russia. Through canals it is linked with Moscow, the Baltic Sea and the White Sea. The **Volga-Don Canal** leads to the Don and so to the Black Sea. In winter the river freezes over in many sections for several months.

In the 20th century many large **dams** were built on the Volga. The Kuybyshev Reservoir near Samara is among the largest reservoirs in Europe. The power plants supply a lot of electricity, but old villages and churches sank beneath the waters. The dams also block the way of fish to their spawning grounds.

In the **Volga Delta** there are hundreds of river arms, reed islands and fields of water lilies. Pelicans, herons and many other birds live here. In the past, huge **sturgeon** such as the beluga swam up the Volga from the Caspian Sea. Caviar is made from their eggs, and through overfishing they are seriously endangered today.

begriffe.erklaerung: A mouth area in which a river divides into many arms.
An artificially built waterway for ships.
A large, ancient-looking fish whose eggs are used to make caviar.
A fortified castle complex in the centre of an old Russian city.

gewusst: The Volga is almost three times as long as the Rhine.
The source of the Volga lies only a good 200 metres above sea level, which is why it flows very slowly.
Because the Caspian Sea lies below sea level, the Volga ends lower than it would if it ended in the ocean.

tnqhza1.t: WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF

teile.einleitung: The WSL Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research SLF in Davos studies snow, ice and avalanches. It is best known for the avalanche bulletin, which warns of avalanche danger in winter.
wichtigste: In 1936 a snow laboratory was opened on the Weissfluhjoch above Davos.
In 1942 the Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research was founded in Davos.
Since 1989 the SLF has been part of the WSL research institute.
Since 1996 its headquarters have been in Davos Dorf.
In winter the avalanche bulletin appears twice a day.
The SLF runs about 180 automatic stations of the IMIS network.
Most fatal avalanche accidents happen at level 3, “considerable”.

abschnitte.text: In **1936**, a **snow laboratory** with a test field was opened on the **Weissfluhjoch** above Davos. Avalanche research began there. In **1942**, the Federal Institute for Snow and Avalanche Research was founded in Davos. Since **1989** it has belonged to the Federal Research Institute **WSL**. Since **1996** its headquarters have been in **Davos Dorf**.

In winter the SLF publishes the **avalanche bulletin** **twice a day**. It shows on a map how great the avalanche danger is in the different regions. There are **five danger levels**, from “low” to “very high”. Most fatal avalanche accidents happen at **level 3, “considerable”**. Many people underestimate this middle level.

For the forecast to be right, measurements are needed. The SLF runs **about 180** automatic snow and wind stations of the **IMIS network**. They measure, for example, snow depth, temperature and wind. There are also observers who measure by hand and examine the snow.

A snowpack is made up of many layers. Some hold together poorly. A typical **weak layer** is **surface hoar** that has been buried by snow. These are fine ice crystals that form on the snow on clear nights. If this layer is covered by new snow, a **slab avalanche** can slide off above it.

In the Valais valley **Vallée de la Sionne**, the SLF runs a special **test site**. There **avalanches are set off artificially** and studied with measuring instruments. This is how people learn how fast avalanches are and what forces they have. It helps in planning protective structures and hazard maps better.

gewusst: The SLF researches not only avalanches but also permafrost, glaciers and natural hazards such as debris flows.
You can also read the Swiss avalanche bulletin with an app on your phone.

teile.einleitung: Zurich main station is the largest railway station in Switzerland. Every working day a great many people arrive or depart here. Its history begins with the first railway line in Switzerland in 1847.
wichtigste: In 1847 the first railway line in Switzerland ran from Zurich to Baden.
It was called the Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn.
The station building by Jakob Friedrich Wanner was finished in 1871.
On a working day about 400,000 passengers use the station (as of 2023).
The station has 26 platform tracks for passenger trains.
Löwenstrasse station opened in 2014.
In front of the station stands the monument to Alfred Escher.

abschnitte.text: In **1847**, the first railway line lying entirely in Switzerland opened. It ran from **Zurich** to **Baden** in Aargau. It was called the **Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn** (“Spanish bun railway”). The name comes from a fine pastry from Baden. With the railway, it could be brought fresh to Zurich.

The architect **Jakob Friedrich Wanner** built the magnificent station building. It was finished in **1871**. In the big **hall** a colourful **guardian angel** now hovers. It was made by the artist **Niki de Saint Phalle**. Right next to the station stands the **Swiss National Museum**, which looks like a castle and shows the history of Switzerland.

The main station has **26 tracks** for passenger trains. 16 of them lie above ground, 10 more below it. The underground **Löwenstrasse station** opened in **2014**. Trains run through it right under the city. On a working day, about **400,000** passengers use the station (as of 2023). That is almost as many as live in the city of Zurich.

Beneath the station and the station square lies the shopping world **Shopville** with many shops. On the **station square** stands the monument to **Alfred Escher**, put up in **1889**. Escher was an important politician and businessman. He founded the **Northeastern Railway** and helped with the building of the Gotthard Tunnel.

gewusst: The name Spanisch-Brötli-Bahn comes from a pastry from Baden.
Zurich main station is one of the most heavily used stations in the world.

teile.einleitung: The Yangtze, Jangtsekiang in German, is the longest river in Asia and one of the longest in the world. It flows right across China from the Tibetan Plateau to the sea at Shanghai. On it stands the Three Gorges Dam, one of the largest structures people have ever built.
wichtigste: The Yangtze is the longest river in Asia.
It is about 6,300 kilometres long, which makes it the third-longest river on Earth after the Nile and the Amazon.
It rises on the Tibetan Plateau and flows into the East China Sea near Shanghai.
In Chinese it is called Chang Jiang, which means long river.
The Three Gorges Dam on the Yangtze is the most powerful hydropower plant in the world.
Big cities such as Chongqing, Wuhan and Nanjing lie on its banks.
About a third of China's people live in the Yangtze region.

abschnitte.text: The **Yangtze** rises on the **Tibetan Plateau** in the Chinese province of Qinghai, at over 5,000 metres above sea level. First it flows south through deep valleys in the mountains. After that it turns east and crosses the whole of China. After about 6,300 kilometres it flows into the East China Sea at **Shanghai**.

On the Yangtze lie some of the largest cities in China. **Chongqing** is a huge city in the west, built on hills above the river. Further downstream lie Wuhan and Nanjing, which was once the capital of China. At the mouth lies Shanghai with one of the largest ports in the world.

In the **Three Gorges**, the Yangtze flows between steep rock walls. There the **Three Gorges Dam** was built, which is about 2.3 kilometres long and was finished around 2006. Its power plant produces more electricity than any other hydropower plant in the world. For the reservoir, over a million people had to leave their homes and move.

The Yangtze roughly divides China into a north and a south. In its fertile valley, **rice** has been grown for thousands of years. Ships transport coal, building materials and goods far inland on the river. At the same time, in times of **high water** the river has often caused great floods, for example in 1998.

In the Yangtze lived the **Chinese river dolphin**, also called the baiji. Since a large search in 2006, it is regarded as probably extinct. The finless porpoise and the rare **Chinese alligator** still live there today. To protect the animals, China introduced a ten-year fishing ban on the Yangtze in 2021.

begriffe.erklaerung: A large wall that holds back a river so that a lake forms.
An installation that produces electricity with the force of flowing water.
A deep, narrow valley with steep rock walls.
The place where a river flows into the sea or into another river.

gewusst: The reservoir of the Three Gorges Dam is over 600 kilometres long, longer than the whole of Switzerland from west to east.
The name Jangtsekiang actually comes from only a short stretch near the sea; the Chinese call the whole river Chang Jiang.
The Chinese river dolphin was probably the first species of whale to be wiped out by humans.

teile.einleitung: The Emme is a river in the canton of Bern and the canton of Solothurn. It gives the Emmental its name, which is known for its cheese with the big holes. The Emme is known for being able to swell very quickly in heavy rain.
wichtigste: The Emme is about 80 kilometres long.
It rises in the Pre-Alps near the Hohgant.
The Emmental is named after the Emme.
The famous Emmental cheese bears the name of the Emmental.
In thunderstorms the Emme can bring dangerous floods.
The Emme joins the Aare near Solothurn.

abschnitte.text: The **Emme** rises in the Pre-Alps near the Hohgant in the Bernese Oberland. It flows through Schangnau, Eggiwil and Signau into the hilly Emmental. At Emmenmatt it takes in the Ilfis and then flows north past Burgdorf. East of Solothurn it joins the **Aare**.

The **Emmental** is a landscape with many green hills, farms and forests. Typical are the big farmhouses with roofs that reach right down low. The famous **Emmental** cheese bears the name of the valley. It is made from cow's milk and matured in big wheels.

The Emme can rise very quickly in thunderstorms and prolonged rain. In the past, such **floods** did great damage to houses, bridges and fields. The writer **Jeremias Gotthelf**, who lived in Lützelflüh in the Emmental, described the flood of 1837 in a story. Today, dams and river works protect the villages better.

Several old **covered wooden bridges** cross the Emme. The roof protects the wood from rain, so that the bridge lasts a long time. Especially well known is the wooden bridge between Hasle and Rüegsau from 1839. It is regarded as one of the largest wooden arch bridges in Europe.

The Emme carries a lot of gravel and rubble with it. Special plants grow on the gravel banks, and birds such as the little ringed plover breed there. Brown trout and graylings live in the water. In summer the Emme can almost dry up in some places, because the water seeps away into the gravel.

begriffe.erklaerung: A river carries much more water than normal and bursts its banks.
A big round piece of cheese or bread.
A bridge with a roof that protects the wood from the weather.
Rounded stones that a river carries along.

gewusst: The holes in Emmental come from gas that bacteria produce during ripening.
In the canton of Lucerne there is a second river with a similar name, the Kleine Emme.
Jeremias Gotthelf wrote the story “Die Wassernot im Emmental” (“The Flood in the Emmental”) about the Emme flood of 1837.

teile.einleitung: The San Bernardino route is an important north south link through the Alps. As the A13 motorway it runs from Chur through the Grisons into Ticino.
wichtigste: The San Bernardino Road Tunnel is about 6.6 kilometres long.
It was opened on 1 December 1967.
Between Thusis and Zillis lies the Viamala Gorge.
The route is the most important alternative to the Gotthard.
The watershed between the Rhine and the Po runs over the pass.
In June 2024 a storm destroyed a section of the A13 in the Misox.

abschnitte.text: The route leads from Chur up the valley of the **Hinterrhein**. Between Thusis and Zillis lies the **Viamala**, a narrow, deep gorge. For a long time it was a dangerous obstacle for travellers. Then, over the pass or through the tunnel, you go into the **Misox** and on towards Bellinzona. Today most of it is built as the **A13 motorway**.

In the past only a **mule track** led over the mountain, on which pack animals carried goods. Between **1818 and 1823** a road fit for vehicles was built over the pass. The pass and the village are named after the travelling preacher **Bernardino of Siena**, to whom a chapel is dedicated there. The pass road is closed in winter.

On **1 December 1967** the **San Bernardino Road Tunnel** was opened. It is about 6.6 kilometres long. The **north portal** is by the village of Hinterrhein at a good 1,600 m above sea level, and the **south portal** by the village of San Bernardino. With the tunnel the route became **safe in winter**, in contrast to the pass road.

A **watershed** runs over the pass. To the north the Hinterrhein flows via the Rhine into the **North Sea**. To the south the **Moesa** flows via the Ticino into the **Po** and into the Adriatic Sea. A **language border** also runs here: in the Rheinwald in the north people speak German, in the Misox in the south Italian. Both valleys belong to the Grisons.

When there is a traffic jam or a closure on the **Gotthard**, many vehicles divert to the A13. Both routes lead into Ticino. In **June 2024**, in a severe **storm**, the Moesa tore away a piece of the A13 near Lostallo. The route was then closed for some time, and traffic had to use other roads.

gewusst: A raindrop on the top of the pass can end up in the North Sea or in the Mediterranean, depending on the side.
Before the tunnel was built, the route over the San Bernardino was often interrupted for months in winter.

teile.einleitung: Olten is a town on the Aare in the canton of Solothurn. It is known above all as a railway hub: important railway lines in Switzerland cross here.
wichtigste: Olten is the largest town in the canton of Solothurn.
In 2022, slightly more than 19,000 people lived there.
At Olten station the lines from Basel to Lucerne and from Bern to Zurich cross.
A stone near the station marks kilometre zero of the railway.
The old wooden bridge over the Aare dates from 1803.
The coat of arms shows three fir trees.

abschnitte.text: Olten lies on the **Aare** in the canton of **Solothurn**, close to the border with Aargau. It is the largest town in the canton. In 2022, slightly more than **19,000** people lived there. Just north of the town, the hills of the **Jura** rise. The old town lies on the left bank of the Aare.

In Olten the railway lines **from Basel to Lucerne** and **from Bern to Zurich** meet. That is why very many travellers change trains here every day. The trains arrive **on the hour and on the half hour**, so that you can change quickly. Olten lies almost in the middle between Basel, Bern, Zurich and Lucerne. You can reach all four cities in about an hour or less.

In the past, the kilometres on the Swiss railway network were measured from Olten. A special **stone** near the station shows this **zero point**. Olten became a centre of the railway as early as the 19th century. At that time a large **workshop** for locomotives and carriages was also built here.

Over the Aare runs an old **covered bridge** made of **wood**. It was built in **1803** by a carpenter. Today only pedestrians may cross it. It connects the old town with the station district and is a landmark of the town.

The **coat of arms of Olten** shows **three green fir trees** on green hills. The background is white. In Switzerland you find coats of arms for all cantons and municipalities. They can often be seen on buildings, flags and fountains.

gewusst: From Olten, the railway's Hauenstein Base Tunnel leads through the Jura towards Basel.
Because you can get everywhere so quickly from Olten, meetings of clubs and associations from all over Switzerland are often held here.

teile.einleitung: The Tectonic Arena Sardona is a mountain area in the eastern Swiss Alps. There you can see how, when the Alps were formed, very old rock was pushed over younger rock. Since 2008 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
wichtigste: The Tectonic Arena Sardona has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2008.
It lies in the cantons of Glarus, St Gallen and the Grisons.
It is famous because older rock lies on top of younger rock.
The visible boundary is called the Glarus Main Thrust.
On top lies the reddish Verrucano, beneath it the younger Flysch.
Albert Heim studied the thrust and from 1902 supported the nappe theory.
The name comes from the Piz Sardona.

abschnitte.titel: A World Heritage Site in the Alps
abschnitte.text: The **Tectonic Arena Sardona** lies in the cantons of **Glarus**, **St Gallen** and the **Grisons**. It is named after the **Piz Sardona**. In **2008** UNESCO inscribed the area as a **World Heritage Site**. It was honoured because here you can understand especially well how mountains are formed. The word **tectonics** describes the movements in the Earth's crust.

Normally rocks are laid down like pages in a pile: the old ones at the bottom, the young ones on top. In the Tectonic Arena it is the other way round. Here **older rock lies on younger rock**. This happened because, when the Alps were formed, huge masses of rock were pushed many kilometres over other layers.

The upper, reddish rock is called **Verrucano**. It is very old, many hundreds of millions of years. Beneath it lies the much younger **Flysch**, a mostly grey, slaty stone. The sharp boundary between the two is called the **Glarus Main Thrust**. On many mountain flanks it can be seen as a clearly visible line running almost horizontally through the rocks.

The Swiss geologist **Albert Heim** studied the Glarus thrust very closely. For a long time people looked for an explanation. From **1902** Heim supported the **nappe theory**. In geology a **nappe** is a large rock slab that was pushed over other rocks. This idea still helps today to explain the structure of the Alps.

gewusst: Through the Martinsloch, a hole in the rock in the Tschingelhörner, the sun shines directly onto the church of Elm on a few days of the year.
The Tectonic Arena Sardona is a UNESCO World Heritage Site that is protected not for buildings but for rocks.

teile.einleitung: Switzerland lies in the middle of Europe and has five neighbouring countries. It is closely connected with all of them by roads, railways, rivers and lakes.
wichtigste: The five neighbouring countries are Germany, France, Italy, Austria and Liechtenstein.
In the east lie Austria and little Liechtenstein.
Liechtenstein is the smallest neighbouring country and has the shortest border with Switzerland.
Germany has the most inhabitants of all the neighbouring countries.
At Lake Constance, Switzerland, Germany and Austria meet.
Liechtenstein, like Switzerland, is not a member of the EU.

abschnitte.text: In the north Switzerland borders **Germany**, in the west **France**, and in the south **Italy**. In the east lie **Austria** and **Liechtenstein**. Many borders follow rivers, lakes or mountain ridges. The Rhine, for example, forms a large part of the border with Germany.

**Lake Constance** lies in the north east of Switzerland. Its shores belong to Switzerland, Germany and Austria. In **Basel**, at the bend of the Rhine, Switzerland, Germany and France meet.
